entries.name: Return the Favor (3/Day)
entries.description: When Oak takes damage from a melee weapon attack, he can make a hooked dagger attack.

info.text:
Oak Truestrike is the "B" Team's decisionist-and, depending on who you talk to, a reincarnated demigod. (It's a long story.) Those who know him acknowledge his confidence, his arrogance, and his odd ability to engage with others by somehow saying exactly what each listener wants to hear. Whether this is some subtle magical ability or simply grifter's charm, he makes good use of it either way.

Oak becomes a radically different person with each of his reincarnations, flipping between neutral good and neutral evil. His memories of past lives have been fractured by his many deaths, but he spends each new life accounting for the previous life in a karmic-ledger kind of way. His current incarnation embraces the good side. Mostly. Except for that occasional toxic bitterness. Oh, and the misanthropy. Actually, if you end up hating this guy, it's probably not your fault.

entries.name: Divine Strike
entries.description: Once on each of his turns when he hits a creature with a weapon attack, Omin can cause the attack to deal an extra 4 (1d8) damage of the same type dealt by the weapon.

entries.name: Fey Ancestry
entries.description: Omin has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put him to sleep.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Omin is a 9th-level spellcaster. His spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save 15, +7 to hit with spell attacks). He has the following cleric spells prepared:

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

Cantrips (at will): guidance, sacred flame, spare the dying, thaumaturgy

Level 1 (4 slots): bless, command, divine favor, shield of faith

Level 2 (3 slots): enhance ability, hold person, magic weapon, silence, spiritual weapon

Level 3 (3 slots): beacon of hope, crusader's mantle, dispel magic, mass healing word, spirit guardians

Level 4 (3 slots): death ward, freedom of movement, locate creature, stoneskin

Level 5 (1 slots): dispel evil and good, flame strike, hold monster, greater restoration, legend lore

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Omin makes two attacks with his maul.

entries.name: Maul
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: War God's Blessing (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries.description: When a creature within 30 feet of Omin makes an attack roll, but before learning whether it hits or misses, Omin can grant the creature a +10 bonus to that roll.

info.text:
My duty, first and foremost, is to my shareholders. And I am the only shareholder.

Ominifis Hereward Dran spent his formative years in the small way-stop of Red Larch, where his mother, Prophetess, ran a popular inn and restaurant. In the brief periods of respite afforded by working the family business, Omin and his sisters, Auspicia and Portentia, were wont to wander the hills and trails around town, dreaming of adventure. But adventure of the wrong kind came calling for the trio one day, when an underground ruin they had often explored-actually a creature called the Wandering Crypt-took Auspicia from the world.

Omin Dran built the organization called Acquisitions Incorporated to facilitate and expand his quest to find his true sister, at least in part. For despite his unprecedented success in establishing the market for franchised adventuring across the Sword Coast and beyond, Omin's full measure eludes most people. He is known to be a worshiper of Tymora, ruthless in matters of business, feckless in matters of love, and hopeless in games of chance. Omin is also often accused of being one of the Masked Lords of Waterdeep, though this bit of fancy earns little more than a chuckle in response. And even if the rumor were true, Omin would never leverage such a position for greater financial gain and power. Because that would be wrong...

entries.name: Echo Spell (1/Day)
entries.description: Pendragon can cast the spell he cast on his last turn, whose casting time becomes 1 bonus action. This bonus casting uses a spell slot as normal.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Pendragon is a 4th-level spellcaster. His spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). He has the following wizard spells prepared:

Spellcasting ability: INT.

Cantrips (at will): acid splash, light, mage hand, poison spray, shocking grasp

Level 1 (4 slots): detect magic, mage armor, magic missile, sleep

Level 2 (3 slots): blindness/deafness, cloud of daggers, scorching ray

entries.name: Shortsword
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

info.text:
Able arcanist Pendragon Beestinger took over as "B" Team cartographer after Brahma Lutier left the group. In fact, his first assignment was to assist in the team's attempts to apprehend the wandering bard. An adopted child of the "C" Team's Rosie Beestinger, Pendragon is his mother's foil in almost every way-including his goal of wanting to mainstream some of the family's rumored criminal interests. Pendragon has, in fact, attempted to kill his mother-and been killed himself in the process. Despite his having been resurrected at Rosie's request, things remain cool between the two.

Pendragon was kicked out of wizarding school as a result of the dark rumors following the Beestinger clan. Now a self-taught mage, he specializes in making use of the dangerous spells and weird trinkets he often comes across in his role as a kind of arcane archaeologist. Seeking out the family feeling that an adventuring group provides keeps him in the "B" Team, even if that unfortunately comes with Oak Truestrike as a kind of father figure.

entries.name: Divine Display (1/Day)
entries.description: As a bonus action, Phoenix causes his shield to flare with divine light. Each creature of his choice within 30 feet of him must succeed on a 13 Wisdom saving throw or be blinded for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself with a success.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Phoenix is a 4th-level spellcaster. His spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). He has the following cleric spells prepared:

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

Cantrips (at will): guidance, light, mending, sacred flame

Level 1 (4 slots): bane, cure wounds, guiding bolt

Level 2 (3 slots): hold person, spiritual weapon

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Phoenix makes two melee attacks.

entries.name: Warhammer
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage, and the target must succeed on a 12 Strength saving throw or be pushed 5 feet.

info.text:
The "B" Team hoards person, Phoenix Anvil is a servant of Waukeen and a soft-spoken sort. Really soft. Like, he talks so infrequently that even he might not recognize his own voice. Phoenix comes from the streets, where he grew up a fighter until a job sweeping the steps of a small temple of Waukeen showed him a new path. His hunger for coin as an adventurer is thus guided by his knowledge of what it is to do without.

More of an object individual than a people person, Phoenix is obsessively dedicated to the franchise's assets and accounts. Thankfully, he includes his fellow members among those assets, making him fiercely loyal. However, Oak Truestrike is the only team member he's ever really warmed to, which doesn't do either of them any good.

entries.name: Sneak Attack (1/Turn)
entries.description: Portentia deals an extra 14 (4d6) damage when she hits a target with a weapon attack and has advantage on the attack roll, or when the target is within 5 feet of an ally of Portentia that isn't incapacitated and Portentia doesn't have disadvantage on the attack roll.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Portentia makes three melee attacks.

entries.name: Shortsword
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage.

entries.name: Change Shape
entries.description: Portentia magically polymorphs into a humanoid or beast that has a challenge rating equal to or less than her own, or back into her true form. Any equipment she is wearing or carrying is absorbed or borne by the new form (her choice). In a new form, Portentia retains her game statistics and ability to speak, but her AC, movement modes, Strength, Dexterity, and special senses are replaced by those of the new form, and she gains any statistics and capabilities (except class features, legendary actions, and lair actions) that the new form has but that she lacks.

info.text:
Now the owner and driving force behind Dran Enterprises-perhaps Acquisitions Incorporated's most notable rival in the adventuring-for-profit-and-power biz—Portentia Dran is more than she appears to be. Quite literally. The person known as Portentia is actually a changeling, who took the place of the real Portentia before her fifth year.

The changeling Portentia can affect a range of dis guises, and has spent long years engaged in a mission of manipulating the members of the Dran family. Years ago, it was Portentia who tricked her sister Auspicia into exploring the depths of the Wandering Crypt. And she would have been successful in arranging for Omin to be claimed by that creature as well if he hadn't fled immediately in search of a weapon to aid his captured sister.

Whether in combat or social encounters, Portentia shifts frequently between different forms and mindsets, only some of which are fully humanoid. She fights to maim, with a cruel combat style that emphasizes surprise and painful instruction. She is willing to affect any appearance or attitude to achieve her goals. But what those goals are-for herself and Dran Enterprises alike-remain a secret known only to her.

entries.name: Divine Eminence
entries.description: As a bonus action, Prophetess can expend a spell slot to cause her melee weapon attacks to magically deal an extra 10 (3d6) radiant damage to a target on a hit. This benefit lasts until the end of the turn. If Prophetess expends a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the extra damage increases by 1d6 for each level above 1st.

entries.name: Fey Ancestry
entries.description: Prophetess has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put her to sleep.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Prophetess is a 5th-level spellcaster. Her spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). Prophetess has the following cleric spells prepared:

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

Cantrips (at will): light, sacred flame, thaumaturgy

Level 1 (4 slots): cure wounds, guiding bolt, sanctuary

Level 2 (3 slots): lesser restoration, spiritual weapon

Level 3 (2 slots): dispel magic, spirit guardians

entries.name: Maul
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Brave
entries.description: Rosie has advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

entries.name: Halfling Nimbleness
entries.description: Rosie can move through the space of any creature that is of a size larger than hers.

entries.name: Evasion
entries.description: If Rosie is subjected to an effect that allows her to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, she instead takes no damage if she succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if she fails. She can't use this trait if she's incapacitated.

entries.name: Shadow Step
entries.description: When Rosie is in dim light or darkness, she can use a bonus action to teleport 60 feet to an unoccupied space she can see that is also in dim light or darkness. She then has advantage on the first melee attack she makes before the end of the turn.

entries.name: Innate Spellcasting
entries.description:
Rosie's innate spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save 12). She can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

At will: minor illusion, sacred flame, thaumaturgy

1/day each: command, darkness, darkvision, pass without trace, silence

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Rosie makes three attacks, then makes two unarmed strike attacks.

entries.name: Staff of the Master (+1 Quarterstaff)
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage, or 8 (1d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage if used with two hands.

entries.name: Unarmed Strike
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage. Rosie's unarmed strikes are magical.

entries.name: Deflect Missiles
entries.description: In response to being hit by a ranged weapon attack, Rosie deflects the missile. The damage she takes from the attack is reduced by 1d10 + 9. If the damage is reduced to 0, she catches the missile if it's small enough to hold in one hand and she has a hand free.

info.text:
Well, I have this jar of eyeballs...

Weighing in at just under 30 pounds and with a grandmotherly demeanor befitting her advanced age, Rosie Beestinger is easily mistaken for someone on the wrong side of the "aggressor/victim" relationship. But this is a mix-up that few people make more than once. Patient and studious, Rosie has schooled more than one malcontent with what the halfling refers to as "the sauce"-a whirlwind of kicks and punches to one or the other haunches that can inspire even the toughest half-orc to sprint toward anyplace Rosie isn't. As an increasing number of folk hear the tales of her prowess, the "C" Team cartographer's fame among her fellow halflings has become nothing short of legendary. Still, this adoration might be augmented by the sheer number of halflings related to Rosie. She has a daunting number of natural and adopted children, many of whom have followed their mother along the adventuring career track.

Rosie's goals have always been more complex than merely seeking after adventure. She has long sought for ultimate meaning in the stars, and to seek justification for her belief that her bonds to her expansive family are reflected in the endless movements and intricate patterns of the sky. However, the Beestinger clan has a less metaphysical reputation in the eyes of many people, as constantly swirling rumors attempt to connect the family to various and nefarious halfling criminal enter prises. Naturally, Rosie knows nothing about any of that. Sure, her nickname is "Grandmother Night," but that probably doesn't mean anything.

entries.name: Defensive Advantage
entries.description: As long as two or more of Splugoth's allies are within 5 feet of him and are not incapacitated, attack rolls against him are made with disadvantage.

entries.name: Nimble Escape
entries.description: Splugoth can take the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action on each of his turns.

entries.name: Touch of Madness
entries.description: Splugoth has advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Splugoth makes two attacks with his dagger.

entries.name: Dagger
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) slashing damage.

entries.name: Word From Beyond (1/Day)
entries.description: Splugoth remembers and repeats aloud a few words from a place he entered while walking back from the next world to this one. Each creature of his choice within 30 feet of him that can hear him must succeed on a 12 Wisdom saving throw or be stunned until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Absorb Attack
entries.description: When a creature Splugoth can see hits him with a melee weapon attack, the weapon snags on a pocket of residual resurrectional energy and is caught fast. The attack is negated and the weapon cannot be used until the creature succeeds on a 12 Strength (Athletics) check as an action to pull it out of Splugoth. Natural weapons can have their attacks negated by this feature, but can then be retracted automatically at the end of the attacking creature's turn.

info.text:
I'm going to give you a piece of advice. Don't trust Acquisitions Incorporated. And never, ever, ever trust Omin Dran. Wait, that's two pieces of advice. You owe me.

Sometimes a goblin can't catch a break. First, you fall in with a cult that works for the release of a death god. Then you get taken prisoner by a group of sociopathic adventurers who end up letting you die after you save their sorry lives. One minute, you're a dead goblin named Splug. And then you're alive again, and it seems like a really good idea to play up the drama of resurrection with a cool new name-and a master plan for cold, cold revenge against those who betrayed you.

Every once in a while, the (accidentally) capricious and (totally unintentionally) self-centered nature of an Acquisitions Incorporated franchise might incur some collateral damage among followers, hirelings, and staff. When that happens, the collateral damage sometimes inspires some collateral damage of its own. No one is entirely sure how many times Splugoth the Returned has actually returned from the dead. But as the point goblin for the group known as the Six (see "Factions and Rivals" in chapter 3), he's made vengeance against Acq Inc and Omin Dran his life's work. And then the work of his next life. And the one after that.

entries.name: Evasion
entries.description: If Viari is subjected to an effect that allows him to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, he instead takes no damage if he succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if he fails. He can't use this trait if he's incapacitated.

entries.name: Second-Story Work
entries.description: Climbing does not cost Viari extra movement. Additionally, when he makes a running jump, the distance he covers increases by 5 feet.

entries.name: Sneak Attack (1/Turn)
entries.description: Viari deals an extra 14 (4d6) damage when he hits a target with a weapon attack and has advantage on the attack roll, or when the target is within 5 feet of an ally of Viari that isn't incapacitated and Viari doesn't have disadvantage on the attack roll.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Viari makes two attacks with his shortsword and two attacks with his rapier.

entries.name: +1 Shortsword
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d6 + 6) piercing damage.

entries.name: Rapier
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) piercing damage.

entries.name: Dagger
entries.description: Melee Weapon or Ranged Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d4 + 5) piercing damage.

entries.name: Uncanny Dodge
entries.description: Viari halves the damage that he takes from an attack that hits him. He must be able to see the attacker.

info.text:
I know a story about that...

A product of life on a small-town farm, the rogue known as Viari carries fond memories of those childhood days and his loving family. (Well, except for that thing where his parents insist on thinking of his older brother as the successful one.) But he can be quick to show self-consciousness when talking of where he came from, and he never speaks of the name he bore in that former life After quickly rising in the ranks of Acquisitions Incorporated since joining that august team, Viari has come to head what's known as the organization's Stabbing Department. A potent threat in both dueling and earnest debate, he demonstrates an equal flair for planning and forethought, mad combat moves (involving leaping off high places whenever possible), and dark vengeance.

Viari's career as an adventurer was nearly cut short during a battle of which the bards still sing. Unleashing a devastating attack with the aptly named Apocalypse Dagger, the rogue destroyed a giant single-handedly—and lost his arm in the process. Although Viari was made bodily whole again in an equally dramatic magical fashion, some of those closest to him have noticed that those miraculous events weigh on him still, perhaps suggesting consequences that only he foresees.

entries.name: Fey Ancestry
entries.description: Walnut has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put her to sleep.

entries.name: Mask of the Wild
entries.description: Walnut can attempt to hide even when she is only lightly obscured by foliage, heavy rain, falling snow, mist, and other natural phenomena.

entries.name: Wild Shape (Recharges after a Short or Long rest)
entries.description:
As a bonus action, Walnut can assume the shape of a dire wolf. She can stay in this form for 3 hours or until she reverts to her normal form as a bonus action. She automatically reverts if she falls unconscious, drops to 0 hit points, or dies.

While transformed, Walnut's game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the dire wolf, except she retains her alignment, personality, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores.

Her attacks in beast form are magical. While in beast form, Walnut can use a bonus action to expend one spell slot and regain 1d8 hit points per level of the spell slot expended.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Walnut is a 7th-level spellcaster. Her spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). She has the following druid spells prepared:

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

Cantrips (at will): druidcraft, produce flame, thorn whip

Level 1 (4 slots): cure wounds, entangle, thunderwave

Level 2 (3 slots): flame blade, moonbeam, pass without trace

Level 3 (3 slots): call lightning, dispel magic, plant growth

Level 4 (1 slots): blight, freedom of movement

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Walnut makes two attacks with Foremother or her longbow.

entries.name: Foremother (+1 Scimitar)
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage.

entries.name: Longbow
entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage.

info.text:
The war ever rages.

Growing up in an all-female clan of druids, healers, and rangers, Walnut Dankgrass was drawn to the role of protector from her earliest years. Dedicated to Mielikki, the matriarchal clan known as the Enclave Panax Anima defended the unspoiled wild by word and blade (with the latter option more prevalent by far). But when tragedy struck the enclave, Walnut's clan was destroyed to the last-leaving her with nothing but the all-consuming desire to seek out and destroy those responsible.

As a guardian of the wild, Walnut has long held an antipathy toward civilization and anything urban. However, understanding that civilization was the source of the evil that destroyed her people, she makes the city her home now. She embraces her role as the "C" Team's documancer, knowing that the city's power-and its weaknesses-can be fully gleaned only from within.

Walnut distrusts most folk she meets, except for those whose bearing reflects the matriarchal structure she was once part of. No matter what shape her struggles take, she knows instinctively that her beliefs are right and true-and that she will follow those beliefs to the bitter end.

entries.name: Elemental Demise
entries.description: If Exul dies, his body disintegrates in a flash of fire and puff of smoke, leaving behind only the equipment he was wearing or carrying.

entries.name: Innate Spellcasting
entries.description:
Exul's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save 15, +7 to hit with spell attacks). He can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

At will: detect magic

3/day each: comprehend languages, tongues

1/day each: conjure elemental (earth or fire elemental only), invisibility, major image, plane shift, wall of fire

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Exul makes two handaxe attacks or uses his Hurl Flame twice.

entries.name: Handaxe
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) fire damage.

entries.name: Hurl Flame
entries.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +7 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (5d6) fire damage.

info.text:
With his skin aglow like searing coal, a beard like sheafs of burnt paper, and hair billowing like smoke, Exul's physical form does nothing to hide his elemental nature. He was born as a spirit of earth and flame. This physical manifestation is a dalliance of mere decades, he hopes.

Exul serves Tyreus not out of loyalty, but due to a geas. Exul bears Tyreus only a little ill will, however, as occasional "arrangements" with mortal wizards are no great hassle. Exul resents and avoids the pain of the geas, ideally, but has no intention of dying for Tyreus's petty, mortal ambitions.
info.source: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms: In Scarlet Flames, page 12

entries.name: Benign Transportation (Recharges after Malivar Casts a Conjuration Spell of 1st Level or Higher)
entries.description:
As a bonus action, Malivar teleports up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space that he can see.

If he instead chooses a space within range that is occupied by a willing Small or Medium creature, they both teleport, swapping places.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Malivar is a 9th-level spellcaster. His spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). He has the following wizard spells prepared:

Spellcasting ability: INT.

Cantrips (at will): acid splash, mage hand, poison spray, prestidigitation

Level 1 (4 slots): mage armor, magic missile, unseen servant*

Level 2 (3 slots): cloud of daggers*, misty step*, web*

Level 3 (3 slots): fireball, thunder step [XGE]*

Level 4 (3 slots): Evard's black tentacles*, stoneskin

Level 5 (2 slots): cone of cold*, conjure elemental*

*Conjuration spell of 1st level or higher

entries.name: Dagger
entries.description: Melee Weapon or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.

info.text:
Malivar Kresk is a Red Wizard of Thay, a conjurer, and recent apprentice to the treacherous Red Wizard named Morwena. Young, pale white, plain, and slender, Malivar usually hates his own appearance but hopes his red robes and smooth scalp give him a "lean and mean" look.

Now alone on his mission, Malivar doesn't hesitate to use or abuse the trust of others if it means he can get revenge, return to Thay alive, and report on Morwena's betrayal.
info.source: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms: In Scarlet Flames, page 12

entries.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries.description: The horror can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (2/Day)
entries.description: If the horror fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Shadow Stealth
entries.description: While in dim light or darkness, the horror can take the Hide action as a bonus action.

entries.name: Shadow Stride
entries.description: As a bonus action, the horror can step into a shadow within 5 feet of it and magically appear in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of a second shadow that is up to 60 feet away. Both shadows must be cast by a Medium or larger creature or object.

entries.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
entries.description: While in sunlight, the horror has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The horror makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 21 (4d8 + 3) piercing damage.

entries.name: Claw
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (4d6 + 3) slashing damage, and the target must succeed on a 16 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of the horror until the end of the target's next turn.

entries.name: Lashing Shadows Recharge 5–6
entries.description: Each creature within 60 feet of the horror, except other horrors, must succeed on a 16 Dexterity saving throw or take 36 (8d8) necrotic damage.

entries.name: Claw
entries.description: The horror makes a weapon attack.

entries.name: Glide
entries.description: The horror moves up to 20 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.

entries.name: Frighten Foe (Costs 2 Actions)
entries.description: The horror targets one enemy it can see within 30 feet of it. If the target can see and hear it, the target must succeed on a 16 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened until the end of horror's next turn.

info.text: This shadowy horror was conjured by Tyreus. It is a powerful example of the terrifying evils that stalk the dark corners of Ravnica. This one is an amorphous creature of living shadow with dim reason and preternatural cunning, left here to keep trespassers from plundering the refuge without Tyreus's permission.
info.source: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms: The Hidden Page, page 12

entries.name: Quarterstaff
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 2 (1d6-1) bludgeoning damage, or 3 (1d8-1) bludgeoning damage if used with two hands.

entries.name: Instinctive Charm (Recharges after Morwena Casts an Enchantment Spell of 1st Level or Higher)
entries.description:
Morwena tries to magically divert an attack made against her, provided that the attacker is within 30 feet of her and visible to her. She must decide to do so before the attack hits or misses.

The attacker must make a 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the attacker targets the creature closest to it, other than Morwena or itself. If multiple creatures are closest, the attacker chooses which one to target.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Morwena is a 10th-level spellcaster. Her spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save 15, +6 to hit with spell attacks). She has the following wizard spells prepared:

Spellcasting ability: INT.

Cantrips (at will): friends, mage hand, mending, message

Level 1 (4 slots): charm person*, mage armor, magic missile

Level 2 (3 slots): hold person*, invisibility, suggestion*

Level 3 (3 slots): fireball, haste, tongues

Level 4 (3 slots): arcane eye, phantasmal killer

Level 5 (2 slots): hold monster*

*Enchantment spell of 1st level or higher

info.text:
Morwena Veilmist was a Red Wizard of Thay, but she was never loyal. She saw the Thayan wizards as a means to acquire power. When she met Tyreus, she thought she saw a new opportunity. She abandoned her old apprentice, Malivar, and joined Tyreus. She hoped she'd found a peer in the pursuit of power. She regrets her choice but remains devoted to her own success and no one else's. The lesson she chose to learn was never to trust anyone.

She is a tall, slender Chondathan woman with a severe hairstyle, kept short for simplicity's sake. She wears her fingernails short but sharp. She is a skilled, even cunning, player of dragonchess.

Personality.

"I read anything I can get my hands on. Most creatures aren't as smart as I am, so I talk down to people when I need them to keep up."

Ideal.

"Power. All things flow from personal power, and although I have little of it right now, I shall find new ways to attain and use power for the only person that matters to me: myself."

Bond.

"I've learned a valuable lesson about trusting people: don't. Other people may be of use to me, but I'm not putting myself in a position to be used again."

Flaw.

"I've let myself be fooled into trusting people, but no one is worth that risk. Only fools tell the whole truth."
info.source: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms: The Hidden Page, page 13

entries.name: Invisibility
entries.description: The usagt's true form is invisible.

entries.name: Shapechanger
entries.description: The usagt can use its action to polymorph into a Small, Medium, or Large humanoid it has seen in person or telepathically, or back into its true form. Its statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. While polymorphed, the usagt is not invisible. Its new form appears to wear clothes, carry equipment, and even wield weapons, but these are all parts of the usagt itself; they vanish if dropped or removed from the creature. It can't activate, use, wield, or otherwise benefit from any of its apparent equipment. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

entries.name: Innate Spellcasting
entries.description:
The usagt's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save 15). It can cast the following spells, requiring no spell components:

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

At will: banishment, detect thoughts, disguise self

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The usagt makes two attacks with its claws.

entries.name: Claws
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) slashing damage plus 11 (2d6 + 4) psychic damage.

entries.name: Personal Insight
entries.description:
The usagt targets one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must contest its Charisma (Deception) check against the usagt's Wisdom (Insight) check.

The target has advantage on the roll if it is immune to being charmed. A target can choose to fail this check.

If the usagt wins, it magically learns the identity of a creature from the target's past, someone the target wishes it could speak to again or with whom the target has left something unsaid. If somehow no such creature exists in the target's past, the usagt learns that instead.

entries.name: Invisibility Response (Recharges When the Usagt Uses Its Shapechanger Ability)
entries.description: When the usagt takes damage, it can choose to revert to its default, invisible form and move up to 15 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.

info.text:
These peculiar creatures originate on a tranquil, lawful plane where they lead gentle, languid existences. They enjoy the experiences of life—in memory and in practice—but have curiously few ambitions. Their natural lifespan is centuries long, and they give little thought to the passage of time.

Some scholars of the planes believe usagt are not organisms in any traditional sense but a kind of intelligent being made of notions and psychic matter.

Curiously Shy.

An usagt's true form is amorphous and invisible. They change shape based on the thoughts and memories they observe in other creatures' memories. Each usagt thus has a peculiar sense of itself and its peers, based on what shapes it can take in what order, rather than any visual cues of its own.

Cunning Observers.

The favorite pastime of most usagt is putting on little improvised plays with others of its kind, changing shapes throughout. Usagt observe other creatures and detect their thoughts to broaden the catalog of characters they can portray.

Strange Nature.

Usagt do not reproduce. An usagt requires no food, drink, or sleep, but enjoys them when it can. It does require air.
info.source: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms: The Hidden Page, page 14

entries.name: Sunlight Vulnerability
entries.description: While in sunlight, the snake has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight. When the snake begins its turn in sunlight, it immediately suffers 10 radiant damage.

entries.name: Undead Fortitude
entries.description: If damage reduces the snake to 0 hit points, it must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit. On a success, the snake drops to 1 hit point instead.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The snake makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with a constrict attack.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) piercing damage, and the target must make a 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 17 (5d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Constrict
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape 16). Until this grapple ends, the creature is restrained and the snake cannot constrict another target.

info.text:
These enormous, rotten husks were living, Medium-sized constrictors when the yuan-ti brought them to honor and entice Kyrilla to share her knowledge and powers. They grew to their full, Huge size on a diet of supplicants and prisoners, many of whose bones can be found elsewhere in the lair. When the yuan-ti turned against Kyrilla, they fought and slew these snakes—only to find them slithering again through cursed, ambient magic in Kyrilla's lair.

The constrictors die if they leave the lair.
info.source: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms: Deepest Night, page 11

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Hamish makes two attacks with his axe or throws two rocks.

entries.name: Axe
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) slashing damage.

entries.name: Rock
entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Parry
entries.description: Hamish adds 2 to his AC against one melee attack that would hit him. To do so, he must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon or a shield.

info.text:
A gentle giant with a ferocious laugh, Hamish hails from the city of Waterdeep. He was never one for the wilderness in his younger days, but he wanted adventure. He joined his friends, Sylvene and Artura, on their journey into the wilds of the Sword Coast, all those years ago, and was part of their adventuring party with a human from Secomber named Waltarn Everlake. That Hamish would be willing to risk his life to protect his friends was never in doubt.

Hamish has brown skin, great posture, and wears his long hair in three tidy braids. He is the sort of fellow who overpacks for an adventure. His pockets usually teem with snacks or rations. Being a giant, he brought both a dungeoneer's pack and an explorer's pack in his knapsack. He carries a big axe, suitable for his size. He also carried a round, wooden shield, made just for him by Artura, but it has rotted to bits.

Personality Traits.

"I am curious about the road not taken, sometimes to a fault. I try to always have food with me."

Ideal.

"Bravery. I would risk my life for true friends. In fact, I have!"

Bond.

"Friendships you choose can mean more than family. A friend made is an enemy defeated."

Flaw.

"I often believe in people to the point of being naive."
info.source: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms: Deepest Night, page 11

entries.name: Feed on Pain (2/Day)
entries.description: The first time she hits with a weapon attack on her turn, Kyrilla can deal an extra 16 (3d10) poison damage to the target and regains a number of hit points equal to half the damage dealt.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (2/Day)
entries.description: If she fails a saving throw, Kyrilla can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Petrifying Gaze
entries.description:
When a creature that can see Kyrilla's eyes starts its turn within 30 feet of her, Kyrilla can force it to make a 14 Constitution saving throw if Kyrilla isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the creature is instantly petrified. Otherwise, a creature that fails the save begins to turn to stone and is restrained. The restrained creature must repeat the saving throw at the end of its next turn, becoming petrified on a failure or ending the effect on a success. The petrification lasts until the creature is freed by the greater restoration spell or other magic.

Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see Kyrilla until the start of its next turn, when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at Kyrilla in the meantime, it must immediately make the save.

Kyrilla's accursed gaze does not affect undead or constructs. If Kyrilla sees herself reflected on a polished surface within 30 feet of her and in an area of bright light, she is, due to her curse, affected by her own gaze.

entries.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
entries.description: While in sunlight, Kyrilla has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Kyrilla makes one attack to constrict and two attacks with her claws, or she makes three attacks with her longbow.

entries.name: Claw
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) slashing damage.

entries.name: Constrict
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape 13) if it is a Large or smaller creature. Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and Kyrilla can't constrict another target.

entries.name: Longbow
entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (3d8 + 3) piercing damage.

entries.name: Summon Swarm of Poisonous Snakes Recharge 5–6
entries.description:
Kyrilla conjures a swarm of poisonous snakes into an empty space within 10 feet of her. The swarm is under Kyrilla's control and acts on her turn, immediately after her in the initiative order.

It remains in existence for up to 1 hour. She can summon no more than three swarms per day. Kyrilla can banish any or all of her summoned swarms with a bonus action.

entries.name: Claw
entries.description: Kyrilla or a swarm of poisonous snakes makes a weapon attack.

entries.name: Detect
entries.description: Kyrilla makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.

entries.name: Slither
entries.description: Kyrilla moves up to her speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

sections.title: Lair Actions
sections.description:
When fighting inside her lair, Kyrilla can invoke the ambient magic there to take lair actions. On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), she takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects:

• Kyrilla casts moonbeam (no components required). While maintaining concentration on this effect, she can't take other lair actions.
• Kyrilla casts cloud of daggers (no components required), except the daggers are flying snakes and the spell deals piercing damage. While maintaining concentration on this effect, she can't take other lair actions.
• Pools of liquid within 60 feet of Kyrilla surge and froth, splashing and soaking any creature on the ground within 5 feet of such pools. Creatures that succeed on a 14 Dexterity saving throw avoid getting liquid in their eyes and mouths. Kyrilla can't use this lair action again until she has used a different one.

sections.title: Regional Effects
sections.description:
The region containing Kyrilla's lair is warped by her accursed nature and the meteoric stone around her, which together create the following effects:

• Water sources within the lair are supernaturally fouled and poisonous. Creatures that drink these waters must make a 14 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. Afflicted creatures can make a new saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the condition on a success.
• Plants within 1 mile of the lair suffer from a calcifying mold that dries and hardens leaves, killing many otherwise hearty thistles and heather.
• Fog lightly obscures the land within 3 miles of the lair.

info.text:
Some small part of Kyrilla hopes she might be pardoned from her immortal curse one day, but her ire and spite have overtaken her heart, and the only way she can imagine escaping eternity is by impressing the gods with her tenacity. She doesn't want pity nor compassion. She wants to be feared and loathed and to press on with existence despite it all. And now that Kathikon is dead and she is alone, she cannot remember mercy.

Personality Trait.

"I am quick to judge others and find them wanting."

Ideal.

"Spite. I survive despite a curse from the gods—I'm not about to go out into the world where fools will try to kill me."

Bond.

"Kathikon was the love of my life. No one else matters to me."

Flaw.

"I never admit when I am wrong."

Horrific Appearance.

Once, Kyrilla looked much like other gorgons of her world. Now, with her curse upon her, Kyrilla's healthy greenish skin has grown sickly pale, and the segmented cables she wore like hair have gone from shiny black to matte gray and green. Her legs became a long, segmented tail. Her eyes now glow green, bright enough to create dim light in front of her. She has grown four needle-like fangs in her mouth, and her hands have become slicing claws.

She reverts to her original appearance when she dies.

Bestowed Power.

The malevolent powers bestowed to Kyrilla by her curse, as well as those given to her by the yuan-ti cult, are hardly of interest to her. She doesn't relish power but instead has taken to wallowing in misery and dwelling in her hatred for the beings that cursed her so long ago that she can hardly remember them.

Magic Ring.

Kyrilla wears a ring of water walking that she was given by an emissary from the Serpent Kingdoms long ago. It is made of a bluish jade and does not reflect light.

Immortal Curse.

Kyrilla does not require food or drink but does breathe and sleep.

Lair Actions.

When fighting inside her lair, Kyrilla can invoke the ambient magic there to take lair actions. On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), she takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects:

• Kyrilla casts moonbeam (no components required). While maintaining concentration on this effect, she can't take other lair actions.
• Kyrilla casts cloud of daggers (no components required), except the daggers are flying snakes and the spell deals piercing damage. While maintaining concentration on this effect, she can't take other lair actions.
• Pools of liquid within 60 feet of Kyrilla surge and froth, splashing and soaking any creature on the ground within 5 feet of such pools. Creatures that succeed on a 14 Dexterity saving throw avoid getting liquid in their eyes and mouths. Kyrilla can't use this lair action again until she has used a different one.

Regional Effects.

The region containing Kyrilla's lair is warped by her accursed nature and the meteoric stone around her, which together create the following effects:

• Water sources within the lair are supernaturally fouled and poisonous. Creatures that drink these waters must make a 14 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. Afflicted creatures can make a new saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the condition on a success.
• Plants within 1 mile of the lair suffer from a calcifying mold that dries and hardens leaves, killing many otherwise hearty thistles and heather.
• Fog lightly obscures the land within 3 miles of the lair.
info.source: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms: Deepest Night, page 12

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The horror makes two attacks with its claws.

entries.name: Claw
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (3d10 + 3) slashing damage.

entries.name: Wave of Bones Recharge 5–6
entries.description: The horror crashes into foes like a wave before quickly reforming. Each creature within 10 feet of the horror must make a 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 18 (4d8) bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that fails this saving throw is also knocked prone.

info.text:
This horrid mass of bones clambers along on a dozen hands and feet without maintaining any consistent shape. One moment it moves like a centipede, the next it rears back to claw like a bear. The only consistent feature is a weird absence: no matter how many skulls make up its mass, this strange horror always seems to be headless.

The skeletal horrors in Kyrilla's lair are made from the bones of yuan-ti supplicants and cultists who came to learn her powers or, later, to steal them. She spared none of these intruders' lives, and in death their remains do her bidding.
info.source: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms: Deepest Night, page 13

entries.name: Inspired Courage
entries.description: The mercenary has advantage on savings throws against being charmed, frightened, grappled, or restrained while within 5 feet of at least one ally.

entries.name: Martial Advantage
entries.description: Once per turn, the mercenary can deal an extra 7 (2d6) damage to a creature it hits with a weapon attack if that creature is within 5 feet of an ally of the mercenary that isn't incapacitated.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The mercenary makes two longsword attacks.

entries.name: Longsword

entries.name: Heavy Crossbow
entries.description:
Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range

100/400 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing damage.

info.text:
These mercenaries stand for the Banner of Blades and the Iron Lions at Tyreus's fortress, but they might not be representative of those armies. These are rank-and-file warriors capable of demonstrating coordinated attacks and formations. They are neither the most capable lieutenants nor the rough-and-tumble masses of these small armies.

For the purposes of their Inspired Courage feature, the mercenaries of both companies consider each other allies while at the fortress—unless the adventurers do something to drive them apart.
info.source: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms: From Cyan Depths, page 10

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries.description: If Tyreus fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Illusory Reality
entries.description:
When Tyreus casts an illusion spell of 1st level or higher, he can choose one inanimate, nonmagical object that is part of the illusion and make that object real. He can do this on his turn as a bonus action while the spell is ongoing.

The object remains real for 1 minute. The object can't deal damage or otherwise directly harm anyone.

entries.name: Displacement (Recharges after Tyreus Casts an Illusion Spell of 1st Level or Higher)
entries.description: As a bonus action, Tyreus projects an illusion that makes him appear to be standing a few inches from his actual location, causing any creature to have disadvantage on attack rolls against Tyreus. The effect ends if Tyreus takes damage, he is incapacitated, or his speed becomes 0.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Tyreus is a 16th-level spellcaster. His spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save 18, +10 to hit with spell attacks). He has the following wizard spells prepared.

Spellcasting ability: INT.

Cantrips (at will): fire bolt, light, mage hand, minor illusion, shocking grasp

Level 1 (4 slots): mage armor, magic missile, shield, thunderwave

Level 2 (3 slots): invisibility*, mirror image*, phantasmal force*

Level 3 (3 slots): counterspell, fly, lightning bolt, major image*

Level 4 (3 slots): banishment, hallucinatory terrain*, phantasmal killer*, stoneskin

Level 5 (2 slots): conjure elemental, mislead*, telekinesis

Level 6 (1 slots): disintegrate

Level 7 (1 slots): plane shift

Level 8 (1 slots): maze

*(Illusion spell of 1st level or higher)

entries.name: Dagger
entries.description: Melee Weapon or Ranged Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.

entries.name: Modify Illusion
entries.description: When Tyreus casts an illusion spell that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, he can use his action to change the nature of that illusion (using the spell's normal parameters for the illusion), provided that he can see the illusion.

entries.name: Scrutinize
entries.description: Tyreus makes an Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Perception) check.

entries.name: Cast Cantrip
entries.description: Tyreus casts a cantrip from his spell list.

entries.name: Cast Spell (Costs 1-3 Actions)
entries.description: Tyreus uses a spell slot to cast a 1st-, 2nd-, or 3rd-level spell that he has prepared. Doing so costs 1 legendary action per level of the spell.

info.text:
When he was young, living in the vast, internecine planar city of Ravnica, Tyreus's parents, Tyberio and Ayraea, forbade him from pursuing any study of magic or wizardry. They didn't want Tyreus embroiled in a life of danger and skullduggery—as was common in Ravnica. But Tyreus came to understand that at least part of his father's motive for forbidding magic was Tyberio's own rebellion against his adventurous parents. When he learned that his grandmother had once been a powerful mage, Tyreus wanted to follow in her footsteps.

Power Hungry.

Tyreus has always wanted to be distinctive, admired, and powerful. He saw magic as a way to achieve a greatness he felt Tyberio had tried to deny him. In secret, Tyreus sought out ways to learn magic, but as he was forced to hide his ambition and his studies, he found cohorts in the worst places. Evil mages stoked his hunger for power and eroded his conscience.

Mundane Fury.

Tyreus went months without speaking to his parents. Before he even knew they were sick, Tyberio and Ayraea passed away. Furious at his inability to help them—and their silent stubbornness—Tyreus sought the kind of power that would help him create places he could control. First, he studied the magic of illusions. He thought he could create illusions so real that he could live within them, fool others, and thus control his own destiny. Then he found another possibility.

Selfish Pursuits.

In journals Tyberio had hidden from him, written by Tyberio's mother, the wizard Sylvene, Tyreus found tales of the Stone of Creation, an artifact capable of creating places and structures seemingly from the imagination alone. Tyreus thus sought out everything he could learn about Sylvene and the Stone, leading him to another world—Faerûn—and the remote Highstar Lake, where the Stone was lost long ago.

Lost to Ambition.

It may be too late for Tyreus. He has devoted himself to his own grandeur now and lost sight of why he wanted power in the first place. He doesn't want to help anyone but himself. He sees those who would help him or share in his ambitions as threats to his own power. He doesn't want approval or alliances; he wants subservience. Whether he realizes it or not, he doesn't care whom he hurts to get what he wants.

Personality Traits.

"I laugh to buy myself time to think, even though my gut instincts are often better than most people's calculated efforts."

Ideals.

"Power. People try to take things from me, to limit or deny me, but I don't allow it. Real power is deciding other people's fates."

Bonds.

"I'll make time for other people when I have a kingdom to call my own. Then I'll know who I can trust: the people who don't get in my way."

Flaws.

"I have a bad temper. Why can't people see I know what I'm doing?"
info.source: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms: From Cyan Depths, page 11

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The archmage has Advantage [XPHB] on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

Failure: 45 (10d8) Force damage, and the target has the Incapacitated [XPHB] condition and is transported to a harmless demiplane until the start of the archmage's next turn, at which point it reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied. Success: Half damage only.

info.text:
Abjurer archmages create powerful magical wards. Their magic allows them to quarantine dangerous foes, and they're adept at nullifying the spells of even fellow archmages. Despite their focus on protective magic, abjurer archmages are formidable offensive combatants.

Masters of Magic

Although all archmages have mastered incredible magical power, some specialize in a particular school of magic, pushing their abilities to greater heights in that area. These archmages stock their spellbooks with spells from their preferred school and have developed unique magical techniques.

Immense and specialized magical prowess isn't an end in its own right. It's how one uses their power that matters.

— Alustriel

info.text:
Undead Protector of Ancient Sites

Baelnorns [AU] are deathless guardians of treasures and lore. Each baelnorn was once a living person who undertook a non-evil process to preserve their existence that involved either a divine blessing or an ancient ritual. Many baelnorns were once elves. In fact, ancient elves were the first to discover the secret to becoming a baelnorn.

Baelnorns [AU] typically dedicate themselves to protecting vaults, castles, or ruins. In the Forgotten Realms, elf baelnorns protect the site of Myth Drannor, a ruined ancient city that was once a magical metropolis. Many enjoy studying ancient lore lost to living scholars. As only the most dedicated can endure the transition into a baelnorn, baelnorns are often proud of the eternal life they've achieved.

Unlike liches, baelnorns almost never have soul jars, although some baelnorns associated with a holy site might house their souls within a sacred relic. Many baelnorns create magical clones their spirits can inhabit if their bodies are destroyed.

Newly risen baelnorns look much as they did in life, albeit with glowing white eyes. They often continue their prior roles as guardians, sages, or teachers. A baelnorn's hair and flesh gradually fade away over many years; the oldest resemble stately skeletons in diaphanous raiment.

Baelnorns [AU] spend years poring over arcane tomes to aid their transition into undeath, and even those who weren't mages at the time of their transformation typically spend much of their long existences studying magical lore. As a result, baelnorns can cast powerful spells.

Baelnorn Lairs.

Most baelnorns guard sites of historical or spiritual importance, sometimes long past the time anyone living remembers the sites. A few baelnorns instead guard great secrets, artifacts, or significant family lines, usually within such ancient sites. A baelnorn's protected site might be a grove of supernatural trees, the ruined capitol of a long-lost nation, or a library holding eons-old magical lore.

A baelnorn extends its presence into the region it inhabits, creating the following effects:

• Projection.

While in its lair, the baelnorn can cast Project Image [XPHB], requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 19). The spell's range is limited to the baelnorn's lair.
• Travel Ward.

Creatures can't use teleportation or planar travel to enter or exit the lair.

If the baelnorn is destroyed or moves its lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately.

Most baelnorns embody the ideal of scholarly focus and self-sacrifice for the benefit of society. If you meet one, I suspect they'd appreciate sharing a lively conversation or ten. Forever can be a lonely existence.

— Alustriel

entries.name: Flyby (Flyer Only)

info.text:
Flying, Mutated Minion of Wickedness

Darkenbeasts [AU] are ferocious, bestial hunters created from ordinary animals by sinister spellcasters. Regardless of darkenbeasts' original forms, the magic used to create them twists them into fanged horrors with leathery wings. Most darkenbeasts have luminous bones that glow through their skin; they resemble eerie flying skeletons as they soar through the night sky. A darkenbeast is loyal to its creators, who can extract the magic used to transform it in a dramatic display that's fatal to the darkenbeast.

Darkenbeasts [AU] might have vestigial characteristics of the animals they were before transformation. Roll on or choose a result from the Darkenbeast Origin table as inspiration for these cosmetic features.

info.text:
Accompanied by blasts of frigid wind, a living cone of cold seeks sources of heat—such as living creatures—to freeze solid.

Animate Magical Effects

Magical energies unleashed during cataclysmic battles or catastrophic experiments can cause spell effects to come to life as living spells. These beings' magical energy is persistent, and they bear features resembling those of their origin spells—usually Conjuration or Evocation spells. Living spells typically linger in the region of their creation, subsisting on ambient magical energy and lashing out at creatures they encounter.

Creating Living Spells.

Living spells come in many varieties; the stat blocks here are three examples. To make a living spell from a different spell, choose a damage-dealing Conjuration or Evocation spell of level 1–5 from the Wizard spell list. Then consult the Living Spell Customization table to see which stat block to customize based on the chosen spell's level.

Living Spell Customization
Spell Level | Stat Block to Customize
1–2 | Living Thunderwave [AU]
3–4 | Living Vitriolic Sphere [AU]
5 | Living Cone of Cold [AU]

Now make the following changes to the stat block:

• Damage Immunity.

Replace the living spell's damage Immunity [XPHB] with Immunity [XPHB] to the type (or types) of damage dealt by the chosen spell.
• Magical Strike.

Change the damage type dealt by Magical Strike to one of the damage types dealt by the chosen spell.
• Spell Mimicry.

Replace the effect of Spell Mimicry with the effect of the chosen spell. If that spell requires a saving throw, use the spell save DC from Spell Mimicry. If the spell involves an attack roll, use the attack bonus from the living spell's Magical Strike.

For example, if you turn Fireball [XPHB] (a level 3 spell) into a living spell, customize the Living Vitriolic Sphere [AU] stat block. The living fireball has Immunity [XPHB] to Fire damage instead of Acid damage, deals Fire damage with its Magical Strike, and replicates Fireball with Spell Mimicry.

Magical energies unleashed during cataclysmic battles or catastrophic experiments can cause spell effects to come to life as living spells. These beings' magical energy is persistent, and they bear features resembling those of their origin spells—usually Conjuration or Evocation spells. Living spells typically linger in the region of their creation, subsisting on ambient magical energy and lashing out at creatures they encounter.

info.text:
Magically Ascended Mage

The most gifted mortal mages can sometimes peer beyond reality to glimpse pure, untrammeled magic. Directly accessing this energy requires years of careful study and dangerous rituals. Any mage who succeeds taps into esoteric powers that strip away the mage's physical body, blending their mortal mind with raw magic to form a quasi-corporeal entity called a taisus, or an ascended mage.

A taisus initially retains the personality and values of the mortal mage it was before, but its mindset eventually becomes alien, taking on a long-term outlook that seems callous to mortals. Most taisuses seek to draw energies from places of significant magical power, such as planar portals or quintessence pools, in order to create bizarre magic items, reshape the nature of magic, or lead others to duplicate their eldritch ascension. A taisus's end goal is unfathomable to mortal minds.

info.text:
Corrupted Force of Evil

An immortal mage and Fiend with an implacable hatred for Tiamat [XDMG], Venger [AU] seeks to rule nations by amassing sycophants and long-lost magical artifacts. Though his bat-like wings allow him to fly, Venger [AU] prefers to ride on his trusted flying steed, a Nightmare [XMM] that lurks on the Ethereal Plane until it's needed. Venger [AU] sends his adviser, Shadow Demon [XMM], to survey distant lands, then weaves interlocking plans based on Shadow Demon's reports.

Venger [AU] was once a good-hearted human studying wizardry under the cryptic tutelage of his father. In time, Venger [AU] grew impatient and sought to increase his magical prowess by dabbling in minor pacts with demons. He eventually met demons who worshipped Tharizdun [XDMG] the Chained God, an entity the demons believed powerful enough to create whole planes of existence. Venger [AU] yearned to forge a pact with this entity, believing that doing so would give him immense power.

With the help of these Tharizdun-worshipping demons, Venger [AU] opened a brief window into the demiplane of Tharizdun's imprisonment. The demons had neglected to mention that the souls of all who look on the Chained God face certain doom. As Venger [AU] gazed on this entity—an unknowable, indescribable blend of demonic and aberrant influence—Venger's form warped, and the last traces of goodness sloughed off him. The demons collected this good essence and locked it in a vault that they spirited away to a distant corner of the Material Plane. Venger [AU] emerged from this encounter as a cruel, twisted version of himself, exalted now with immortality and magical might, and he vowed to free the Chained God.

At first, Venger [AU] earnestly pursued this promise. In time, though, he grew to despise his vow and neglected it in favor of his own pursuit of power. Now he no longer wants Tharizdun freed, knowing his disloyalty could make him a target of Tharizdun's wrath.

After abandoning his quest to free Tharizdun, Venger [AU] sought to use several Orbs of Dragonkind [XDMG] to control Tiamat. This futile endeavor earned Venger Tiamat's lifelong enmity. Venger [AU] now plots endlessly to destroy or subjugate Tiamat, among other nefarious designs. Roll on or choose a result from the Venger's Schemes table to inspire Venger's next power play.

Venger's Schemes
1d6 | Venger Plots To...
1 | Imprison those who would oppose him in a vast labyrinth of his own creation called the Maze of Darkness.
2 | Summon a two-headed, Abyssal dragon called the Demodragon [WttHC] (use the Adult Black Dragon [XMM] stat block) and unleash it on a nation.
3 | Recruit heroes to help him thwart the League of Malevolence, a villainous group led by his former lackey, the mage Kelek.
4 | Disguise himself as a wise wizard or noble paladin to trick innocents into giving him a powerful artifact.
5 | Assemble six powerful magic items and use their magic at a site called the Hall of Bones to gain enough power to destroy Tiamat for good.
6 | Find an artifact called the Box of Balefire and keep it away from other villains; Venger [AU] fears it could unleash Tharizdun.

Venger's Lairs.

Venger [AU] keeps several lairs in each of the worlds he visits. Each is a castle perched above or extending from the side of a treacherous cliff, but none are identical.

Venger's presence fouls the regions his lairs inhabit, creating the following effects:

• Desolate Terrain.

Plant life within 1 mile of a lair withers and dies, creating a barren wasteland of cracked dirt.
• Tormented Rest.

Abyssal whispers plague visitors' dreams. Whenever a creature other than Venger [AU] or his allies finishes a Long Rest [XPHB] within 1 mile of a lair, it must succeed on a 15 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 Exhaustion [XPHB] level.

If Venger dies or moves a lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately.

info.text:
Wicked Serpentine Oppressors

Powerful and magical, sarrukhs once commanded a wicked empire that spanned Faerûn, but it fell tens of thousands of years ago. In the millennia that followed, the many species sarrukhs created drove them nearly to extinction. Only a small number of sarrukhs remain in isolated enclaves, including a small community beneath the Citadel at the heart of Thaymount.

Sarrukhs have snakelike lower bodies and heads but torsos that resemble those of humanoids. Their gleaming eyes are alight with inner fire. Sarrukhs can live for up to a millennium, and most expect to see their empire rise again.

Sarrukh Tyrant.

Most remaining sarrukhs are tyrants who fervently believe the sarrukh empire's resurgence is inevitable. Tyrants live in clans with other sarrukhs, roaming ruins and subjugating creatures that live nearby. They command only a small portion of the magical power their former empire's leaders held.

Arisen Sarrukh.

The most powerful sarrukhs are arisen: horrific creatures that have subverted death. While arisen sarrukhs have lost their ability to cast spells, their unliving flesh is unnaturally strong.
