If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone [XPHB] condition. If the target already has the Prone [XPHB] condition, it instead takes an extra 7 (2d6) Bludgeoning damage. Hit or Miss:The hammer magically returns to the rendelith's hand immediately after a ranged attack.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The rendelith casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 19):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: Move Earth [XPHB], Passwall [XPHB], Shatter [XPHB] (level 6 version), Wall of Stone [XPHB]

entries.name: Quick Fortifications Recharge 5–6
entries.description: The rendelith uses Spellcasting to cast Move Earth [XPHB] or Wall of Stone [XPHB].

info.text:
Demon of Destruction and Sieges

Rendeliths are hulking demons that lead armies in destroying enemy castles, strongholds, and other fortifications. They delight in toppling defenses so demonic hordes can rush into the fray.

Rendeliths have the upper bodies of humanoids but the lower bodies of oxen, with stony spikes along their backs. These cruel demons are masters of strategy that delight in magically producing walls and ditches to drive enemy armies into ambushes. Such ambushes often involve hordes of armanites—similar-looking but weaker demons driven by unrestrained bloodlust.

Most rendeliths have fought for so long in the Blood War, a raging conflict between demons and devils, that they think only in terms of combat. Each wall they collapse brings them grim satisfaction, but their unquenchable drive for the next battle pushes them ever onward.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries.description: If the sarrukh fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The sarrukh has Advantage [XPHB] on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The sarrukh makes two attacks, using Bite or Fearsome Fauchard in any combination.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +12, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) Piercing damage plus 13 (3d8) Poison damage.

entries.name: Fearsome Fauchard
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +12, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) Piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it has the Frightened [XPHB] condition. If the target already has the Frightened [XPHB] condition, it takes an additional 10 (3d6) Psychic damage. Hit or Miss:The fauchard magically returns to the sarrukh's hand immediately after a ranged attack.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The sarrukh casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 20):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: Detect Magic [XPHB], Invisibility [XPHB], Polymorph [XPHB]

2/day each: Fireball [XPHB] (level 5 version), Scrying [XPHB], Teleport [XPHB], Wall of Force [XPHB]

entries.name: Shape Control
entries.description: Trigger: A creature the sarrukh can see shape-shifts. Response: The sarrukh chooses the resulting form from among the options available to the shape-shifting creature or prevents the creature from shape-shifting.

entries.name: Fearsome Glance
entries.description: WIS Saving Throw: 20, one creature the sarrukh can see within 30 feet. Failure: 18 (4d8) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened [XPHB] condition. Success: Half damage only.

entries.name: Slither
entries.description: The sarrukh moves up to half its Speed [XPHB] without provoking Opportunity Attacks [XPHB], and it makes one Bite attack.

entries.name: Twisted Transformation
entries.description: The sarrukh uses Spellcasting to cast Polymorph [XPHB], and if the target fails its saving throw, the target also has the Stunned [XPHB] condition until the end of its next turn. The sarrukh can't take this action again until the start of its next turn.

info.text:
Wicked Serpentine Oppressors

Powerful and magical, sarrukhs once commanded a wicked empire that spanned Faerûn, but it fell tens of thousands of years ago. In the millennia that followed, the many species sarrukhs created drove them nearly to extinction. Only a small number of sarrukhs remain in isolated enclaves, including a small community beneath the Citadel at the heart of Thaymount.

Sarrukhs have snakelike lower bodies and heads but torsos that resemble those of humanoids. Their gleaming eyes are alight with inner fire. Sarrukhs can live for up to a millennium, and most expect to see their empire rise again.

Sarrukh Tyrant.

Most remaining sarrukhs are tyrants who fervently believe the sarrukh empire's resurgence is inevitable. Tyrants live in clans with other sarrukhs, roaming ruins and subjugating creatures that live nearby. They command only a small portion of the magical power their former empire's leaders held.

Arisen Sarrukh.

The most powerful sarrukhs are arisen: horrific creatures that have subverted death. While arisen sarrukhs have lost their ability to cast spells, their unliving flesh is unnaturally strong.

images.title: An arisen sarrukh commands two sarrukh tyrants.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (4/Day, or 5/Day in Lair)
entries.description: If Szass Tam fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Spirit Jar
entries.description: If destroyed, Szass Tam re-forms in 1d10 days if he has a spirit jar, reviving with all his Hit Points [XPHB]. The new body appears in an unoccupied space within Szass Tam's lair.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Szass Tam makes three attacks, using Paralyzing Touch or Soul-Draining Ray in any combination. He can replace two attacks with a use of Spellcasting to cast Finger of Death [XPHB].

entries.name: Paralyzing Touch
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +13, reach 5 ft. Hit: 16 (3d6 + 6) Cold damage, and the target has the Paralyzed [XPHB] condition until the start of Szass Tam's next turn.

entries.name: Soul-Draining Ray
entries.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +13, range 120 ft. Hit: 25 (3d12 + 6) Necrotic damage, and the target has Disadvantage [XPHB] on attack rolls and saving throws until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Szass Tam casts one of the following spells, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 21, +13 to hit with spell attacks):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: Detect Magic [XPHB], Detect Thoughts [XPHB], Finger of Death [XPHB], Fireball [XPHB] (level 8 version), Lightning Bolt [XPHB] (level 8 version), Mage Hand [XPHB], Prestidigitation [XPHB]

2/day each: Animate Dead [XPHB], Dimension Door [XPHB], Plane Shift [XPHB]

1/day each: Power Word Kill [XPHB], Project Image [XPHB], Scrying [XPHB], Sending [XPHB]

entries.name: Deathly Teleport
entries.description: Szass Tam teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space he can see, and each creature within 10 feet of the space he left takes 13 (3d8) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Disrupt Life
entries.description: CON Saving Throw: 21, each creature that isn't an Undead in a 20-foot Emanation [XPHB] originating from Szass Tam. Failure: 14 (4d6) Necrotic damage and the creature's Hit Point [XPHB] maximum decreases by an amount equal to the damage taken. Success: Half damage only. Success or Failure: Szass Tam can't take this action again until the start of his next turn.

entries.name: Withering Magic
entries.description:
Szass Tam casts Blight [XPHB] or Dispel Magic [XPHB], using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

Spellcasting ability: INT.

legendary: 1: Blight [XPHB]

Dispel Magic [XPHB]

sections.title: Regional Effects
sections.description:
Szass Tam extends his presence into the region he inhabits, creating the following effects:

• Soul Siphon.

Whenever a Humanoid dies within the lair, its soul is immediately consumed by Szass Tam. A Humanoid whose soul is consumed in this way can be brought back to life only by a True Resurrection [XPHB] or Wish [XPHB] spell.
• Whispers of Necromancy.

Whenever a creature within 1 mile of the lair casts a Necromancy spell, Szass Tam knows the spell and the identity of the creature that cast it.

If Szass Tam is destroyed or moves his lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately. These effects resume if Szass Tam gains a new body (see his Spirit Jar trait).

entries.name: Protective Magic
entries.description:
Szass Tam casts Counterspell [XPHB] or Shield [XPHB] in response to the spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: Counterspell [XPHB], Shield [XPHB]

info.text:
Once the undisputed regent of Thay, Szass Tam is an old and powerful lich who plots to regain control over the nation. Although he still wields great power as the zulkir of necromancy and the tharchion of Thaymount (see chapter 1), Szass Tam believes it's his destiny to rule Thay and use its living people as fodder for his undead armies.

History.

An eloquent and inventive wizard, Szass Tam rose through the ranks of the Red Wizards to become the zulkir of necromancy more than three centuries ago and became a lich not long afterward.

Regency.

Over a century ago, Szass Tam turned against the other zulkirs and claimed rulership over Thay. On winning the ensuing civil war, he declared himself regent and turned his rivals into undead servants. Under his rule, necromancers dominated Thay, and all paid fealty to him.

Pursuit of Godhood.

Eventually Szass Tam craved more than ruling Thay. Obsessed with gaining more power, he began a ritual to ascend to godhood. When this ritual failed spectacularly a few decades ago, civil unrest in Thay prompted him to reestablish the zulkir council with members loyal to him. He relinquished his title of regent, though in reality, the new zulkirs reported to him. These zulkirs dealt with the details of government, leaving him free to pursue new approaches to attaining godhood.

While Szass Tam remained distracted with finding a different way to attain godhood, new rivals systematically overthrew his sycophant zulkirs. Suddenly he was again part of a zulkir council with Red Wizards who saw themselves as his equals and refused to bow to him as the nation's ruler.

Returning Tyrant.

While Szass Tam still aspires to godhood, he can't bear the loss of political power to rivals he views as inferiors. After years of plotting, he again moves to subdue Thay with undead before crushing the zulkirs who oppose him. If successful, he'll return Thay to the undead-dominated land it was under his rule.

Personality.

Szass Tam takes the long view in his many plots, some of which span lifetimes. He is quick to pivot to contingencies when necessary.

While he enjoys commanding fear in his Thayan subjects, he also wields diplomacy to maintain foreign allies and is skilled at keeping foes off balance. Those who cross Szass Tam might evoke one of his legendary rages or might earn a nod of appreciation, as of someone witnessing a clever move in a game of strategy.

Szass Tam's Lair.

Szass Tam's lair is the Citadel, a fortress in the mountainous region of Thaymount. Here he plans his evil schemes and issues commands to his underlings.

Regional Effects.

Szass Tam extends his presence into the region he inhabits, creating the following effects:

• Soul Siphon.

Whenever a Humanoid dies within the lair, its soul is immediately consumed by Szass Tam. A Humanoid whose soul is consumed in this way can be brought back to life only by a True Resurrection [XPHB] or Wish [XPHB] spell.
• Whispers of Necromancy.

Whenever a creature within 1 mile of the lair casts a Necromancy spell, Szass Tam knows the spell and the identity of the creature that cast it.

If Szass Tam is destroyed or moves his lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately. These effects resume if Szass Tam gains a new body (see his Spirit Jar trait).

entries.name: Evocation Sculptor
entries.description: When Thrul casts a spell that creates an area of effect, she can choose herself and up to five other creatures she can see, sculpting the spell's energy around them. A chosen creature automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the spell, and it takes no damage if it would normally take half damage on a successful save.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: Thrul has Advantage [XPHB] on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Thrul makes four Arcane Burst attacks. She can replace two attacks with a use of Spellcasting to cast Fireball [XPHB] (level 5 version) or Lightning Bolt [XPHB] (level 5 version).

entries.name: Arcane Burst
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +11, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit: 32 (5d10 + 5) Force damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Thrul casts one of the following spells, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 19):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: Alter Self [XPHB], Detect Magic [XPHB], Fireball [XPHB] (level 5 version), Illusory Script [XPHB], Lightning Bolt [XPHB] (level 5 version), Mage Armor [XPHB] (included in AC), Mage Hand [XPHB], Prestidigitation [XPHB]

2/day each: Demiplane [XPHB], Modify Memory [XPHB], Scrying [XPHB], Sending [XPHB], Teleport [XPHB]

1/day each: Chain Lightning [XPHB], Sunburst [XPHB]

entries.name: Protective Magic (3/Day)
entries.description:
Thrul casts Counterspell [XPHB] or Shield [XPHB] in response to the spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

Spellcasting ability: INT.

3/day: Counterspell [XPHB], Shield [XPHB]

info.text:
Xelnene Thrul is the zulkir of evocation. With the exception of Szass Tam, she is the most powerful mage on the Council of Zulkirs. She hates tyranny and wants Szass Tam destroyed. To her, the only good tyrant is a dead one.

History.

Xelnene Thrul is the scion of a powerful family. Her ancestor, Aznar Thrul, was zulkir of evocation a century ago. He murdered countless Thayans and conscripted vast armies in failed attempts to conquer Rashemen. Xelnene hates Aznar's deeds but trades on her family's fearsome reputation when needed.

As a youth, Thrul was apprenticed to a Red Wizard named Sabeine who cultivated Thrul's sense of justice and encouraged Thrul to foster goodness among the Red Wizards. Szass Tam later executed Sabeine for treason. Ever since, Thrul has kept her desire for reform secret.

Personality.

Thrul is shrewd and pragmatic. She exudes physical, political, and magical might but avoids showing emotion lest her enemies find her weak. She commands a network of spies, allies, and political operatives who advance her goal of creating a better future for Thay's populace.

entries.name: Invisible in Water
entries.description: The big water slurpent is invisible while fully immersed in water.

entries.name: Water Bound
entries.description: The big water slurpent dies if it leaves the water to which it is bound or if that water is destroyed.

entries.name: Constrict
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, one target. Hit: 13 (3d6+3) bludgeoning damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, it is grappled (escape 13) and pulled 5 feet toward the big water slurpent. Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, the big water slurpent tries to drown it, and the big water slurpent can't constrict another target.

info.text:
The Big Water Slurpent is a magical creature that has lived within the Big Water for centuries. It was created by a wizard to guard the tower that has long since sunk into the Big Water. Many goblins have seen the slurpent and have run away. Many goblins believe that it likes to eat goblins.

The Big Water Slurpent is dangerous if goblins go snooping around the Big Water. But there are ways to get around it if you do one of the following:

• Sing it a song (gotta really sing your goblin heart out!)
• Feed it some tasty goblin pie (it better be a good one!)
• Hold up a mirror and show it its reflection (it is a lonely slurpent)

entries.name: Pack Tactics
entries.description: Birdsquirrel has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the Birdsquirrel's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Birdsquirrel makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its claws.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6+2) piercing damage.

entries.name: Claws
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4+2) slashing damage.

info.text: Birdsquirrel is a plucky, little critter who loves Muk with all its heart. Some say that Birdsquirrel was created by Doonwaggle the wizard, and that it is the only birdsquirrel in the Dankwood (and maybe the whole world) but who knows?

images.title: Birdsquirrel can't read so good... can you please help?

entries.name: Pack Tactics
entries.description: The Boontu monkey has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the boontu monkey's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +1 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1 (1d4 - 1) piercing damage.

info.text:
Boontu monkeys are skittish and furtive creatures that are greedy and are always on the lookout for food. Although they are greedy, they never eat the sacred golden nuts from the boontu tree in which they live.

Some say that they were once greedy thieves that were turned to monkeys by a powerful dryad who caught them stealing the nuts from her sacred tree.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.description: The merfolk can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Siren Song
entries.description: Lovely singing voices charm every humanoid or giant within 300 feet. The targets must succeed on a 11 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed until the song ends.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, one target. Hit: 3 (1d6) piercing damage.

info.text:
The Crystal Cave merfolk have long, flowing fins and silvery scales. They have lovely, melodic voices that are enhanced by the vibrating crystals of the cave in which they dwell.

They love anything silver and are willing to trade pearls and bits of gold treasure that they have found on their hunts under the waters. They also have magical potions that can help a surface dweller breathe underwater.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.description: The hag can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Mimicry (Green Hag)
entries.description: The hag can mimic animal sounds and humanoid voices. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful 14 Wisdom (Insight) check.

entries.name: Innate Spellcasting
entries.description:
The hag's spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save 12). It can innately cast the following spells:

At will: dancing lights, minor illusion, vicious mockery

entries.name: Illusory Appearance
entries.description: The hag covers herself with a magical illusion that allows her to look like another creature of her general size and shape. The illusion ends when the hag chooses, or if she dies. A 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check will expose the hag's disguise.

entries.name: Invisible Passage
entries.description: The hag magically turns invisible until she attacks or casts a spell, or until her concentration ends. While invisible, she leaves no physical evidence of her passage, and can only be tracked by magic.

entries.name: Claws
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, one target. Hit: 17 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage.

info.text:
Dankwood hags are the worst kind of hags in the world. They are creepy and grumpy with long fingers that end in iron claws. They are known to eat small goblins and other warm-blooded creatures, but Dankwood hags are especially fond of sparkleberry tarts.

Since sparkleberries grow only where dryads have their sacred groves, Dankwood hags don't dare enter lest they anger the dryads and suffer their wrath. Dankwood hags are also very greedy and this can be used against them to lure them into a trap or trick them into eating something they shouldn't.

entries.name: Nimble Escape
entries.description: The goblin can take the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action on each of its turns.

entries.name: Catch me if you can!
entries.description: Dum-Dum Goblins will opt to run and hide before fighting! A 15 Dexterity check must be made before they can be attacked.

entries.name: Scimitar
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, one target. Hit: 3 (1d6 +2) slashing damage.

entries.name: Shortbow
entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

info.text: Dum Dum goblins are your average run-of-the-mill goblins that live in the Dankwood. They are led by their chief, Grobble, who loves to eat mushroom pie and send out his gang of goblin thieves to steal stuff. He loves to be flattered and thinks he's the toughest goblin in the Dankwood.

entries.name: Dwarven Resilience
entries.description: They have advantage on saving throws against poison, and they have resistance to poison damage.

entries.name: Shortbow
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) slashing damage.

info.text:
Although there are no dwarves that live in the actual Dankwood, they will sometime pass through in travel or explore the forest for coveted materials and magical stones. They pride themselves in their skills and can create beautiful artifacts from the objects they find in nature.

The dwarves in the area are naturally cautious towards goblins. They will go out of their way to avoid contact and rarely stay for long periods in the Dankwood.

entries.name: Tunneler
entries.description: The worm can burrow through solid rock at half its burrow speed and leaves a 10-foot-diameter tunnel in its wake.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The worm makes two attacks:

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, one target. Hit: 22 (3d8) piercing damage. Target must make a 19 Dexterity save, or be swallowed by the worm!

entries.name: Tail Stinger
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, one creature. Hit: 19 (3d6 + 9) piercing damage Target must make a 19 Constitution save, or take 42 (12d6) poison damage.

info.text:
Great Kroom is a purple worm that comes to the Dankwood every twenty years to feed on all kinds of stuff that grows under the forest.

The Great Kroom is a terrifying and dangerous monster that could easily destroy Gob-Town but there are ways to stop it:

• You need to find a tickling stick. This magical stick can be used on a purple worm to tickle it into a docile state. Then it can be led away from the Dankwood.
• You need to have it eat a rare mushroom called a Punderpuff. This mushroom grows deep in the Dankwood and has a powerful chemical that can put a purple worm to sleep.

entries.name: Limited Telepathy
entries.description: The otyugh can magically transmit simple messages and images to any creature within 120 feet of it that can understand a language. This form of telepathy doesn't allow the receiving creature to telepathically respond.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The otyugh makes three attacks:

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) piercing damage. Target must make a 15 Constitution save, or take 6 (1d10) poison damage until cured.

entries.name: Tentacle
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage. Target must make a 19 Constitution save, or take 42 (12d6) poison damage.

entries.name: Slam!
entries.description: Target must make a 14 Constitution save, or be grappled.

info.text:
Otyughs are really stinky and ugly monsters that dine on offal, garbage, and dung. They are generally grumpy and aggressive. Most people don't like otyughs at all.

This otyugh can be dealt with in a few ways:

• You can get it to dance by playing music and dancing. Who knew that otyughs liked to dance? It will follow you anywhere now.
• If you feed an otyugh a magical pie made with the nectar of a fairy fob lily, mixed with spit nettles, and gobnobs, it will be your best friend. (But it will still be stinky.)
• Otyughs are scared of vampires. If you dress up as one, you might be able to scare it away. You better do a good job of scaring it!

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The giant makes two greatclub attacks.

entries.name: Greatclub
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, one target. Hit: 18 (3d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Rock
entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, one target. Hit: 21 (3d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage.

info.text:
The hill giant, Blorbo, is an ill-tempered brute who has a taste for goblin flesh. Goblins tell their children horror stories of Blorbo around the campfire at night to keep them from wandering too far into the Dankwood.

Blorbo is not aware that there is a shiny stone and a lost dwarven king deep within his cave but he's not interested in those things. He wants to eat stuff.

Blorbo is too powerful to defeat in combat but he can be tricked with food. Poison from a pooka toad on a well-aimed arrow might do the trick, but you better be a good shot!

entries.name: Magic Weapons
entries.description: The couatl's weapon attacks are magical.

entries.name: Shielded Mind
entries.description: The couatl is immune to scrying and to any effect that would sense its emotions, read its thoughts, or detect its location.

entries.name: Innate Spellcasting
entries.description:
The couatl's spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save 14). It can innately cast the following spells, requiring only verbal components:

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

At will: detect evil and good, detect magic, detect thoughts

3/day each: bless, create food and water, cure wounds, lesser restoration, protection from poison, sanctuary, shield

1/day each: dream, greater restoration, scrying

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 8 (1d6 + 5) piercing damage. Target must make a 13 Constitution save, or fall unconscious. Another creature can use an action to shake the target awake.

entries.name: Constrict
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one Medium or smaller creature. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage. Target is grappled (escape 15). The couatl can constrain only one target at a time.

entries.name: Change Shape
entries.description:
The couatl magically polymorphs into a humanoid or beast that has a challenge rating equal to or less than its own, or back into its true form. It reverts to its true form if it dies. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying is absorbed or borne by the new form (the couatl's choice).

In a new form, the couatl retains its game statistics and ability to speak, but its AC, movement modes, Strength, Dexterity, and other actions are replaced by those of the new form, and it gains any statistics and capabilities (except class features, legendary actions, and lair actions) that the new form has but that it lacks. If the new form has a bite attack, the couatl can use its bite in that form.

info.text: Saleeth is a wise and beautiful couatl that is very kind to polite and well-mannered goblins. If she is approached by adventurers, she may have a noble quest for them to undertake if they are ready to help her defend the world against the forces of evil.

entries.name: Spider Climb
entries.description: The aartuk can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The aartuk makes two Branch attacks, two Radiant Pellet attacks, or one of each.

entries.name: Branch
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Radiant Pellet
entries.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +4 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (4d4) radiant damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting (Psionics)
entries.description:
The aartuk casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save 12):

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

1/day each: calm emotions, detect magic, sending

entries.name: Tongue Recharge 6
entries.description: The aartuk tries to use its gooey tongue to snare one Large or smaller creature it can see within 30 feet of itself. The target must make a 12 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the target is grappled by the tongue (escape 14) and pulled up to 25 feet toward the aartuk. The tongue can grapple one creature at a time.

info.text:
Aartuks are intelligent plant creatures that live to wage war. Beholders destroyed their original home world and scattered the survivors across the Material Plane. These survivors formed small nomadic cells.

Aartuk cells can be found throughout Wildspace, including aboard spelljamming ships whose former crews were either murdered or forcibly ejected by a band of aartuks.

An aartuk's body is shaped like a five-pointed star and is covered with thick, flexible bark. The tips of its branch-like extremities end in suction cups that allow the creature to climb on vertical surfaces and along ceilings. Each suction cup houses three retractable pseudopods that are used to manipulate small objects.

The head of an aartuk surmounts a 6-foot-tall stalk that can be extruded from the center of the star. The head contains the aartuk's sensory organs, including a long tongue that the creature uses as a weapon.

sections.title: Regional Effects
sections.description:
The region containing an ancient or adult lunar dragon's lair is warped by the dragon's magic, which produces one or more of the following effects:

• Black Frost.

A thin layer of black frost covers the ground, which kills all ordinary plants growing within 6 miles of the lair if the dragon is ancient, or within 3 miles if the dragon is an adult.
• Haunting Moan.

A haunting sound gets louder or fainter (dragon's choice) the closer one gets to the lair. The moan is audible 6 miles from the lair if the dragon is ancient, or 3 miles if the dragon is an adult.
• Moon Devils.

Swirling funnels of dust and frost known as moon devils crisscross the area within 1 mile of the lair, intercepting other creatures they encounter. A moon devil is a free-willed air elemental that deals cold damage instead of bludgeoning damage.

If the dragon dies, the moaning stops, the moon devils dissipate, and the black frost disappears over the course of 1d10 days, allowing plant life in the area to recover.

info.text:
A Lunar Dragon's Lair.

The cave complex where a lunar dragon makes its lair contains ample space for food, as well as one or more hidden chambers where the dragon keeps its treasure. Depending on the composition and features of the moon, the lair might contain natural springs and heat vents, wild gardens, crystal formations, magical phenomena, or an ecosystem of lesser life forms that have adapted to living with the dragon.

Lunar dragons (also known as moon dragons or phase dragons) are capricious, xenophobic creatures that make their lairs inside desolate moons by burrowing through the rock.

Before laying eggs, a female lunar dragon stocks her lair with food; she won't leave the lair again until the eggs hatch and the offspring are old enough to fend for themselves. Lunar dragon eggs have stony shells that are pale white to light gray in color. Lunar dragons are alabaster white when they hatch and gradually turn darker as they age. Ancient moon dragons are the color of slate.

Lunar dragons enjoy depriving other creatures of treasure more than acquiring the treasure themselves. Often found among the treasures in a lunar dragon's hoard are one or more spelljamming helms (see the Astral Adventurer's Guide) taken from vessels that dared to invade the dragon's territory.

A lunar dragon can become incorporeal, but not to the extent that it can pass through other creatures or solid objects. In this semi-incorporeal state, roughly half of the dragon's body has a dark, indistinctly spectral form.

A solar dragon customarily lairs in a star's radiant core or nests in a gigantic, hollowed-out rock engulfed by the star's blinding radiance. A star in which a solar dragon makes its lair has the following effects on creatures:

• Blinding Radiance..

A creature that is within 10 miles of the star or inside it is blinded by its intense light unless the creature has protective gear to shield its eyes, such as goggles of night or a similar form of eyewear.
• Stellar Incineration..

Any creature that enters the star or starts its turn inside it takes 132 (24d10) radiant damage.

info.text:
A solar dragon (also known as a radiant dragon or a sun dragon) is born in the heart of a star. It divides its time outside its lair between patrolling its territory and hunting for food. The dragon has a serpentine body, a pair of ventral limbs ending in long fins, nebulous wings that give off light, and gleaming, multicolored scales. It can see clearly even in blindingly bright light.

Solar dragons are fond of treasure just as all dragons are, but in the airless void of Wildspace, they value food even more. Solar dragons typically feed on kindori, scavvers, and other forms of space-dwelling wildlife. A solar dragon might mistake a distant spelljamming ship for possible prey and come within range of the vessel's weapons before realizing its error and veering away. A wise or experienced captain won't take the dragon's approach as a sign of hostility. Solar dragons that are fired upon have been known to batter the offending ships to flinders.

Solar dragons are territorial carnivores, and they behave accordingly. A young solar dragon might lay claim to an asteroid belt, where food is relatively plentiful, while an ancient solar dragon might consider an entire Wildspace system its hunting ground. They tend to give a wide berth to Humanoid folk, whom they find violent and tiresome. Trespassers who are detected in a solar dragon's lair can expect to be met with resistance, followed by hostility, especially if the lair contains eggs.

A solar dragon egg has an obsidian shell, shiny black and opaque. When an egg is close to hatching, the shell becomes translucent, allowing the light from the unborn wyrmling's wings to shine through.

info.text:
An astral elf aristocrat is a brilliant, highborn leader gifted with magical abilities, including the power to channel sunlight and summon a solar dragon.

Astral Elves.

Long ago, some elves ventured to the Astral Plane to be closer to their gods. There, they ceased to age and could exist indefinitely without sustenance.

Astral elves were among the first creatures to dwell in the Silver Void. As other explorers have reached for the stars, astral elves have had to reckon with violent neighbors and strange visitors. Over the eons, astral elves have clashed with numerous invaders, including psurlons, mind flayers, and githyanki. When dealing with others, astral elves customarily cover their faces with ornate visors, becoming faceless extensions of their gods. Their fierce devotion to the pantheon of elven deities is repaid with divine power. For example, the gods invest astral elf warriors with the power to channel the radiant energy of starlight through their weapons, just as they empower astral elf leaders with the ability to cast spells and summon solar dragons.

Astral elves ply the Astral Sea and Wildspace in ships of their own design. These ships are fashioned from crystals harvested from Wildspace systems and bound together with an organic, plant-based material that hardens like ceramic. The elves sculpt these substances in various configurations to create star moths (see the Astral Adventurer's Guide) and other vessels. The elves also reshape the petrified bodies of dead gods found adrift in the Silver Void, transforming them into floating cities and citadels.

Although the Silver Void is their home, astral elves often venture into Wildspace systems and place their ships and citadels in orbit around stars. Astral elves do this for several reasons. Proximity to a star allows the astral elves to forge pacts with solar dragons and to collect starlight, which the elves use to grow crystals and repair their ships. Most important, astral elves use their time outside the Deep Astral to replenish their numbers by having and raising children.

Many astral elves are thousands (in some cases tens of thousands) of years old. Whatever their disposition, their longevity gives astral elves a perspective on time that few other kinds of creatures can appreciate. Whether they choose to live in quiet contemplation or strike out to explore the far reaches of the multiverse, astral elves tend to see events happening elsewhere as having little or no meaning to them.

Astral Elves of Xaryxis.

The adventure, Light of Xaryxisfeatures an amoral astral elf society called the Xaryxian Empire. This empire is based in Xaryxispace, a Wildspace system illuminated by an enormous radiant sun named Xaryxis.

Over the eons, astral elves have clashed with numerous invaders, including psurlons, mind flayers, and githyanki. When dealing with others, astral elves customarily cover their faces with ornate visors, becoming faceless extensions of their gods. Their fierce devotion to the pantheon of elven deities is repaid with divine power. For example, the gods invest astral elf warriors with the power to channel the radiant energy of starlight through their weapons, just as they empower astral elf leaders with the ability to cast spells and summon solar dragons.

Astral elves ply the Astral Sea and Wildspace in ships of their own design. These ships are fashioned from crystals harvested from Wildspace systems and bound together with an organic, plant-based material that hardens like ceramic. The elves sculpt these substances in various configurations to create star moths (see the Astral Adventurer's Guide) and other vessels. The elves also reshape the petrified bodies of dead gods found adrift in the Silver Void, transforming them into floating cities and citadels.

Although the Silver Void is their home, astral elves often venture into Wildspace systems and place their ships and citadels in orbit around stars. Astral elves do this for several reasons. Proximity to a star allows the astral elves to forge pacts with solar dragons and to collect starlight, which the elves use to grow crystals and repair their ships. Most important, astral elves use their time outside the Deep Astral to replenish their numbers by having and raising children.

Many astral elves are thousands (in some cases tens of thousands) of years old. Whatever their disposition, their longevity gives astral elves a perspective on time that few other kinds of creatures can appreciate. Whether they choose to live in quiet contemplation or strike out to explore the far reaches of the multiverse, astral elves tend to see events happening elsewhere as having little or no meaning to them.

Astral Elves of Xaryxis.

The adventure, Light of Xaryxisfeatures an amoral astral elf society called the Xaryxian Empire. This empire is based in Xaryxispace, a Wildspace system illuminated by an enormous radiant sun named Xaryxis.

entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d8 + 2) slashing damage, or 13 (2d10 + 2) slashing damage when used with two hands, plus 10 (3d6) radiant damage.

entries.name: Radiant Ray
entries.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +6 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (4d10) radiant damage.

info.text:
The safety of important individuals and locations is entrusted to astral elf honor guards, highly trained warriors who are more than capable of holding their own in combat.

entries.name: Rain of Radiance

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The elf casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save 16):

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

2/day each: cure wounds (8th-level version), hold person

1/day each: divination, sending, word of recall

entries.name: Starlight Step (2/Day)
entries.description: The elf magically teleports up to 30 feet, along with anything it is wearing or carrying, to an unoccupied space it can see.

info.text:
Star priests draw their strength from the pantheon of elven gods and oversee religious practices in astral elf society. It's common for them to serve aboard spelljamming ships, not only as emissaries of the gods but also as spelljammers.

entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) radiant damage.

Astral elf warriors operate elven spelljamming ships and defend elven strongholds throughout the Astral Plane.
