entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The soldier makes two longsword attacks or two longbow attacks. It can use its Life Drain in place of one longsword attack.

entries.name: Life Drain
entries.description:
Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) necrotic damage. The target must succeed on a 13 Constitution saving throw or its hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0.

A humanoid slain by this attack rises 24 hours later as a zombie under the soldier's control, unless the humanoid is restored to life or its body is destroyed. The soldier can have no more than twelve zombies under its control at one time.

entries.name: Longsword
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) slashing damage, or 7 (1d10 + 2) slashing damage if used with two hands.

entries.name: Longbow
entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

info.source: Dragonlance: Shadow of the Dragon Queen, page 96

entries.name: Death Throes
entries.description: When Virruza is reduced to 0 hit points, he turns into a puddle of acid and splashes acid on those around him. Each creature within 5 feet of him must succeed on a 12 Dexterity saving throw or be covered in acid for 1 minute. A creature can use its action to scrape or wash the acid off itself or another creature. A creature covered in the acid takes 7 (2d6) acid damage at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: Virruza has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Regeneration
entries.description: Virruza regains 10 hit points at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 hit point.

entries.name: Innate Spellcasting
entries.description:
Virruza's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save 12). Virruza can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

At will: detect magic, detect thoughts, mage hand

1/day: fireball

2/day each: fear, invisibility (self only)

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Virruza makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws or staff. Alternatively, it uses its Hurl Flame twice.

entries.name: Bite (Slaad Form Only)
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage.

entries.name: Claw (Slaad Form Only)
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage.

entries.name: Staff
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Hurl Flame
entries.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +4 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (3d6) fire damage. The fire ignites flammable objects that aren't being worn or carried.

info.text: Changed by days of strange experiments involving draconian blood and exposure to the Spawning Shard, Virruza now looks like a tumescent draconian with warty green skin and an overly large mouth.
info.source: Dragonlance: Shadow of the Dragon Queen, page 119

entries.name: Flyby
entries.description: The dragonnel doesn't provoke opportunity attacks when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The dragonnel makes two Rend attacks.

entries.name: Rend
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage.

entries.name: Acid Spit
entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (5d6 + 3) acid damage.

info.text:
The Northern Wastes of Ansalon are home to wasteland dragonnels, draconic creatures closely related to copper dragons. Wasteland dragonnels are lithe and quick, with scales the color of dull copper. These playful creatures defend their territory by flying out of a foe's reach and spitting potent acid, in an approximation of their copper dragon relatives.

Dragonnels.

Dragonnels are distantly related to chromatic and metallic dragons and resemble them in basic form. Intelligent enough to understand speech but incapable of speaking themselves, they are willful creatures largely motivated by the desire for food.
info.source: Dragonlance: Shadow of the Dragon Queen, page 201

entries.name: Undead Fortitude
entries.description: If damage reduces Wersten to 0 hit points, she must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is bludgeoning or from a critical hit. On a success, Wersten drops to 1 hit point instead.

entries.name: Unusual Nature
entries.description: Wersten doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Wersten makes three Banner Pike attacks and uses Terrifying Litany if it's available.

entries.name: Banner Pike
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (1d10 + 5) piercing damage plus 13 (3d8) necrotic damage. If the target is a Humanoid, it must succeed on a 16 Charisma saving throw or be cursed. The curse lasts until it is lifted by remove curse or similar magic. Black, thorny rose stems sprout from the creature's body while it is cursed, imposing disadvantage on the creature's ability checks and attack rolls and halving its speed. A creature that succeeds on the saving throw against the curse is immune to it for 24 hours.

entries.name: Terrifying Litany Recharge 5–6
entries.description: Wersten recites names of souls slain by Soth and his company, channeling their mortal terror. Each creature that isn't an Undead within 30 feet of her must make a 16 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 22 (4d10) psychic damage and is frightened of Wersten for 1 minute. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't frightened. At the end of each of its turns, a frightened creature can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Wersten casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save 16):

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

1/day each: dispel magic, wall of stone

info.text: Wersten Kern is Lord Soth's standard bearer and champion. As with many of Soth's knights, she died alongside her liege during the Cataclysm and was cursed with undeath. In battle, she wields a wicked pike that flies Soth's black rose standard, and her cries can stop mighty warriors' hearts. Wersten staunchly follows Soth's commands, and she will serve him until she faces a second doom.
info.source: Dragonlance: Shadow of the Dragon Queen, page 209

entries.name: Dagger
entries.description: Melee Weapon or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Wyhan is a 9th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). Wyhan has the following wizard spells prepared:

Spellcasting ability: INT.

Cantrips (at will): fire bolt, light, mage hand, prestidigitation

Level 1 (4 slots): detect magic, mage armor, magic missile, shield

Level 2 (3 slots): misty step, suggestion

Level 3 (3 slots): counterspell, fireball, fly

Level 4 (3 slots): greater invisibility, ice storm

Level 5 (1 slots): cone of cold

info.source: Dragonlance: Shadow of the Dragon Queen, page 79

entries.name: Hustle
entries.description: The smuggler can move through the space of any creature that is of a larger size, but it can't stop there.

entries.name: Shortsword
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) Poison damage.

entries.name: Pistol
entries.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 30/90 ft. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) Piercing damage.

info.text: Smugglers employed by the Boromar Clan (mostly halflings) are notoriously hard to catch. These speedy criminals traffic everything from narcotics to illegal arcane weaponry across Sharn.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 57

entries.name: Hustle
entries.description: The underboss can move through the space of any creature that is of a larger size, but it can't stop there.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The underboss makes three attacks, using Poisoned Blade or Arcane Firearm in any combination.

entries.name: Poisoned Blade
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned [XPHB] condition until the start of the underboss's next turn. If the target is already Poisoned [XPHB], it instead takes an extra 7 (2d6) Poison damage.

entries.name: Arcane Firearm
entries.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +7, range 30/90 ft. Hit: 26 (4d10 + 4) Force damage.

entries.name: Uncanny Dodge
entries.description: Trigger: The underboss is hit by an attack roll. Response: The underboss halves the damage (round down) it takes from that attack.

info.text: Underbosses supervise larger clan operations, such as gambling halls and warehouses of smuggled goods awaiting transport. Accustomed to the criminal lifestyle, these hardy individuals (mostly halflings) dismiss and dispose of threats with calculated ease.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 57

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The artificer makes two attacks, using Battering Mace or Artillery Strike in any combination.

entries.name: Battering Mace
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage, and if the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone [XPHB] condition.

entries.name: Artillery Strike
entries.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +6, range 120 ft. Hit: 22 (4d8 + 4) Force damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The artificer casts one of the following spells, using its Tinker's Tools as an Arcane Focus and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 14):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: Burning Hands [XPHB] (level 3 version), Mending [XPHB], Thunderwave [XPHB] (level 3 version)

1/day each: Cure Wounds [XPHB], Invisibility [XPHB]

info.text: Dragonmarked artificers of House Cannith (typically human) often wield compact devices similar to eldritch cannons that can produce a variety of devastating effects. Both these cannons and the artificers' force-empowered maces function only in their creator's hands.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 80

entries.name: Blood Frenzy
entries.description: The bruiser has Advantage [XPHB] on attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all its Hit Points [XPHB].

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The bruiser makes three Pummel attacks and uses Glare.

entries.name: Pummel
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Glare
entries.description: WIS Saving Throw: 14, one creature the bruiser can see within 30 feet. Failure: The target has the Frightened [XPHB] condition until the start of the bruiser's next turn.

entries.name: Smackback
entries.description: Trigger: The bruiser takes damage from a creature within 5 feet. Response: The bruiser makes one Pummel attack, targeting the triggering creature.

info.text: Intimidating and powerful, bruisers lead Daask operations when more violent and decisive shows of force are needed. These enforcers relish the brutality of their work.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 58

entries.name: Pack Tactics
entries.description: The raider has Advantage [XPHB] on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the raider's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated [XPHB] condition.

entries.name: Pummel
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Smackback
entries.description: Trigger: The raider takes damage from a creature within 5 feet. Response: The raider makes one Pummel attack, targeting the triggering creature.

info.text: Raiders use guerrilla tactics to ambush warehouses and beat down opponents. These skilled fistfighters work in tandem to claim goods and territory for Daask.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 58

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The infiltrator makes three Mind Blade attacks.

entries.name: Mind Blade
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. or range 30 ft. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) Psychic damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The infiltrator casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 15):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

1/day: Synaptic Static [XPHB]

3/day: Detect Thoughts [XPHB]

entries.name: Mind Curse
entries.description: WIS Saving Throw: 15, one creature hit by the infiltrator's Mind Blade attack this turn. Failure: The target takes 14 (4d6) Psychic damage and is cursed. While cursed in this way, it has Disadvantage [XPHB] on attack rolls against the infiltrator, and the infiltrator always knows its location while it and the infiltrator are on the same plane of existence. A cursed creature repeats the save whenever it finishes a Short [XPHB] or Long Rest [XPHB], ending the effect on itself on a success. Success: Half damage only.

info.text: Dreaming Dark Infiltrators are spies sent to gather intelligence. They plant psychic seeds in their minds of their foes that enhance the infiltrators' combat prowess against those enemies.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 59

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The mindkiller makes two Nightmare Whisper attacks.

entries.name: Nightmare Whisper
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. or range 30 ft. Hit: 27 (5d8 + 5) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened [XPHB] condition until the start of the mindkiller's next turn. If the target is already Frightened [XPHB], it instead takes an extra 10 (3d6) Psychic damage.

entries.name: Primal Fear (1/Day)
entries.description: WIS Saving Throw: 17, each creature in a 30-foot-radius Sphere [XPHB] centered on a point the mindkiller can see within 120 feet. Failure: 35 (10d6) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened [XPHB] condition until the start of the mindkiller's next turn. While Frightened [XPHB] in this way, the target can do only one of the following on each of its turns: move, take an action, or take a Bonus Action [XPHB]. Success: Half damage only.

entries.name: Slayer's Puppet (1/Day)
entries.description:
The mindkiller casts Dominate Person [XPHB], requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 17).

Spellcasting ability: INT.

1/day: Dominate Person [XPHB]

info.text: Mindkillers are the assassins of the Dreaming Dark, sent to terrify their foes before striking to kill. Mindkillers force foes to attack their own allies, causing physical and emotional devastation to grow the power of the Dreaming Dark.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 60

entries.name: Aura of Authority
entries.description: While in a 30-foot Emanation [XPHB] originating from the commander, the commander and its allies have Advantage [XPHB] on attack rolls and saving throws, provided the commander doesn't have the Incapacitated [XPHB] condition.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The commander makes two attacks, using Flail or Javelin in any combination.

entries.name: Flail
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage—plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage if the commander is Bloodied—and the target has Disadvantage [XPHB] on its next attack roll before the start of the commander's next turn.

entries.name: Javelin
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Piercing damage—plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage if the commander is Bloodied [XPHB].

info.text: Emerald Claw commanders lead large groups of soldiers, inspiring the fanatical devotion of Humanoids and Undead alike.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 90

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The knight makes two attacks, using Flail or Javelin in any combination.

entries.name: Flail
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage—plus 4 (1d8) Necrotic damage if the knight is Bloodied—and the target has Disadvantage [XPHB] on its next attack roll before the start of the knight's next turn.

entries.name: Javelin
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage—plus 4 (1d8) Necrotic damage if the knight is Bloodied [XPHB].

info.text: Knights of the Emerald Claw command squads of Humanoid or Undead soldiers. As they draw nearer to death, the chill of the grave suff uses their weapon attacks.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 90

entries.name: Hustle
entries.description: The troubleshooter can move through the space of any creature that is of a larger size, but it can't stop there.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The troubleshooter makes two Poisoned Dagger attacks.

entries.name: Poisoned Dagger
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Piercing damage, and the target has the Poisoned [XPHB] condition until the start of the troubleshooter's next turn.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The troubleshooter casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save 13):

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

1/day each: Sleep [XPHB], Unseen Servant [XPHB]

entries.name: Nimble Escape
entries.description: The troubleshooter takes the Disengage [XPHB] or Hide [XPHB] action.

info.text: The inns of House Ghallanda are meant to be places of safe refuge and quiet rest, so the house employs troubleshooters (mostly halflings) to protect the safety and serenity of its guests.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 80

entries.name: Evasion
entries.description: If the homunculus is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, the homunculus instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the save and only half damage if it fails. It can't use this trait if it has the Incapacitated [XPHB] condition.

entries.name: Magic Bond
entries.description: Add the spell's level to any ability check or saving throw the homunculus makes.

entries.name: Force Strike
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: your spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. or range 30 ft. Hit: 1d6 + summonSpellLevel Force damage.

entries.name: Channel Magic
entries.description: Trigger: You cast a spell that has a range of touch while the homunculus is within 120 feet of you. Response: The homunculus delivers the spell through its touch.

info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 21

entries.name: Lucky
entries.description: When the medic rolls a 1 on the d20 of a D20 Test [XPHB], it can reroll the die, and it must use the new roll.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The medic makes two Radiant Burst attacks.

entries.name: Radiant Burst
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. or range 30 ft. Hit: 7 (2d6) Radiant damage, and the creature has the Blinded [XPHB] condition until the start of the medic's next turn.

entries.name: Mark of Healing (2/Day)
entries.description:
The medic casts Cure Wounds [XPHB] or Lesser Restoration [XPHB], using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability.

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

2/day: Cure Wounds [XPHB], Lesser Restoration [XPHB]

info.text: Dragonmarked heirs of House Jorasco served alongside every nation's armies in the Last War, providing medical care and magical healing to the injured. Though the warring nations treated Jorasco medics as sacrosanct, these medics also learned to channel their healing power into dazzling light to help them reach the wounded and escape from the thick of combat when necessary.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 81

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The warden has Advantage [XPHB] on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The warden makes two Arcane Whip attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Shackling Glyph if available.

entries.name: Arcane Whip
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) Force damage, and if the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Prone [XPHB] condition. If the target already has the Prone [XPHB] condition, the attack deals an extra 7 (2d6) Force damage.

entries.name: Shackling Glyph Recharge 6
entries.description: STR Saving Throw: 14, one creature the warden can see within 60 feet. Failure: The creature has the Grappled [XPHB] condition (escape 14). While Grappled [XPHB], the creature has the Restrained [XPHB] condition.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The warden casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 14):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: Alarm [XPHB], Arcane Lock [XPHB], Mage Armor [XPHB] (included in AC)

1/day: Dispel Magic [XPHB]

entries.name: Protective Magic (3/Day)
entries.description:
The warden casts Counterspell [XPHB] or Shield [XPHB] in response to the spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

Spellcasting ability: INT.

3/day: Counterspell [XPHB], Shield [XPHB]

info.text: Some dragonmarked heirs (mostly dwarves) of House Kundarak serve as personal guardians for the house's vaults and storehouses, and even its infamous prison, Dreadhold. Some also serve as agents of the mysterious Ghorad'din, a secretive group of assassins and spies little known beyond the members of the house. Kundarak wardens are adept at bypassing security measures as well as reinforcing them.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 81

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The scion makes two Thunderbolt attacks and uses Spellcasting.

entries.name: Thunderbolt
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. or range 30 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Lightning damage plus 9 (2d8) Thunder damage. Critical Hit: The creature also has the Deafened [XPHB] condition for 1 minute.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The scion casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save 14):

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

At will: Elementalism [XPHB], Gust of Wind [XPHB], Thunderwave [XPHB]

entries.name: Jump (2/Day)
entries.description:
The scion casts Jump [XPHB], requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

2/day: Jump [XPHB]

entries.name: Feather Fall (2/Day)
entries.description:
The scion casts Feather Fall [XPHB] in response to that spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

2/day: Feather Fall [XPHB]

info.text:
The Khoravar dragonmarked scions of House Lyrandar include swashbuckling sky captains, seafaring adventurers, and sinister cultists of the Hurricane Harvest. The power of their dragonmarks manifests as easy control of wind, thunder, and lightning, which they wield as readily in combat as in navigating the sea and sky.

Members of the Hurricane Harvest believe that the Mark of Storm is not a gift of the Sovereign Host, as others in their house teach, but the sign of the Devourer. They maintain that the greatest ancestors of their house live on as krakens in the deep and guide the cult through visions to use their power for destruction and domination. They sometimes partner with kuo-toa, sahuagin, and other monsters of the deep.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 82

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The inquisitive makes three Crooked Staff attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Inquisitive Eye.

entries.name: Crooked Staff
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Prone [XPHB] condition. If the target already has the Prone [XPHB] condition, the attack deals an extra 7 (2d6) Radiant damage.

entries.name: Inquisitive Eye
entries.description: WIS Saving Throw: 13, one creature the inquisitive can see within 60 feet. Failure: 10 (3d6) Psychic damage, and the target is marked. The inquisitive has Advantage [XPHB] on attack rolls against a target it has marked. While marked, the target can't become hidden from the inquisitive, and if it has the Invisible [XPHB] condition, it gains no benefit from that condition against the inquisitive. The mark disappears after 1 minute or when the inquisitive uses this action again. Success: Half damage only.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The inquisitive casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save 13):

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

At will: Guidance [XPHB]

1/day each: Detect Thoughts [XPHB], See Invisibility [XPHB]

entries.name: Spontaneous Barrier Recharge 4–6
entries.description: Trigger: The inquisitive or an ally it can see is hit with an attack roll. Response: The inquisitive adds 2 to its or the ally's AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

info.text: The most prized inquisitives of House Medani, a house of mostly Khoravar, employ their dragonmarks and their keen intellects to anticipate threats from any quarter. Some are part of a secretive order called the Basilisk's Gaze, dedicated to hunting down fugitive war criminals who committed atrocities during the Last War.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 82

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The enforcer makes three Dagger attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Lightning Cage if available.

entries.name: Dagger
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 9 (2d4 + 4) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage.

entries.name: Lightning Cage Recharge 5–6
entries.description: CON Saving Throw: 13, each creature in a 20-foot-radius Sphere [XPHB] centered on a point the enforcer can see within 60 feet. Failure: 13 (3d8) Lightning damage, and the creature can't take Reactions until the end of the enforcer's next turn. Success: Half damage only.

entries.name: Temporal Disruption (1/Day)
entries.description: Trigger: The enforcer takes damage from a melee attack. Response: The enforcer teleports up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. Each creature within 10 feet of the space the enforcer left must succeed on a 13 Constitution saving throw, or its Speed [XPHB] is halved until the start of the enforcer's next turn.

entries.name: Misty Step (2/Day)
entries.description:
The enforcer casts Misty Step [XPHB], using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability.

Spellcasting ability: INT.

2/day: Misty Step [XPHB]

info.text: Whether riding on an Orien cart, guarding the lightning rail on a cross-continental journey, or using OrienTeleportation Circlesto transport precious parcels in an instant, dragonmarked enforcers of House Orien (mostly humans) protect their house's interests and maintain its reputation for dependability.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 83

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The marshal makes three attacks, using Longsword or Pistol in any combination.

entries.name: Longsword
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Slashing damage, and the target has Disadvantage [XPHB] on the next attack roll it makes before the start of the marshal's next turn.

entries.name: Pistol
entries.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +7, range 30/90 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Shield (3/Day)
entries.description:
The marshal casts Shield [XPHB] in response to the spell's trigger, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability.

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

3/day: Shield [XPHB]

info.text:
The Sentinel Marshals of House Deneith, who are typically human, hold the honor of the house in their hands. The Treaty of Thronehold upheld their authority to pursue criminals across international borders, giving them the unique privilege and responsibility of upholding the law across Khorvaire.

Only the most trusted heirs of the house are honored with a position in the Sentinel Marshals, either after serving in the house's other guilds for several years (as bodyguards in the Defenders Guild and mercenary officers in the Blademarks Guild) or by special dispensation of House Deneith.

Sentinel Marshals are never authorized to break local or international laws, but neither are they accountable to the legal authorities of any nation. A rogue marshal can be punished only by the leadership of House Deneith, but some nations (such as Darguun and Droaam) ignore these conventions.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 83

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The agent makes two Shadow Knife attacks.

entries.name: Shadow Knife
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 10 (2d4 + 5) Piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) Necrotic damage, and the target's Speed [XPHB] is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The agent casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (14):

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

At will: Disguise Self [XPHB], Minor Illusion [XPHB]

1/day: Pass without Trace [XPHB]

entries.name: Shadow Cloak
entries.description: The agent has the Invisible [XPHB] condition until the start of its next turn. This invisibility ends early immediately after the agent makes an attack roll.

info.text:
Agents of House Phiarlan and House Thuranni, who are primarily elves, combine stealth and espionage with mastery of the performing arts—and dragonmarked heirs augment those skills with shadow magic. This stat block can serve for an agent of either house.

Even though House Phiarlan agents don't typically work as entertainers or artists in addition to their espionage activities, they receive extensive training in those arts alongside other members of their house. House Thuranni agents, in contrast, are always both artists and spies.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 84

entries.name: Words of Reason
entries.description: Allies in a 10-foot Emanation [XPHB] originating from the scribe have Advantage [XPHB] on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed [XPHB] or Frightened [XPHB] condition. This trait doesn't function if the scribe has the Incapacitated [XPHB] condition.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The scribe makes two Bursting Sigil attacks.

entries.name: Bursting Sigil
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) Radiant damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The scribe casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (13):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: Comprehend Languages [XPHB], Mage Armor [XPHB] (included in AC), Message [XPHB]

1/day each: Sending [XPHB]

entries.name: Word of Stasis Recharge 5–6
entries.description: CON Saving Throw: 13, each creature in a 20-foot-radius Sphere [XPHB] centered on a point the scribe can see within 60 feet. Failure: The target has the Incapacitated [XPHB] condition until the start of the scribe's next turn. While the target is Incapacitated [XPHB], its Speed [XPHB] is 0 and can't increase.

info.text: The dragonmarked heirs of House Sivis are typically accomplished gnome scholars of magic. In addition to the might that comes with their marks, they favor magical sigils and words of power.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 84

entries.name: Steel Bond
entries.description: Add your Proficiency Bonus [XPHB] to any ability check or saving throw the defender makes.

entries.name: Force-Empowered Rend
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: your spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1d8 + 2 plus your Intelligence modifier Force damage.

entries.name: Repair (3/Day)
entries.description: The defender, or one Construct or object it can see within 5 feet of itself, regains a number of Hit Points [XPHB] equal to 2d8 plus your Intelligence modifier.

entries.name: Deflect Attack
entries.description: Trigger: A creature the defender can see within 5 feet of itself makes an attack roll against a creature other than the defender. Response: The triggering creature makes the attack roll with Disadvantage [XPHB].

info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 19

entries.name: Evasion
entries.description: If the marauder is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, the marauder instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the save and only half as much damage if it fails. It can't use this trait if it has the Incapacitated [XPHB] condition.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The marauder makes three Aberrant Strike attacks.

entries.name: Aberrant Strike
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) Piercing damage, plus 21 (6d6) Force damage if the marauder had Advantage [XPHB] on the attack roll.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The marauder casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Constitution as the spellcasting ability (spell save 17):

Spellcasting ability: CON.

At will: Message [XPHB]

1/day: Disintegrate [XPHB]

entries.name: Tear Through Space
entries.description: The marauder teleports to a space it can see within 30 feet, appearing in a dazzling flash. CON Saving Throw: 17, each creature in a 5-foot Emanation [XPHB] originating from the marauder when it appears. Failure: The target has the Blinded [XPHB] condition until the end of the marauder's next turn.

info.text: This powerful assassin relies on teleportation to catch targets unaware and deal out rapid death.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 73

entries.name: Aberrant Surge
entries.description: When the ruffian casts Witch Bolt [XPHB], roll 1d8. On an even number, the ruffian gains a number of Temporary Hit Points [XPHB] equal to the number rolled. On an odd number, one creature of the ruffian's choice within 30 feet of it takes Force damage equal to the number rolled; if no other creatures are in range, it takes the damage.

entries.name: Spear
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The ruffian casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Constitution as the spellcasting ability (spell save 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks):

Spellcasting ability: CON.

At will: Thaumaturgy [XPHB]

1/day: Witch Bolt [XPHB]

info.text: This rank-and-file gang member, recruited off the streets of Sharn, uses sinister lightning powers to supplement ordinary weaponry.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 73

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The hunter makes three attacks, using Shortsword or Longbow in any combination.

entries.name: Shortsword
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Piercing damage, and the target has Disadvantage [XPHB] on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Longbow
entries.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +7, range 150/600 ft. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) Piercing damage, and the target's Speed [XPHB] is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Mark of Tharashk
entries.description: The hunter magically marks one creature it can see within 150 feet. The mark lasts for 1 hour, until the target dies, or until the hunter uses this Bonus Action [XPHB] again. While the target is marked in this way, the hunter has Advantage [XPHB] on attack rolls against the target, and the target gains no benefit from the Invisible [XPHB] condition against the hunter.

entries.name: Uncanny Dodge
entries.description: Trigger: The hunter is hit by an attack roll. Response: The hunter halves the damage (round down) it takes from that attack.

info.text:
House Tharashk's heirs include inquisitives, dragonshard prospectors, and bounty hunters. They are more at home in the trackless wilds than in crowded city streets, but they are quite capable of tracking and pursuing their prey in any environment.

Tharashk hunters, typically humans or orcs, often work alongside Druids of the Gatekeepers, and occasionally with Aberrant Cultists of the Dragon Below.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 85

entries.name: Fey Ancestry
entries.description: Magic can't put the shadow walker to sleep.

entries.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
entries.description: While in sunlight, the shadow walker has Disadvantage [XPHB] on ability checks and attack rolls.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The shadow walker makes three Gloom Burst attacks and uses Shadow Cowl.

entries.name: Gloom Burst
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Psychic damage.

entries.name: Shadow Cowl
entries.description: WIS Saving Throw: 17, one creature the shadow walker can see within 120 feet. Failure: 14 (4d6) Necrotic damage, and the target has the Blinded [XPHB] condition until the start of the shadow walker's next turn.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The shadow walker casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save 17):

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

At will: Dancing Lights [XPHB], Darkness [XPHB], Minor Illusion [XPHB]

info.text: Umbragen drow are the descendants of drow who fled the giants and found refuge underground. For countless generations, they have lived in the lightless caverns of Khyber. There, they tapped into a mysterious magical shadow they called the Umbra. Though some have emerged to haunt the surface in the wake of the giant empire's fall, they retain a spiritual and physical connection to the darkness below. Umbragen shadow walkers weave shadow magic to confound foes.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 99

entries.name: Pack Tactics
entries.description: The heir has Advantage [XPHB] on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the heir's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated [XPHB] condition.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The heir makes four attacks, using Scimitar or Lunar Wisp in any combination.

entries.name: Scimitar
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) Poison damage.

entries.name: Lunar Wisp
entries.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +5, range 60 ft. Hit: 9 (2d8) Radiant damage, and the target emits Dim Light [XPHB] in a 10-foot radius and can't benefit from the Invisible [XPHB] condition until the end of the heir's next turn.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The heir casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save 13):

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

At will: Druidcraft [XPHB], Light [XPHB], Speak with Animals [XPHB]

1/day: Ice Storm [XPHB]

3/day each: Animal Friendship [XPHB], Animal Messenger [XPHB]

entries.name: Spur Beast
entries.description: The heir targets a Beast it can see within 30 feet. The target can take a Reaction [XPHB] to move up to half its Speed [XPHB] and make one melee attack.

info.text: Combining druidic magic with skill at handling natural and monstrous animals, the dragonmarked heirs of House Vadalis, most of whom are human, are more fearsome than their innocuous-seeming house suggests—especially when accompanied by a Giant Boar, Polar Bear, or Rhinoceros.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 85

entries.name: Fey Ancestry
entries.description: Magic can't put the stingblade to sleep.

entries.name: Stingblade
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) Poison damage.

entries.name: Boomerang
entries.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, reach 30/120 ft. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) Bludgeoning damage.

info.text: Vulkoori drow warriors coat their weapons with the same deadly scorpion venom they use to tattoo their skin. Thanks to their extensive use of poison, they are resistant to the scorpion venom's full effects.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 98

entries.name: Fey Ancestry
entries.description: Magic can't put the priest to sleep.

entries.name: Venom Staff
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Poisoned [XPHB] condition until the end of the priest's next turn.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The priest casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks):

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

At will: Dancing Lights [XPHB], Ray of Sickness [XPHB], Thaumaturgy [XPHB]

1/day each: Cure Wounds [XPHB], Hold Person [XPHB], Protection from Poison [XPHB]

entries.name: Intensify Poison
entries.description: Each creature with the Poisoned [XPHB] condition within a 30-foot Emanation [XPHB] originating from the priest takes 3 (1d6) Poison damage.

info.text: Vulkoori venom priests delight in inflicting suffering through poison. Their weaponry and magic are carefully crafted to evoke the presence of the scorpion-god and strike terror into their enemies' hearts.
info.source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, page 98

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The absorber has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Pounce
entries.description: If the absorber moves at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and then hits its claws attack on the same turn, that target must succeed on a 17 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. If the target is prone, the absorber can make one bite attack against it as a bonus action.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The absorber makes three attacks: one with its bite or Mind Bolt and two with its claws.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 10 (1d10 + 5) piercing damage plus 5 (1d10) force damage.

entries.name: Claws
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d6 + 5) slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) force damage.

entries.name: Mind Bolt
entries.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +8 to hit, range 120 ft., one creature. Hit: 22 (4d10) psychic damage.

entries.name: Tail Ray
entries.description: When the absorber takes damage from a spell, the absorber takes only half the triggering damage. If the spellcaster is within 60 feet of the absorber, the absorber can force the caster to make a 16 Dexterity saving throw. Unless the save succeeds, the caster takes the other half of the damage.

info.text:
Resembling some sort of canine or feline quadruped at a distance, the absorber's monstrous nature becomes quickly apparent as it closes in. Named for its ability to draw magical energy into its body, the absorber can release that energy in devastating blasts through its tail, whose eye is constantly on the lookout for prey.

Brought to life by mages in the flying city of Aeor during the Age of Arcanum, Aeorian hunters were created to take on angels, demons, devils, fey, and the gods themselves. When Aeor crashed into Eiselcross, many of these magically mutated monstrosities survived, and they now stalk Aeor's ruins and the islands' icy wastes.

Created by Experimentation.

Aeorian hunters were created through arcane experimentation on beasts and humanoids—both captives and volunteers. These experiments resulted in monstrosities with brightly colored flesh and the power to resist and destroy Aeor's enemies. It is theorized that the mages of Aeor must have possessed some means of controlling their monstrous soldiers, but no such device has yet been found in the wastes of Eiselcross. Draconic was the language used by these mages to train and bind the Aeorian hunters, and the hunters retain an understanding of this language even though they can't speak it.

Madness through Immortality.

Aeorian hunters do not age. As such, the lust for violence their creators instilled in their minds has grown ravenous after centuries without war. Most immediately attack any creature they see.

Never Harm Another Hunter.

Though they crave violence, Aeorian hunters have never been seen attacking each other. Most scholars believe that Aeor's mages must have enchanted this behavior into them, given the cost in gold and magic required to create each hunter. Some adventurers in Eiselcross boast about sneaking past Aeorian hunters using disguises or illusions to mimic a hunter's form, but these are most likely tall tales.

Ageless Memories.

Each Aeorian hunter has perfect recall of every experience since the moment of its creation. Their limited intellects and desire for violence prevent them from effectively communicating, but each hunter holds a wealth of knowledge—often including the location of rare Aeorian relics—inside its mind.

Perfect Soldiers.

Aeorian hunters don't require food or drink.

entries.name: Horrid Gnashing
entries.description:
The nullifier's mouths gnash incoherently while it can see any enemies. Each creature that starts its turn within 20 feet of the nullifier and can hear it must make a 16 Wisdom saving throw. Unless the save succeeds, the creature rolls a d8 to determine what it does during the current turn:

• 1-4:.

The creature is stunned until the end of the turn.
• 5-6:.

The creature is frightened until the end of the turn and uses its movement to get as far as possible from the nullifier.
• 7-8:.

The creature doesn't move, and it uses its action to make one melee attack against a random creature (other than itself) if one is within reach. It otherwise does nothing

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The nullifier has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Innate Spellcasting
entries.description:
The nullifier's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save 16). It can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

At will: counterspell (see "Reactions" below), detect magic, dispel magic, see invisibility

1/day: antimagic field

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The nullifier makes three attacks: one with its bites and two with its claws.

entries.name: Bites
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 17 (2d12 + 4) piercing damage plus 11 (2d10) force damage.

entries.name: Claws
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage plus 11 (2d10) force damage, and the target is grappled (escape 16) if it's a creature. The nullifier has two claws, each of which can grapple one creature.

entries.name: Counterspell
entries.description: The nullifier attempts to interrupt a creature that it can see within 60 feet in the process of casting a spell. If the creature is casting a spell of 3rd level or lower, its spell fails and has no effect. If it is casting a spell of 4th level or higher, the nullifier makes a Charisma check with a DC equal to 10 + the spell's level. On a success, the creature's spell fails and has no effect.

info.text:
Nullifiers are the bane of all magic users, with their physical forms and innate powers shaped specifically to resist and cancel magical effects. Against other foes, a nullifier is no less fearsome for the grotesque mouths filled with razor-sharp teeth that cover its torso—and which set up a cacophony of gnashing that can drive other creatures mad.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The reverser has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The reverser makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, range 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 11 (1d12 + 5) piercing damage plus 6 (1d12) force damage.

entries.name: Claws
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d6 + 5) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) force damage.

entries.name: Reversal
entries.description: When a creature the reverser can see within 30 feet of it regains hit points, the reverser reduces the number of hit points regained to 0, and the reverser deals 13 (3d8) force damage to the creature.

info.text:
A reverser is a terrible foe in melee, laying into other creatures with teeth and claw. But the chaos it imposes is more fearful by far, as its enemies' healing magic are unraveled and turned against them.

entries.name: Fear of Fire
entries.description: If the yeti takes fire damage, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Keen Smell
entries.description: The yeti has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.

entries.name: Snow Camouflage
entries.description: The yeti has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in snowy terrain.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The yeti can use its Chilling Gaze and makes two claw attacks.

entries.name: Claw
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d6 + 7) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) cold damage.

entries.name: Chilling Gaze
entries.description: The yeti targets one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. If the target can see the yeti, the target must succeed on a 18 Constitution saving throw against this magic or take 21 (6d6) cold damage and then be paralyzed for 1 minute, unless it is immune to cold damage. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If the target's saving throw is successful, or if the effect ends on it, the target is immune to this yeti's gaze for 1 hour.

entries.name: Cold Breath Recharge 6
entries.description: The yeti exhales a 30-foot cone of frigid air. Each creature in that area must make a 18 Constitution saving throw, taking 45 (10d8) cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

info.text:
A yeti's windborne howl sounds out across remote mountains, striking fear into the hearts of the scattered miners and herders that dwell there. These hulking creatures stalk alpine peaks in a ceaseless hunt for food. Their snow-white fur lets them move like ghosts against the frozen landscape. A yeti's icy simian eyes can freeze its prey in place.

When Aeor fell into Foren, the impact threw a monolithic, purple crystal miles away from the crash site. The stone pierced the body of an abominable yeti named Allowak, but the crystal's magic preserved the yeti's corpse and absorbed Allowak's soul. When other yetis touched the crystal, their intellect increased and their innate desire to slaughter faded away. A society of the monstrosities living in huts and keeping mammoths for food sprung up around the crystal. These peaceful yetis abhor their more savage kin.

A Secret Place.

The yetis of Allowak's Sanctuary keep their home a secret, for they worry that outsiders might try to steal the crystal. Although the crystal's effects seem permanent, the yetis fear that if it were removed from Allowak's remains, they would lose their newfound intelligence. If outsiders get close to the village, the yetis patrolling the village's borders approach and act like the more common and savage members of their species. The yetis of Allowak's Sanctuary do not kill unless forced to, but they will cause injury to guard their secret.

In recent years, the yetis have acquired books and journals from explorers who died close to their camp. The tomes gave the yetis an understanding of the world beyond Eiselcross.

entries.name: Fear of Fire
entries.description: If the yeti takes fire damage, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Keen Smell
entries.description: The yeti has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.

entries.name: Snow Camouflage
entries.description: The yeti has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in snowy terrain.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The yeti can use its Chilling Gaze and makes two claw attacks.

entries.name: Claw
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) cold damage.

entries.name: Chilling Gaze
entries.description: The yeti targets one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. If the target can see the yeti, the target must succeed on a 13 Constitution saving throw against this magic or take 10 (3d6) cold damage and then be paralyzed for 1 minute, unless it is immune to cold damage. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If the target's saving throw is successful, or if the effect ends on it, the target is immune to the Chilling Gaze of all yetis (but not abominable yetis) for 1 hour.

entries.name: Antimagic Susceptibility
entries.description: The knife is incapacitated while in the area of an antimagic field. If targeted by dispel magic, the knife must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against the caster's spell save DC or fall unconscious for 1 minute.

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.description: While the knife remains motionless and isn't flying, it is indistinguishable from a normal knife.

entries.name: Dagger
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.description: While the tree remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal tree.

entries.name: Siege Monster
entries.description: The tree deals double damage to objects and structures.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The tree makes two slam attacks.

entries.name: Slam
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (3d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Rock
entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, range 60/180 ft., one target. Hit: 28 (4d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Animate Trees (1/Day)
entries.description: The tree magically animates one or two trees it can see within 60 feet of it. These trees have the same statistics as a treant, except they have Intelligence and Charisma scores of 1, they can't speak, and they have only the Slam action option. An animated tree acts as an ally of the tree. The tree remains animate for 1 day or until it dies; until the tree dies or is more than 120 feet from the tree; or until the tree takes a bonus action to turn it back into an inanimate tree. The tree then takes root if possible.

entries.name: Blood Curse of Binding (1/Day)
entries.description: As a bonus action, the blood hunter targets one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a 14 Strength saving throw or have its speed reduced to 0 and be unable to take reactions. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Blood Frenzy
entries.description: The blood hunter has advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all its hit points.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The blood hunter has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Innate Spellcasting (1/Day)
entries.description:
The blood hunter can innately cast hex. Its innate spellcasting ability is Intelligence.

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: hex

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The blood hunter attacks twice with a weapon.

entries.name: Greatsword
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) fire damage.

entries.name: Heavy Crossbow
entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d10 + 1) piercing damage.

info.text:
To mortals and monsters alike, the blood hunter is a legendary figure—a humanoid stalker said to embrace monstrous power. Long years ago, a group of mortals undertook dark rituals and alchemical experiments to gain the power of the deadliest monsters, allowing them to better hunt those monsters.

Blood hunters are steely on the surface, but roiling emotion lies beneath that impassive mask. Bestial fury and fathomless sorrow drive every stroke of a blood hunter's blade. Humanoids who draw the ire of a blood hunter are often in league with monsters—or the victims of a terrible misunderstanding. Such misunderstandings are tough to clear up, for blood hunters are the kind of folk to slay first and ask questions later.

entries.name: Dark One's Blessing
entries.description: When Bol'bara reduces a hostile creature to 0 hit points, she gains 6 temporary hit points.

entries.name: Nimble Escape
entries.description: Bol'bara can take the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action on each of her turns.

entries.name: Innate Spellcasting
entries.description:
Bol'bara's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks). She can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

At will: eldritch blast, false life, mage armor, mage hand

1/day each: charm person, hex, hold person, invisibility

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Bol'bara makes two melee attacks.

entries.name: Dagger
entries.description: Melee Weapon or Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.

entries.name: Eldritch Blast (Cantrip)
entries.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +4 to hit, range 120 ft., one creature. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) force damage.

sections.title: Legendary Actions
sections.description: Legendary actions: 2.

entries.name: Incorporeal Dash
entries.description: Bol'bara moves up to her speed. She can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. She takes 5 (1d10) force damage if she ends her turn inside an object.

entries.name: Zone of Calamity (Costs 2 Actions)
entries.description: A 15-foot-radius sphere of magical confusion extends from a point Bol'bara can see within 60 feet of her and spreads around corners. Each creature that starts its turn in that area is treated as if targeted by the confusion spell (save 12). The sphere lasts as long as Bol'bara maintains concentration, up to 1 minute (as if concentrating on a spell).

entries.name: Bladed Hide
entries.description: At the start of each of its turns, the moorbounder deals 5 (2d4) piercing damage to any creature grappling it.

entries.name: Standing Leap
entries.description: The moorbounder's long jump is up to 40 feet and its high jump is up to 20 feet, with or without a running start.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The moorbounder makes two attacks: one with its blades and one with its claws.

entries.name: Blades
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage.

entries.name: Claws
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (4d4 + 4) slashing damage.

info.text:
A weird and deadly offshoot of the moorbounder has rows of long, bladelike bristles covering its sleek body. The creature weaponizes these blades, using them to slash nearby creatures to ribbons. However, these blades make the bristled moorbounder less suitable as a mount.

One of the many predators to stalk the marshlands and muddy foothills of Xhorhas, moorbounders are known as dangerous killers to those who try to avoid them on their travels—and as prized mounts for those willing to capture and train them. Though the process of domesticating a moorbounder is fraught with peril, these creatures can become favored hunting companions and powerful war mounts.

Natural Hunters.

Moorbounders hunt with elongated tusks and retractable claws. With a vague resemblance to large hunting cats, their muscular bodies are built for combat, granting them incredible prowess at leaping and a running speed that makes them dominant carnivores.

entries.name: Pack Tactics
entries.description: The crawler has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the crawler's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The crawler makes four attacks: one with its bite, two with its claws, and one with its tail.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage and the target must succeed on a 11 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened until the start of the crawler's next turn.

entries.name: Claws
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) slashing damage.

entries.name: Tail
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

info.text:
The smallest and most numerous of the core spawn, these eyeless creatures scurry through the subterranean darkness with the help of their four irregular, gangly arms and hooked prehensile tails. Core spawn crawlers rarely travel alone, and a group of these agile predators is known as a vein of crawlers. Their clattering taloned limbs warn of their presence as they scuttle through the shadow-haunted depths of the earth.

The Elder Evils assault the multiverse in strange and calamitous ways. Sometimes they breach the Material Plane by exploiting the unfathomable energy and darkness found in the world's depths. These terrestrial manifestations of loathsome alien agendas are known as core spawn, and they are as varied in their physiology as they are horrific.

Their concentration in the desolate lands of Blightshore makes the core spawn a challenge to research, and many who have sought to observe or study these nightmarish entities rarely return. Those who do return are often shells of their former selves who speak of horrifying underground labyrinths of twisting caverns and malevolent nests where other denizens of the Miskath Strand are dragged below to some infernal purpose.

Offspring of Calamity.

The aberrant creatures known as core spawn are a subterranean breed of heralds, servants, foot soldiers, and lieutenants of the Elder Evils, awakened in the depths by the cataclysmic actions of the Betrayer Gods and their minions. They often appear on the surface world in the wake of seismic events, such as that which created the bottomless Miskath Pit of Eastern Wynandir. Warlocks and cultists sometimes gather together to hasten the arrival of core spawn to the Material Plane, focusing their arcane power on areas of natural seismic instability when the signs and stars are right.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The emissary has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The emissary makes three talons attacks.

entries.name: Talons
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 14 (2d10 + 3) slashing damage.

entries.name: Alluring Thrum Recharge 5–6
entries.description: The emissary emits a dreadful yet alluring hum. Each creature within 20 feet of the emissary that can hear it and that isn't an aberration must succeed on a 14 Constitution saving throw or be charmed for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Crystal Spores Recharge 6
entries.description: A 15-foot-radius cloud of toxic crystalline spores extends out from the emissary. The spores spread around corners. Each creature in the area must succeed on a 14 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned. While poisoned in this way, a creature takes 11 (2d10) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

info.text:
These airborne predators serve as assassins and sentinels for the core spawn. The terrible thrum of its insectoid wings and a chittering of mandibles announces an emissary's arrival.

The core spawn emissary can expel clouds of crystalline spores from tubes in its head. These spores act like a contact poison and can be deadly if inhaled.

entries.name: Earth Glide
entries.description: The seer can traverse through nonmagical, unworked earth and stone. While doing so, the seer doesn't disturb the material it moves through.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The seer has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The seer uses Fission Staff twice, Psychedelic Orb twice, or each one once.

entries.name: Fission Staff
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 9 (1d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) radiant damage, and the target is knocked prone.

entries.name: Psychedelic Orb
entries.description: The seer hurls a glimmering orb at one creature it can see within 120 of it. The target must succeed on a 19 Wisdom saving throw or take 27 (5d10) psychic damage and suffer a random condition until the start of the seer's next turn. Roll a d6 for the condition: (1-2) blinded, (3-4) frightened, or (5-6) stunned.

entries.name: Fuse Damage
entries.description: When the seer is hit by an attack, it takes only half of the triggering damage. The first time the seer hits with a melee attack on its next turn, the target takes an extra 1d6 radiant damage.

info.text:
Core spawn seers are humanoid arcanists corrupted by the eldritch power of the Elder Evils through blasphemous rites or accursed encounters. Ravaged by otherworldly radiation and disease, their bodies are covered in horrible protrusions of fluorescent crystals, which emit a psychedelic glow from beneath the tattered folds of their robes.

entries.name: Illumination
entries.description: The worm sheds dim light in a 20-foot radius.

entries.name: Radiant Mirror
entries.description: If the worm takes radiant damage, each creature within 20 feet of it takes that damage as well.

entries.name: Tunneler
entries.description: The worm can burrow through solid rock at half its burrowing speed and leaves a 10-foot-diameter tunnel in its wake.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The worm makes two attacks: one with its barbed tentacles and one with its bite.

entries.name: Barbed Tentacles
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. Hit: 25 (5d6 + 8) piercing damage, and the target is grappled (escape 18). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained. The tentacles can grapple only one creature at a time.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description:
Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 30 (5d8 + 8) piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it must succeed on a 18 Dexterity saving throw or be swallowed by the worm. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the worm, and takes 21 (6d6) fire damage at the start of each of the worm's turns.

If the worm takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the worm must succeed on a 21 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which fall prone in a space within 10 feet of the worm. If the worm dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse by using 20 feet of movement, exiting prone.

info.text:
This invertebrate horror has quivering, barbed tentacles set around its massive, toothy maw. The worm's cracked and stony hide pulses with a dull orange glow, as if it might be composed of primordial lava perpetually on the verge of hardening into solid rock.
