entries.description: Zilchyn magically summons a quasit, or attempts to summon a shadow demon with a 50% summoning chance chance of success. The summoned demon appears in an unoccupied space within 60 feet of its summoner, acts as an ally of its summoner, and can't summon other demons. It remains for 10 minutes, until it or its summoner dies, or until its summoner dismisses it as an action.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The behir makes two attacks: one with its bite and one to constrict.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage.

entries.name: Constrict
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one Large or smaller creature. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage plus 17 (2d10 + 6) slashing damage. The target is grappled (escape 16) if the behir isn't already constricting a creature, and the target is restrained until this grapple ends.

entries.name: Lightning Breath Recharge 5–6
entries.description: The behir exhales a line of lightning that is 20 feet long and 5 feet wide. Each creature in that line must make a 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking 66 (12d10) lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Swallow
entries.description:
The behir makes one bite attack against a Medium or smaller target it is grappling. If the attack hits, the target is also swallowed, and the grapple ends. While swallowed, the target is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the behir, and it takes 21 (6d6) acid damage at the start of each of the behir's turns. A behir can have only one creature swallowed at a time.

If the behir takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from the swallowed creature, the behir must succeed on a 14 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate the creature, which falls prone in a space within 10 feet of the behir. If the behir dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse by using 15 feet of movement, exiting prone.

info.source: The Orrery of the Wanderer, page 173

entries.name: Divine Eminence
entries.description: As a bonus action, Dagdra can expend a spell slot to cause its melee weapon attacks to magically deal an extra 10 (3d6) radiant damage to a target on a hit. This benefit lasts until the end of the turn. If Dagdra expends a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the extra damage increases by 1d6 for each level above 1st.

entries.name: Dwarven Resilience
entries.description: Dagdra has advantage on saving throws against poison, and has resistance against poison damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Dagdra is a 5th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). Dagdra has the following cleric spells prepared:

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

Cantrips (at will): light, sacred flame, thaumaturgy

Level 1 (4 slots): cure wounds, guiding bolt, sanctuary

Level 2 (3 slots): lesser restoration, spiritual weapon

Level 3 (2 slots): dispel magic, spirit guardians

entries.name: Mace
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Scroll Service (1/Day)
entries.description: As an action, Dagdra draws a spell scroll from her documancy satchel [AI]. The scroll contains a spell of up to 3rd level of Dagdra's choice. Only Dagdra can use the scroll, which vanishes after 1 minute.

info.text: Priests bring the teachings of their gods to the common folk. They are the spiritual leaders of temples and shrines and often hold positions of influence in their communities. Evil priests might work openly under a tyrant, or they might be the leaders of religious sects hidden in the shadows of good society, overseeing depraved rites. A priest typically has one or more acolytes to help with religious ceremonies and other sacred duties.
info.source: The Orrery of the Wanderer, page 145

entries.name: Club
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 2 (1d4) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Devil Dog is a 1st-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks). Devil Dog has the following cleric spells prepared:

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

Cantrips (at will): light, sacred flame, thaumaturgy

Level 1 (3 slots): bless, cure wounds, sanctuary

info.source: The Orrery of the Wanderer, page 85

entries.name: Reach
entries.description: The tentacle can reach anywhere in the room.

entries.name: Constrict
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 35 ft., one creature. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape 16). Until this grapple ends, the creature is restrained, and the tentacle can't constrict another target.

info.source: The Orrery of the Wanderer, page 94

entries.name: Relentless Endurance
entries.description: When reduced to 0 hit points, Gildha drops to 1 hit point instead (but can't do this again until they finish a long rest).

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Gildha is a 1st-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks). Gildha has the following cleric spells prepared:

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

Cantrips (at will): light, sacred flame, thaumaturgy

Level 1 (3 slots): bless, cure wounds, sanctuary

entries.name: Club
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 2 (1d4) bludgeoning damage.

info.source: The Orrery of the Wanderer, page 110

entries.name: Martial Advantage
entries.description: Once per turn, Grunka can deal an extra 7 (2d6) damage to a creature it hits with a weapon attack if that creature is within 5 feet of an ally of Grunka that isn't incapacitated.

entries.name: Longsword
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) slashing damage, or 6 (1d10 + 1) slashing damage if used with two hands.

entries.name: Longbow
entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.

entries.name: Acid Spray Gun Recharge 5–6
entries.description:
Grunka sprays acid in a 10-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a 10 Dexterity saving throw, taking 7 (2d6) acid damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

The spray gun has a tank that can be filled with ten standard vials of acid mixed with water, allowing it to be used five times.

info.source: The Orrery of the Wanderer, page 115

entries.name: Shortsword
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

entries.name: Shortbow
entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

info.source: The Orrery of the Wanderer, page 84

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The chimera makes three attacks: one with its bite, one with its horns, and one with its claws. When its fire breath is available, it can use the breath in place of its bite or horns.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage.

entries.name: Horns
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (1d12 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Claws
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage.

entries.name: Fire Breath Recharge 5–6
entries.description: The dragon head exhales fire in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 31 (7d8) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

info.source: The Orrery of the Wanderer, page 134

entries.name: Keen Smell
entries.description: The cat has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.

entries.name: Relative Size
entries.description: Any damage Onyx would take is reduced to 0. She has advantage on ability checks and saving throws.

entries.name: Dealing with Onyx
entries.description: Onyx cannot be overcome or killed by combat. Any weapon attack against her that hits AC 12 makes contact but deals no lasting damage. However, if the attack would deal 10 or more damage, Onyx has disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of her next turn. If Onyx would take 10 or more damage from spells or other effects, it yields the same result. Spells that impose conditions function normally against Onyx, but those conditions end automatically at the end of the cat's next turn.

entries.name: Claws
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d10) slashing damage.

info.text:
Onyx is a regular cat, with special traits, and a modified attack, that only apply when used in the Onyx Ascendant [OoW] encounter.

Further information can be found within that encounter on how to run it.

Without the special circumstances from that encounter, Onyx can be considered a standard cat
info.source: The Orrery of the Wanderer, page 186

entries.name: Axiomatic Mind
entries.description: The duodrone can't be compelled to act in a manner contrary to its nature or its instructions.

entries.name: Dismantlable
entries.description: If the replica duodrone dies, its body falls into a pile of parts (gears, plates, screws, and wires), leaving behind its weapons and anything else it was carrying.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The duodrone makes two fist attacks or two javelin attacks.

entries.name: Fist
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 2 (1d4) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Javelin
entries.description: Melee Weapon or Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage.

info.source: The Orrery of the Wanderer, page 132

entries.name: Axiomatic Mind
entries.description: The monodrone can't be compelled to act in a manner contrary to its nature or its instructions.

entries.name: Dismantlable

entries.name: Dagger
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.

entries.name: Javelin
entries.description: Melee Weapon or Ranged Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d6) piercing damage.

entries.description: The pentadrone can't be compelled to act in a manner contrary to its nature or its instructions.

entries.name: Dismantlable
entries.description: If the replica pentadrone dies, its body falls into a pile of parts (gears, plates, screws, and wires), leaving behind its weapons and anything else it was carrying.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The pentadrone makes five arm attacks.

entries.name: Arm
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Paralysis Gas Recharge 5–6
entries.description: The pentadrone exhales a 30-foot cone of gas. Each creature in that area must succeed on a 11 Constitution saving throw or be paralyzed for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

info.source: The Orrery of the Wanderer, page 132

entries.name: Dismantlable
entries.description: If the replica quadrone dies, its body falls into a pile of parts (gears, plates, screws, and wires), leaving behind its weapons and anything else it was carrying.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The quadrone makes two fist attacks or four shortbow attacks.

entries.name: Fist
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Shortbow
entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The tridrone makes three fist attacks or three javelin attacks.

entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Javelin
entries.description: Melee Weapon or Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage.

entries.name: Turn Immunity
entries.description: The foot is immune to effects that turn undead.

entries.name: Stomp
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) bludgeoning damage.

info.source: The Orrery of the Wanderer, page 92

entries.name: Cunning Action
entries.description: On each of its turns, Two Dry Cloaks can use a bonus action to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.

entries.name: Sneak Attack (1/Turn)
entries.description: Two Dry Cloaks deals an extra 7 (2d6) damage when it hits a target with a weapon attack and has advantage on the attack roll, or when the target is within 5 feet of an ally of Two Dry Cloaks that isn't incapacitated and Two Dry Cloaks doesn't have disadvantage on the attack roll.

entries.name: Feline Agility
entries.description: When Two Dry Cloaks moves on its turn in combat, they can double their speed until the end of the turn. Once they uses this ability, Two Dry Cloaks can't use it again until they moves 0 feet on one of their turns.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Two Dry Cloaks makes two melee attacks.

entries.name: Shortsword
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

entries.name: Hand Crossbow
entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

entries.name: Claws
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 2 (1d4) slashing damage.

info.text: Rulers, nobles, merchants, guildmasters, and other wealthy individuals use spies to gain the upper hand in a world of cutthroat politics. A spy is trained to secretly gather information. Loyal spies would rather die than divulge information that could compromise them or their employers.
info.source: The Orrery of the Wanderer, page 162

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a 11 Constitution saving throw against being magically petrified. On a failed save, the creature begins to turn to stone and is restrained. It must repeat the saving throw at the end of its next turn. On a success, the effect ends. On a failure, the creature is petrified for 24 hours.

info.source: The Orrery of the Wanderer, page 114

entries.name: Aberrant Form
entries.description: The zealot exudes the chaos of the Far Realm. Any non-Aberration creature that starts its turn within 5 feet of the zealot must succeed on a 15 Wisdom saving throw or take 7 (2d6) psychic damage.

entries.name: Weirdly Pliable
entries.description: The zealot, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, is unnaturally flexible. The zealot can move through any space as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The zealot makes one Psychic Rend attack and two Shortsword attacks.

entries.name: Psychic Rend
entries.description: Melee Spell or Ranged Spell Attack: +7 to hit, reach 15 ft. or range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) psychic damage, and the target must succeed on a 15 Wisdom saving throw or have the stunned condition until the start of the zealot's next turn.

entries.name: Shortsword
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting (Psionics)
entries.description:
The zealot casts one of the following spells, requiring no components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save 15):

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

At will: detect thoughts, minor illusion

1/day each: arcane gate, hunger of Hadar

entries.name: Void Warp Recharge 5–6
entries.description: The zealot teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, to an unoccupied space it can see within 120 feet of itself, leaving a churning void in the space it left. Immediately after it teleports, each creature within 30 feet of the void other than the zealot must make a 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 18 (4d8) force damage and is pulled to the unoccupied space closest to the void. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only. The void then disappears.

info.text: Aberrant zealots are cultists who have reached out to the powers of the Far Realm—only for something to reach back. Steeped in strange energy, aberrant zealots borrow their vicious might from the monstrous entities that inhabit that fell plane.
info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 203

entries.name: Undead Fortitude
entries.description: If damage reduces the zombie to 0 hit points, it must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit. On a success, the zombie drops to 1 hit point instead.

entries.name: Ash Cloud
entries.description: When the zombie dies, it leaves a cloud of ash that lasts for 5 minutes but does not obscure vision.

entries.name: Slam
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) bludgeoning damage.

info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 52

entries.name: Creature Sense
entries.description: The brain breaker is aware of creatures within 1 mile of itself that have an Intelligence score of 4 or higher. It knows the distance and direction to each creature, as well as each one's Intelligence score, but can't sense anything else about it. A creature protected by a mind blank spell, a nondetection spell, or similar magic can't be perceived in this manner.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The brain breaker has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Telepathic Hub
entries.description: The brain breaker can use its telepathy to initiate and maintain telepathic conversations with up to ten creatures at a time. The brain breaker can let those creatures telepathically hear each other while connected in this way.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The brain breaker makes two Tentacle attacks.

entries.name: Tentacle
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (3d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it has the grappled condition (escape 14) and takes 9 (1d8 + 5) psychic damage at the start of each of its turns until the grapple ends. The brain breaker can have up to four targets grappled at a time.

entries.name: Mind Blast Recharge 5–6
entries.description: Creatures of the brain breaker's choice within 60 feet of itself must succeed on a 17 Intelligence saving throw or take 32 (5d10 + 5) psychic damage and have the stunned condition for 1 minute. A stunned creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Spellcasting (Psionics)
entries.description:
The brain breaker casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 17):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: detect thoughts, levitate

entries.name: Psychic Link
entries.description: The brain breaker targets one creature with the incapacitated condition that the brain breaker senses with its Creature Sense trait and establishes a psychic link with the target. Until the link ends, the brain breaker can perceive everything the target senses. The target becomes aware that something is linked to its mind once it no longer has the incapacitated condition, and the brain breaker can terminate the link at any time (no action required). The target can use an action on its turn to attempt to break the link, doing so with a successful 17 Charisma check. If the target breaks the link this way, the target takes 10 (3d6) psychic damage. The link also ends if the target and the brain breaker are more than 1 mile apart. The brain breaker can form psychic links with up to ten creatures at a time.

info.text: Brain breakers look like giant brains with stout legs, and they wear steel armor made from interlocked links of Ilvaash's runes (knots of tentacles, brains, and jagged lines reminiscent of jaws).
info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 199

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries.description: If Chishinix fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: Chishinix has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Severed Head
entries.description: Chishinix is always accompanied by a severed head [PaBTSO].

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Chishinix makes two Tentacle attacks.

entries.name: Tentacle
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 21 (3d10 + 5) psychic damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, it has the grappled condition (escape 17) and must succeed on a 17 Intelligence saving throw or have the incapacitated condition until the grapple ends.

entries.name: Extract Brain
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one incapacitated Humanoid grappled by Chishinix. Hit: 55 (10d10) piercing damage. If this damage reduces the target to 0 hit points, Chishinix kills it by extracting and devouring its brain.

entries.name: Unleash Void Recharge 5–6
entries.description: Chishinix opens a rift into the Far Realm, centered on a point Chishinix can see within 60 feet of itself, and a tentacle lashes across creatures near the rift. Each creature other than mind flayers within 30 feet of the rift must make a 17 Intelligence saving throw, after which the tentacle disappears and the rift closes. On a failed save, a creature takes 18 (4d8) cold damage from the rift plus 18 (4d8) psychic damage from the tentacle and has the stunned condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only. A stunned creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Spellcasting (Psionics)
entries.description:
Chishinix casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 17):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: detect magic, detect thoughts, mage hand (the hand is invisible)

1/day: plane shift (self only)

3/day each: clairvoyance (as an action), dispel magic

entries.name: Warp Reality
entries.description: When hit by an attack roll, Chishinix gains a +4 bonus to its AC against that attack roll, potentially causing it to miss. Then Chishinix, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, magically teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.

info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 194

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The head has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Psychic Slam
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (3d10) psychic damage.

entries.name: Leech
entries.description: The head targets one creature within 5 feet of itself and forces the target to make a 14 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the head enters the target's space and attaches to the target. While the head is attached, the target takes 7 (3d4) piercing damage at the start of each of its turns, and the head can't use Leech again until it detaches. It can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement. As an action, the target or a creature within 5 feet of the target can detach the head by succeeding on a 15 Strength check.

info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 194

entries.name: Avoidance
entries.description: If the mutate is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.

entries.name: Light Sensitivity
entries.description: While in bright light, the mutate has disadvantage on attack rolls.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The mutate makes one Corpse Swipe attack and two Tail attacks, or it makes four Tail attacks.

entries.name: Corpse Swipe
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (3d10 + 4) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a 16 Constitution saving throw or have the poisoned condition for 1 minute. While poisoned in this way, a creature can't regain hit points.

entries.name: Tail
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage.

entries.name: Phantasmal Duplicates
entries.description: The mutate magically projects up to four illusory copies of itself. These duplicates make it difficult to ascertain the mutate's true location and last until the end of the mutate's next turn. While the copies exist, attack rolls against the mutate are made with disadvantage.

entries.name: Psychic Moan Recharge 6
entries.description: The mutate lets out a moan charged with psychic energy. Each creature within 60 feet of the mutate that isn't an Aberration must succeed on a 16 Wisdom saving throw or take 17 (5d6) psychic damage and have the frightened condition until the end of the mutate's next turn.

info.text:
The malign energy of the Far Realm causes a cloaker to merge with the rotted corpse of its last meal, resulting in a hideous puppeteering Aberration. The cloaker mutate shrouds its actions in a miasma of phantasmic duplicates. It uses the corpse melded to its underside to absorb damage and to strike at prey.

Mutates.

A creature exposed to the strange energy of the Far Realm risks developing mutations. Such a creature undergoes a metamorphosis as the powers of the Far Realm rewrite the fundamentals of the creature's existence.

Any creature can become a mutate and transform to exhibit physical characteristics associated with the Far Realm. Some creatures become mutates after prolonged exposure to Far Realm energy or magic drawn from that strange plane. Others deliberately change themselves, seeking to embrace the fell powers they worship. Creatures that become mutates often inexplicably change back to their previous forms once the Far Realm influence abates.

Forcing a transformation on creatures inexplicably fails, though evil forces—such as the mind flayer empire of old—have conducted much research on the topic. For centuries, mind flayers have tried to create armies of mutates to sweep through the Underdark. However, their efforts always proved fruitless, and eventually the mind flayers gave up their schemes.

Several common types of mutates exist. The individuals with stat blocks presented in this section are found in the preceding adventure, although other mutates exist. Some creatures are more prone to becoming Far Realm mutates, such as the cloaker and otyugh.

Mutates often gain psionic abilities, grow wings, become covered in otherworldly slime, or exhibit other unsettling traits. Specific mutated creatures are further described in appendix A.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries.description: If the cluster fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The cluster has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.description: The cluster bulges and spews 1d4 mature eggs. Each egg lands in an unoccupied space of the cluster's choice within 30 feet of itself and immediately transforms into an encephalon gemmule [PaBTSO]. The gemmules obey the cluster's commands and take their turns immediately after it.

entries.name: Aggressive Hunger
entries.description: Immediately after being hit by an attack, the cluster moves up to its speed toward the attacker. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks. If the cluster ends this movement within 5 feet of the attacker, it then makes one Slam attack against that attacker.

info.text:
An encephalon cluster pays no heed to an elder brain or its mind flayer progenitors. This grotesque creature shambles through dark and forgotten caverns, spewing warped progeny so it can multiply. As such, many mind flayers view encephalon clusters as insidious viruses. If left unchecked, a single encephalon cluster can quickly become a gorging menace that can overrun an entire mind flayer colony.

Encephalons.

When an illithid colony lays its eggs dangerously close to a Far Realm rift, an egg sac has a chance to mutate into what is known as an encephalon cluster—a ravenous, slimy, psionic, brain-shaped mass that spawns horrors called encephalon gemmules.
info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 205

entries.name: Encephalon Progeny
entries.description: The gemmule matures into an encephalon cluster if not killed within 30 (4d12 + 4) days of its creation.

entries.name: Magic Resistance

entries.name: Leech
entries.description: The gemmule targets one creature within 5 feet of itself and forces the target to make a 14 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the gemmule enters the target's space and attaches to the target. While the gemmule is attached, the target takes 7 (3d4) piercing damage at the start of each of its turns, and the gemmule can't use Leech again until it detaches. It can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement. As an action, the target or a creature within 5 feet of the target can detach the gemmule by succeeding on a 15 Strength check.

info.text:

When spawned, a gemmule appears as a misshapen, spindly legged, pyramid-shaped nugget of soft, fleshy matter. If left to its own devices, an encephalon gemmule grows into an encephalon cluster in a matter of days, at which point it begins producing its own gemmules.

The flesh meld targets one Large or smaller creature within 5 feet of itself that it's grappling. The target must succeed on a 15 Dexterity saving throw or be swallowed by the flesh meld. The flesh meld can have one creature swallowed at a time.

A swallowed creature no longer has the grappled condition. If this damage reduces a swallowed creature to 0 hit points, the creature dies, and the flesh meld consumes its body.

If the flesh meld takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from the swallowed creature, the flesh meld must succeed on a 15 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate the creature, which falls with the prone condition in a space within 5 feet of the flesh meld. If the flesh meld dies, the swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse by using 10 feet of movement, exiting with the prone condition.

Squelching and quivering with insatiable hunger, a flesh meld is a hulking amalgamation of teeth, blood, and body parts. Sinuous appendages of gore, each ending in a gnashing mouth, bite at prey before yanking the piteous creatures into the flesh meld's core. The stench of death surrounds a flesh meld.

When a creature is consumed by a flesh meld, the creature's mind is merged into the flesh meld's consciousness. More resilient minds may fight against this assimilation, but inevitably, the mind succumbs to the discordant chorus of thoughts to kill and consume.

Psionic Goblins.

The specifics of how a psionic goblin comes to exist vary. Some are born, changed by energy leaking from the Far Realm. Others transform themselves with their psionic power or enter into agreements with other Aberrations, which help them transform in return for their service as shock troops. Regardless, the result is the same: a goblin with unnatural and barely contained psychic power.

Psionic goblins often struggle to handle the turbulent psychic energy within their minds and bodies. Those psionic goblins who learn how to safely tap into this psychic power are formidable forces in combat. Psionic goblins often augment their martial skills with telekinesis, and stealthy squads of psionic goblin warriors can communicate via telepathy, making them excellent infiltrators and ambushers.

Awakened to the total breadth of their psionic abilities, goblin psi commanders wield blades of pure psychic energy. Whenever Grandlejaw takes 25 or more damage in a single turn, one of its heads dies. If all its heads die, Grandlejaw dies.

At the end of its turn, it grows two heads for each of its heads that died since its last turn, unless it has taken fire damage since its last turn. Grandlejaw regains 10 hit points for each head regrown in this way.

entries.name: Petrifying Gaze

When a creature that can see Honna's eyes starts its turn within 30 feet of Honna, Honna can force it to make a 14 Constitution saving throw if Honna isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the creature is instantly petrified. Otherwise, a creature that fails the save begins to turn to stone and is restrained. The restrained creature must repeat the saving throw at the end of its next turn, becoming petrified on a failure or ending the effect on a success. The petrification lasts until the creature is freed by the greater restoration spell or other magic.

Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see Honna until the start of its next turn, when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at Honna in the meantime, it must immediately make the save.

If Honna sees itself reflected on a polished surface within 30 feet of it and in an area of bright light, Honna is, due to its curse, affected by its own gaze.

When the influence of the Far Realm affects Humanoids, the resulting creature might be a thing of nightmares. Multitudinous webbed wings sprout haphazardly along this mutate's body. Its skin becomes clammy and as smooth as a salamander's.

Some intelligent Humanoid mutates retain their personalities from before they were exposed to the Far Realm. Some, driven by the allure of otherworldly powers, seek this transformation to become malevolent prophets and harbingers. Others find magical ways to return to their previous forms.

info.text:
A former member of the Lords' Alliance, Glasstaff seized an opportunity in Phandalin to line his own pockets. Originally tasked with setting up a constabulary, he instead assembled a group of outlaws and local ruffians to secure his own position in town.

Glasstaff puts on airs of gentility and courteous manners, addressing his bandits and ruffians as "my good fellows," and referring to sordid acts such as kidnapping or arson as "that unpleasant little business" or "those unfortunate events." He may refer to the characters as his "honored guests," and expresses regret that he cannot provide suitable entertainment for the occasion of their visit. Beneath his genteel demeanor, however, Glasstaff is just as violent and arrogant as any of the Redbrands.
info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 43

entries.name: Creature Sense
entries.description: The elder brain is aware of creatures within 1 mile of itself that have an Intelligence score of 4 or higher. It knows the distance and direction to each creature, as well as each one's Intelligence score, but can't sense anything else about it. A creature protected by a mind blank spell, a nondetection spell, or similar magic can't be perceived in this manner.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The elder brain has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Telepathic Hub
entries.description: The elder brain can use its telepathy to initiate and maintain telepathic conversations with up to ten creatures at a time. The elder brain can let those creatures telepathically hear each other while connected in this way.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The elder brain makes two Tentacle attacks.

entries.name: Tentacle
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (3d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it has the grappled condition (escape 14) and takes 9 (1d8 + 5) psychic damage at the start of each of its turns until the grapple ends. The elder brain can have up to four targets grappled at a time.

entries.name: Mind Blast Recharge 5–6
entries.description: Creatures of the elder brain's choice within 60 feet of itself must succeed on a 17 Intelligence saving throw or take 32 (5d10 + 5) psychic damage and have the stunned condition for 1 minute. A stunned creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Spellcasting (Psionics)
entries.description:
The elder brain casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 17):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: detect thoughts, levitate

entries.name: Psychic Link
entries.description: The elder brain targets one creature with the incapacitated condition that the elder brain senses with its Creature Sense trait and establishes a psychic link with the target. Until the link ends, the elder brain can perceive everything the target senses. The target becomes aware that something is linked to its mind once it no longer has the incapacitated condition, and the elder brain can terminate the link at any time (no action required). The target can use an action on its turn to attempt to break the link, doing so with a successful 17 Charisma check. If the target breaks the link this way, the target takes 10 (3d6) psychic damage. The link also ends if the target and the elder brain are more than 1 mile apart. The elder brain can form psychic links with up to ten creatures at a time.

info.text: The Far Realm has tainted the elder brain that fuels Illithinoch's mind flayers.
info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 159

entries.name: Reckless

entries.name: Psychic Slam
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) psychic damage.

info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 139

entries.name: Cacophony of Minds
entries.description: Any creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of the intellect snare must succeed on a 17 Wisdom saving throw or have the incapacitated condition for 1 minute. An incapacitated creature can repeat the saving throw at the start of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on the saving throw is immune to this intellect snare's Cacophony of Minds for 24 hours.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The intellect snare has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The intellect snare makes two Tentacle attacks.

entries.name: Tentacle
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (1d8 + 6) force damage, and if the target is a Medium or smaller creature, the target has the grappled condition (escape 17).

entries.name: Siphon Thoughts
entries.description: The intellect snare targets one creature it is grappling. The target must make a 17 Intelligence saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The intellect snare then regains a number of hit points equal to the amount of damage taken.

info.text:
When the strange horrors of the Far Realm rip at the minds of individuals, some of those wayward shreds of thought conglomerate to form an intellect snare. An intellect snare appears as a writhing ball of tentacles, echoing with the cacophonous sounds of every thought the snare has consumed.

Intellect snares are scavengers, often found scouring the aftermath of a mind flayer attack to feast on whatever hapless creatures are left behind. An intellect snare feeds by wrapping a creature in one of its tentacles and then siphoning shreds of thought, leaving a tattered mind in its wake.
info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 208

entries.name: Invisible in Water
entries.description: Kellikilli is invisible while fully immersed in water.

entries.name: Water Bound
entries.description: Kellikilli dies if it leaves the water to which it is bound or if that water is destroyed.

entries.name: Constrict
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. Hit: 13 (3d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, it is grappled (escape 13) and pulled 5 feet toward Kellikilli. Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, Kellikilli tries to drown it, and Kellikilli can't constrict another target.

info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 121

entries.name: Claw

On a failed save, a creature takes 36 (8d8) force damage, and its speed becomes 0 until the start of the dragon's next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

entries.name: Spellcasting (Psionics)

Lowarnizel casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 16):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

1/day each: dispel magic, haste, protection from evil and good, sending

entries.description: Lowarnizel magically transforms into any creature that is Medium or Small, while retaining his game statistics (other than his size). This transformation ends if the dragon is reduced to 0 hit points or uses a bonus action to end it.

info.text: Lowarnizel is a young amethyst dragon, and his companion is a lawful neutral human mage named Gossa. Both hate the Far Realm and anything tainted by it.
info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 181

Each creature other than mind flayers within 30 feet of the rift must make a 17 Intelligence saving throw, after which the tentacle disappears and the rift closes. info.text:
In pursuit of reconstructing their lost empire, a few mind flayers have turned to their home plane, the Far Realm, for answers. A mind flayer clairvoyant has peered into that realm's starless depths and been subsequently rewarded with extraordinary powers.

Instead of heeding an elder brain, a mind flayer clairvoyant listens to the whispers and whims of the voices of the Far Realm. In addition to feasting on brains, a mind flayer clairvoyant can summon tentacles that rip through the fabric of reality and distort the minds of enemies.

Mind Flayers.

Mind flayers, also known as illithids, feast on the brains of Humanoids across the multiverse. They are distinguished by their purple-toned skin and octopus-like heads, from which extend writhing tentacles.
info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 209

The target's spirit rises as a specter in the space of its corpse or in the nearest unoccupied space. The specter is under Mormesk's control. Many oculorbs are dreamed into existence by beholders. The Far Realm's strange power can pervade a beholder's dreams, resulting in the birth of an oculorb.

Oculorbs resemble a slimy conglomeration of eyes in many sizes and shapes. They are dreaded even by the beholders that birth them. An oculorb is a tangle of negative emotions—the fury, melancholy, and obsession of its creator, all given gruesome, corporeal form. Like a beholder, an oculorb can fire beams of energy from its eyes, but an oculorb's eyes lack the more sophisticated magical nature of a beholder's eyestalks. Instead, an oculorb unleashes powerful waves of energy charged with negative emotions, cowing its foes with despair and ire.

info.text:
Rising from piles of carrion and filth exposed to Far Realm energy, an otyugh mutate grows chitinous, jet-black plating over its limbs. The plates contrast sharply with the translucent, almost ghostly, appearance of its flesh, which provides a grotesque window into the virulent refuse the otyugh recently consumed.

Mutates.

A creature exposed to the strange energy of the Far Realm risks developing mutations. Such a creature undergoes a metamorphosis as the powers of the Far Realm rewrite the fundamentals of the creature's existence.

Any creature can become a mutate and transform to exhibit physical characteristics associated with the Far Realm. Some creatures become mutates after prolonged exposure to Far Realm energy or magic drawn from that strange plane. Others deliberately change themselves, seeking to embrace the fell powers they worship. Creatures that become mutates often inexplicably change back to their previous forms once the Far Realm influence abates.

Forcing a transformation on creatures inexplicably fails, though evil forces—such as the mind flayer empire of old—have conducted much research on the topic. For centuries, mind flayers have tried to create armies of mutates to sweep through the Underdark. However, their efforts always proved fruitless, and eventually the mind flayers gave up their schemes.

Several common types of mutates exist. The individuals with stat blocks presented in this section are found in the preceding adventure, although other mutates exist. Some creatures are more prone to becoming Far Realm mutates, such as the cloaker and otyugh.

Mutates often gain psionic abilities, grow wings, become covered in otherworldly slime, or exhibit other unsettling traits. Specific mutated creatures are further described in appendix A.
info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 213

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The ashenwight makes two Necrotic Shard attacks. It also uses Psionic Crown if available.

entries.name: Necrotic Shard
entries.description: Melee Weapon or Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, it has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Psionic Crown Recharge 5–6
entries.description: The ashenwight wreathes the head of a creature it can see within 60 feet of itself with a crown of jagged, spectral crystals. The target must succeed on a 14 Wisdom saving throw or have the charmed condition for 1 minute. While charmed in this way, the target's thoughts are sluggish; it can't take reactions, its speed is halved, and it takes 9 (2d8) psychic damage at the start of each of its turns. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Spellcasting (Psionics)
entries.description:
The ashenwight casts one of the following spells, requiring no spellcasting components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 14):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: mage hand (the hand is invisible)

1/day: calm emotions

info.text:
When an ashenwight arises near a crystal vein infused with aberrant power, or when one lingers in an area of fell magic, there is a chance for the ashenwight to develop psionic abilities. A psionic ashenwight is markedly more sapient than other ashenwights, though the resulting consciousness is a new creation separate from who the ashenwight was in life.

Some psionic ashenwights dedicate their existence to piecing together their previous life, while others strive to enlighten other ashenwights to this new psionic power.

Ashenwights.

When a Humanoid consumed by cruelty and rage dies in an area corrupted by the Far Realm, the creature sometimes rises as an ashenwight. The skin of these Undead horrors is desiccated, and their eyes often glow with otherworldly power.
info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 204

entries.name: Lightning Absorption
entries.description: Whenever the shambling mound is subjected to lightning damage, it takes no damage and regains a number of hit points equal to the lightning damage dealt.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The shambling mound makes two slam attacks. If both attacks hit a Medium or smaller target, the target is grappled (escape 14), and the shambling mound uses its Engulf on it.

entries.name: Slam
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Engulf
entries.description: The shambling mound engulfs a Medium or smaller creature grappled by it. The engulfed target is blinded, restrained, and unable to breathe, and it must succeed on a 14 Constitution saving throw at the start of each of the mound's turns or take 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. If the mound moves, the engulfed target moves with it. The mound can have only one creature engulfed at a time.

entries.name: Spellcasting (Psionics)
entries.description:
The shambling mound casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 8):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: minor illusion

1/day: charm person (already cast)

entries.name: Tentacle
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) psychic damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, it has the grappled condition (escape 16) and must succeed on a 16 Intelligence saving throw or have the stunned condition until the grapple ends.

entries.name: Eldritch Bolt
entries.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +8 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (3d10 + 4) force damage.

entries.name: Extract Brain

entries.name: Mind Blast Recharge 5–6
entries.description: Qunbraxel magically emits psychic energy in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in that area must succeed on a 16 Intelligence saving throw or take 26 (5d8 + 4) psychic damage and have the stunned condition for 1 minute. A stunned creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Spellcasting (Psionics)
entries.description:
Qunbraxel casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save 16):

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

At will: detect magic, detect thoughts, levitate, mage armor (self only), mage hand (the hand is invisible), prestidigitation

2/day each: confusion, sending, telekinesis

1/day each: dominate monster, plane shift (self only)

info.text:
Qunbraxel is an arrogant mind flayer warlock. Qunbraxel is always attended by four loyal grimlocks. They swap this duty with other grimlocks nearby, although Qunbraxel can hardly be bothered to tell one grimlock minion from another.

Cut off from any elder brain Qunbraxel considers worthy, the mind flayer hopes to join the Ilvaash fanatics and receive power and insight from the Far Realm.
info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 135

info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 216

entries.name: Creature Sense
entries.description: The refraction is aware of creatures within 100 miles of it that have an Intelligence score of 4 or higher. It knows the distance and direction to each creature, as well as each one's Intelligence score, but can't sense anything else about it. A creature protected by a mind blank spell, a nondetection spell, or similar magic can't be perceived in this manner.

entries.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries.description: The refraction can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (5/Day)
entries.description: If the refraction fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Magic Resistance

A stunned creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Teleport

Spellcasting ability: INT.

3/day each: dispel magic, modify memory

entries.name: Mindbreaker
entries.description: The refraction targets a creature within 120 feet of itself and disrupts its mental processes, causing the target to have disadvantage on all ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws until the end of the target's next turn.

entries.name: Projected Claw (Costs 2 Actions)
entries.description: The refraction makes one Dissonant Claw attack.

info.text:
Ilvaash was formed from the remains of the mind flayer god Ilsensine, the God-Brain. When Ilsensine left the Far Realm to establish a divine domain elsewhere, pieces of the God-Brain sloughed away and awoke to sentience. This is Ilvaash, the Dissonant Psyche.

The refraction of Ilvaash wields only a sliver of the godlet's power but is nevertheless a formidable foe.
info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 197

At will: nondetection (self only)

entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (2/Day)
entries.description: When Ruxithid fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

entries.description: Ruxithid has advantage on saving throws against the charmed and frightened conditions.

entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage.

entries.name: Brain Tendrils Recharge 5–6
entries.description: Ruxithid unleashes a flurry of crystalline psychic tendrils from his brain, targeting one creature that he can see within 30 feet of himself. The target must succeed on a 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 9 (2d8) psychic damage and have the stunned condition until the start of Ruxithid's next turn.

info.text:
Centuries ago, an abandoned duergar mining outpost called Zorzula's Rest was conquered by mind flayers, and the goblins there were exposed to the illithids' strange powers, leading a subset of the goblins to develop unusual psionic powers. The mind flayers eventually left, but the goblins remained, sequestered from the rest of the world until recently when the mind flayer fanatics called on them. Some of these goblins' descendants possess psionic powers, as evidenced by the goblin psi commanders and goblin psi brawlers (see appendix A for descriptions of both) that make up their ranks. Collectively, the goblins call themselves the Sawplees: a simplification of the word for "goblin" in the illithids' dialect of Deep Speech.

In recent weeks, the Sawplee goblins' leader found a mysterious gemstone. Unknown to Ruxithid the Chosen, a new group of mind flayer fanatics that draw power from the Far Realm planted it for him to find. The gemstone lets Ruxithid telepathically communicate with the mind flayers, who he believes are gods.
info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 99

entries.name: Aberrant Form
entries.description: Shalfi exudes the chaos of the Far Realm. Any non-Aberration creature that starts its turn within 5 feet of Shalfi must succeed on a 15 Wisdom saving throw or take 7 (2d6) psychic damage.

entries.name: Weirdly Pliable
entries.description: Shalfi, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, is unnaturally flexible. Shalfi can move through any space as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Shalfi makes one Psychic Rend attack and two Shortsword attacks.

entries.name: Psychic Rend
entries.description: Melee Spell or Ranged Spell Attack: +7 to hit, reach 15 ft. or range 120 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) psychic damage, and the target must succeed on a 15 Wisdom saving throw or have the stunned condition until the start of Shalfi's next turn.

entries.name: Shortsword
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) psychic damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting (Psionics)
entries.description:
Shalfi casts one of the following spells, requiring no components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save 15):

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

At will: detect thoughts, minor illusion

1/day each: arcane gate, hunger of Hadar

entries.name: Void Warp Recharge 5–6
entries.description: Shalfi teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, to an unoccupied space it can see within 120 feet of itself, leaving a churning void in the space it left. Immediately after it teleports, each creature within 30 feet of the void other than Shalfi must make a 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 18 (4d8) force damage and is pulled to the unoccupied space closest to the void. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only. The void then disappears.

info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 174

entries.name: Multiattack

entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) slashing damage, or 6 (1d10 + 1) slashing damage if used with two hands.

entries.name: Heavy Crossbow
entries.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d10) piercing damage.

entries.name: Parry
entries.description: When an attacker Sildar can see would hit him with a melee attack, he can roll a d6 and add the number rolled to his AC against the triggering attack, provided he's wielding a melee weapon.

info.text: Sildar is a kindhearted human man of nearly fifty years who holds a place of honor in the famous griffon cavalry of Waterdeep. He is an agent of the Lords' Alliance, a group of allied political powers along the Sword Coast concerned with mutual security and prosperity. The order ensures the safety of the cities and other settlements of Faerûn by proactively handling violent threats, and order members work to bring honor and glory to their leaders and their homeland.
info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 22

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Varakkta makes two silver greatsword attacks.

entries.name: Silver Greatsword
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) psychic damage. This is a magic weapon attack. On a critical hit against a target in an astral body (as with the astral projection spell), Varakkta can cut the silvery cord that tethers the target to its material body, instead of dealing damage.

entries.name: Innate Spellcasting (Psionics)
entries.description:
Varakkta's innate spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). It can innately cast the following spells, requiring no components:

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: mage hand (the hand is invisible)

3/day each: jump, misty step, nondetection (self only), tongues

1/day each: plane shift, telekinesis

info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 174

entries.description: If Voalsh fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: Voalsh has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.description: Voalsh opens a rift into the Far Realm, centered on a point Voalsh can see within 60 feet of itself, and a tentacle lashes across creatures near the rift. Each creature other than mind flayers within 30 feet of the rift must make a 17 Intelligence saving throw, after which the tentacle disappears and the rift closes. On a failed save, a creature takes 18 (4d8) cold damage from the rift plus 18 (4d8) psychic damage from the tentacle and has the stunned condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only. A stunned creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Spellcasting (Psionics)
entries.description:
Voalsh casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 17):

At will: detect magic, detect thoughts, mage hand (the hand is invisible)

1/day: plane shift (self only)

3/day each: clairvoyance (as an action), dispel magic

entries.name: Warp Reality
entries.description: When hit by an attack roll, Voalsh gains a +4 bonus to its AC against that attack roll, potentially causing it to miss. Then Voalsh, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, magically teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.

info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 194

entries.name: Shapechanger
entries.description: Zeond can use its action to polymorph into a beast form that resembles a bat (speed 10 ft. fly 40 ft.), a centipede (40 ft., climb 40 ft.), or a toad (40 ft., swim 40 ft.), or back into its true form. Its statistics are the same in each form, except for the speed changes noted. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

entries.name: Magic Resistance

entries.name: Claw (Bite in Beast Form)

The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Scare (1/Day)
entries.description: One creature of Zeond's choice within 20 feet of it must succeed on a 10 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, with disadvantage if Zeond is within line of sight, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Invisibility
entries.description: Zeond magically turns invisible until it attacks or uses Scare, or until its concentration ends (as if concentrating on a spell). Any equipment Zeond wears or carries is invisible with it.

info.source: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk, page 43

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries.description: If the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The dragon can use its Frightful Presence. It then makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (2d10 + 8) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.

entries.name: Claw
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d6 + 8) slashing damage.

entries.name: Tail
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d8 + 8) bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Frightful Presence
entries.description: Each creature of the dragon's choice that is within 120 feet of the dragon and aware of it must succeed on a 19 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the dragon's Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours.

entries.name: Fire Breath Recharge 5–6
entries.description: The dragon exhales fire in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a 21 Dexterity saving throw, taking 63 (18d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Detect
entries.description: The dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.

entries.name: Tail Attack
entries.description: The dragon makes a tail attack.

entries.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
entries.description: The dragon beats its wings. Each creature within 10 feet of the dragon must succeed on a 22 Dexterity saving throw or take 15 (2d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. The dragon can then fly up to half its flying speed.

info.text:
Dragons are fierce monsters with heavy reptilian bodies, crocodilian heads, and leathery wings, and are distinguished by their ability to breathe fire. Though Nicol Bolas is also a dragon, he feels no kinship for these savage, dim-witted beasts. They live mostly in the remote reaches of the desert, soaring in lazy circles through the sky as they search for prey. Sometimes they are captured and brought inside the Hekma, where they are put to use within the trials of the five gods—especially in the climactic battles of the final Trial of Zeal.

The dragons of Amonkhet are red dragons, though they lack the high Intelligence of the red dragons in the Monster Manual [PHB].

entries.name: Hold Breath
entries.description: The ammit can hold its breath for 30 minutes.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The ammit makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its tail.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 21 (3d10 + 5) piercing damage, and the target is grappled (escape 16). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the ammit can't bite another target.

entries.name: Tail
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target not grappled by the ammit. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a 16 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

info.text:
Demons.

Deep in the desert, far from the protection of the Hekma and the safety of Naktamun, lies a place called Ifnir, the Demons' Nest. The people of Amonkhet believe that the God-Pharaoh banished all the demons of this plane to the desolation of Ifnir as punishment when they rose up in rebellion against him. Some say that the angels carry the worst dissenters into the heart of Ifnir, which is a fate far worse than merely being abandoned amid the scouring sands.

The demons of Ifnir bear some resemblance to Bolas, with long limbs and tails, huge wings, and gaunt bodies adorned with horns and blades. Other demonic creatures have more bestial features, including ammits [PSA]—crocodilian demons sometimes used as challenges within the trials of the five gods—and the scorpion demons called soulstingers [PSA], whose venom causes excruciating pain in its victims.

Use the statistics of a nalfeshnee [MM] for a demon such as an Archfiend of Ifnir [PSA]. The statistics of a giant crocodile [MM] can model an ammit [PSA], and those of a bone devil [MM] work well for a soulstinger demon [PSA].

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) fire damage.

entries.name: Fire Breath Recharge 5–6
entries.description: The dragon exhales fire in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 24 (7d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Hold Breath
entries.description: The hydra can hold its breath for 1 hour.

entries.name: Multiple Heads
entries.description:
The hydra has five heads. While it has more than one head, the hydra has advantage on saving throws against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, and knocked unconscious.

Whenever the hydra takes 25 or more damage in a single turn, one of its heads dies. If all its heads die, the hydra dies.

At the end of its turn, it grows two heads for each of its heads that died since its last turn, unless it has taken fire damage since its last turn. The hydra regains 10 hit points for each head regrown in this way.

entries.name: Reactive Heads
entries.description: For each head the hydra has beyond one, it gets an extra reaction that can be used only for opportunity attacks.

entries.name: Wakeful
entries.description: While the hydra sleeps, at least one of its heads is awake.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The hydra makes as many bite attacks as it has heads.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d4 + 5) piercing damage, and the target must make on a 16 Constitution saving throw, taking 7 (2d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

info.text:
The hydras of Amonkhet have heads like those of a cobra. A successful bite attack from one of these heads deals 7 (1d4 + 5) piercing damage, and the target must make a 16 Constitution saving throw, taking 7 (2d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

The Desert Lands.

The desolate wilderness beyond the protection of the Hekma is largely uncharted. Immediately beyond the protective veil is a chaotic dune sea called Shefet, the Scouring Sands. The desert wears away at the edges of the fertile lands surrounding Naktamun, serving as a constant reminder that only the bounty and protection of the God-Pharaoh stand between the people of the city-state and a grisly death in the sands beyond. Beyond Shefet are parched, cracked expanses called Ramunap, the Broken Lands. The ruins of ancient civilizations are said to lie in the Broken Lands, though no one has ever explored such ruins and returned to Naktamun to tell of them.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The mummy can use its Dreadful Glare and makes one attack with its rotting fist.

entries.name: Rotting Fist
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a 12 Constitution saving throw or be cursed with mummy rot. The cursed target can't regain hit points, and its hit point maximum decreases by 10 (3d6) for every 24 hours that elapse. If the curse reduces the target's hit point maximum to 0, the target dies, and its body turns to dust. The curse lasts until removed by the remove curse spell or other magic.

entries.name: Dreadful Glare
entries.description: The mummy targets one creature it can see within 60 feet of it. If the target can see the mummy, it must succeed on a 11 Wisdom saving throw against this magic or become frightened until the end of the mummy's next turn. If the target fails the saving throw by 5 or more, it is also paralyzed for the same duration. A target that succeeds on the saving throw is immune to the Dreadful Glare of all mummies (but not mummy lords) for the next 24 hours.

info.text:
Not every citizen of Naktamun proves to be worthy of the afterlife. Acolytes sometimes die before the Ceremony of Measurement, perhaps in training accidents. Many initiates [PSA] perish in one of the first four trials, before earning their five cartouches. Viziers [PSA] sometimes die before they have truly earned a place in the afterlife serving their gods. Without having proven themselves worthy, these poor souls have no place as Eternals in the afterlife—but neither have they committed a grievous sin that would warrant abandoning them to the Curse of Wandering as marauding mummies [PSA].

Fortunately, the beneficence of the God-Pharaoh is great enough to provide a role for these people. Called the anointed, they are carefully embalmed, protected from the Curse of Wandering, and allowed to spend another lifetime in service to the worthy. The God-Pharaoh promises that those who faithfully serve as the anointed will earn a place as attendants in the afterlife as well, and even an eternity of service in the afterlife is preferable to an eternity subjected to the Curse of Wandering.

The bodies of the anointed are carefully wrapped in cloth and adorned with cartouches. In contrast to the cartouches of initiates [PSA] and viziers [PSA], these do not harbor the life essence of the deceased at their best. Instead, they coach the anointed for a particular form of service. With their cartouches in place, the anointed rise and join the ranks of serving mummies [PSA] who attend to the needs of daily life in Amonkhet.

The Curse of Wandering.

The Curse of Wandering is the greatest danger of the desert lands. A creature killed in the desert rises again as a zombie as soon as the moisture has dried from its flesh. As a result, the corpses of every kind of desert creature shamble across the dunes alongside the humanoid zombies of dissenters and would-be explorers. Most of these former humanoids are mindless marauders, though some tales speak of mummies [PSA] that have retained a sinister intelligence and even magical ability, becoming mummy lords [PSA].

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The mummy lord has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Rejuvenation
entries.description: A destroyed mummy lord gains a new body in 24 hours if its heart is intact, regaining all its hit points and becoming active again. The new body appears within 5 feet of the mummy lord's heart.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The mummy lord is a 10th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save 17, +9 to hit with spell attacks). The mummy lord has the following cleric spells prepared:

Spellcasting ability: WIS.

Cantrips (at will): sacred flame, thaumaturgy

Level 1 (4 slots): command, guiding bolt, shield of faith

Level 2 (3 slots): hold person, silence, spiritual weapon

Level 3 (3 slots): animate dead, dispel magic

Level 4 (3 slots): divination, guardian of faith

Level 5 (2 slots): contagion, insect plague

Level 6 (1 slots): harm

entries.description: The mummy can use its Dreadful Glare and makes one attack with its rotting fist.

entries.name: Rotting Fist
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 21 (6d6) necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a 16 Constitution saving throw or be cursed with mummy rot. The cursed target can't regain hit points, and its hit point maximum decreases by 10 (3d6) for every 24 hours that elapse. If the curse reduces the target's hit point maximum to 0, the target dies, and its body turns to dust. The curse lasts until removed by the remove curse spell or other magic.

If the target can see the mummy lord, it must succeed on a 16 Wisdom saving throw against this magic or become frightened until the end of the mummy's next turn. If the target fails the saving throw by 5 or more, it is also paralyzed for the same duration. entries.name: Attack
entries.description: The mummy lord makes one attack with its rotting fist or uses its Dreadful Glare.

entries.name: Blinding Dust
entries.description: Blinding dust and sand swirls magically around the mummy lord. Each creature within 5 feet of the mummy lord must succeed on a 16 Constitution saving throw or be blinded until the end of the creature's next turn.

entries.name: Blasphemous Word (Costs 2 Actions)
entries.description: The mummy lord utters a blasphemous word. Each non-undead creature within 10 feet of the mummy lord that can hear the magical utterance must succeed on a 16 Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of the mummy lord's next turn.

entries.name: Channel Negative Energy (Costs 2 Actions)
entries.description: The mummy lord magically unleashes negative energy. Creatures within 60 feet of the mummy lord, including ones behind barriers and around corners, can't regain hit points until the end of the mummy lord's next turn.

entries.name: Whirlwind of Sand (Costs 2 Actions)
entries.description: The mummy lord magically transforms into a whirlwind of sand, moves up to 60 feet, and reverts to its normal form. While in whirlwind form, the mummy lord is immune to all damage, and it can't be grappled, petrified, knocked prone, restrained, or stunned. Equipment worn or carried by the mummy lord remain in its possession.
