Spellcasting ability: CHA.

At will: greater restoration, pass without trace, water breathing, water walk

1/day each: commune, dispel evil and good, earthquake, fire storm, plane shift (self only)

entries.name: Maul
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 31 (6d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a 15 Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of Ulamog's next turn.

entries.name: Bolt
entries.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +15 to hit, range 600 ft., one target. Hit: 24 (7d6) damage of one of the following types (empyrean's choice): acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, radiant, or thunder.

entries.description: Ulamog makes one attack.

entries.name: Bolster
entries.description: Ulamog bolsters all nonhostile creatures within 120 feet of it until the end of its next turn. Bolstered creatures can't be charmed or frightened, and they gain advantage on ability checks and saving throws until the end of Ulamog's next turn.

entries.name: Trembling Strike (Costs 2 Actions)
entries.description: Ulamog strikes the ground with its maul, triggering an earth tremor. All other creatures on the ground within 60 feet of Ulamog must succeed on a 25 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

entries.name: Undead Fortitude
entries.description: If damage reduces the null to 0 hit points, it must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit. On a success, the null drops to 1 hit point instead.

entries.name: Slam
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) bludgeoning damage.

info.text: The various forms of undead ghosts are the incorporeal remnants of life and personality left after the death of a mortal body. But sometimes the reverse is true: a body retains its animation and hunger while losing any trace of its soul, becoming a zombie. When a vampire who is not a bloodchief drains the blood from a living humanoid, that creature undergoes a horrible transformation, becoming a stronger, faster version of a zombie called a null. Nulls' heads are featureless except for a gaping mouth filled with jagged teeth. Their bodies are shriveled and distorted, but preternaturally strong. They are mindlessly loyal servants to the vampire nobility, and the number of nulls under a vampire's control is a mark of status and power among the vampire houses of Guul Draz.

entries.name: Trampling Charge
entries.description: If the baloth moves at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and then hits it with a gore attack on the same turn, that target must succeed on a 13 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. If the target is prone, the baloth can make one stomp attack against it as a bonus action.

entries.name: Gore
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 24 (4d8 + 6) piercing damage.

entries.name: Stomp
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one prone creature. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

info.text: Baloths are perhaps the most distinctive of Zendikar's beasts. They are muscular, omnivorous hunters covered in horns, spines, and plates of various shapes. The woodcrasher baloths of the Turntimber forest are surprisingly agile, leaping from tree to tree by using their great claws to clutch each spiraling trunk. The leatherback baloths of Ora Ondar are heavier and keep to the ground, where their thick, plated hide protects them from danger. Baloth herds occasionally stampede across the Onduan plains—and do so more frequently since the rise of the Eldrazi, as if sharing in Zendikar's anger. Use the triceratops statistics for baloths, but woodcrasher baloths have a climbing speed of 30 feet in addition to their normal walking speed.

entries.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries.description: The wraith can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

entries.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
entries.description: While in sunlight, the wraith has disadvantage on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

entries.name: Life Drain
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 21 (4d8 + 3) necrotic damage. The target must succeed on a 14 Constitution saving throw or its hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0.

entries.name: Create Specter
entries.description: The wraith targets a humanoid within 10 feet of it that has been dead for no longer than 1 minute and died violently. The target's spirit rises as a specter in the space of its corpse or in the nearest unoccupied space. The specter is under the wraith's control. The wraith can have no more than seven specters under its control at one time.

info.text:
Magic fueled by black mana can alter the natural cycle of life and death. Whether wielded by mortal wizards or demons, or simply an environmental manifestation of black mana's flow through the land, such magic can trap spirits between the realm of the living and the mysterious fate of the dead. These ghostly undead are as destructive and hateful as the magic that calls them into being. Zendikar's shades and wraiths can be represented by the shadows and wraiths in the Monster Manual.

Not all spirits are created with black mana, however, and not all are malevolent. The spirits of the dead sometimes linger in the world to protect their kin or communities, or to stand guard over sacred or important sites. These spirits can be dangerous, but they are not usually malicious. Both the kor and the Mul Daya elves remain in communion with the spirits of their dead kindred, entreating them for wisdom and protection. Such spirits are best described as the ghosts in the Monster Manual.

entries.name: Tunneler
entries.description: The wurm can burrow through solid rock at half its burrow speed and leaves a 10-foot-diameter tunnel in its wake.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The wurm makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its stinger.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description:
Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (3d8 + 9) piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it must succeed on a 19 Dexterity saving throw or be swallowed by the wurm. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the wurm, and it takes 21 (6d6) acid damage at the start of each of the wurm's turns.

If the wurm takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the wurm must succeed on a 21 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which fall prone in a space within 10 feet of the wurm. If the wurm dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse by using 20 feet of movement, exiting prone.

entries.name: Tail Stinger
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. Hit: 19 (3d6 + 9) piercing damage, and the target must make a 19 Constitution saving throw, taking 42 (12d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

info.text:
The wurms of Zendikar are gigantic creatures with features akin to both snakes and insects. A wurm's serpentine body is covered in heavy bands of scales, giving it a segmented appearance. Its misshapen head is crowned with at least eight eyes, and is dominated by a ring of four or five enormous, hook-like fangs surrounding the mouth. The creature's jaws extend like a tube out from its mouth when it is ready to feed, accompanied by a horrendous carrion stench and a nauseating squelching sound.

The purple worm in the Monster Manual is a fine representation of Zendikar's wurms.

entries.name: Multiattack

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) fire damage.

entries.name: Claw

entries.name: Fire Breath Recharge 5–6
entries.description: The dragon exhales fire in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a 17 Dexterity saving throw, taking 56 (16d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

info.text:
Dragons are the ultimate representation of the chaos, ferocity, and reckless independence of red mana. They are found across Zendikar in mountainous regions where red mana is plentiful, particularly in Akoum, though never in great numbers.

A dragon is an enormous reptilian monster with thick, tough scales and leathery wings. Sharp spines or thick plates run down its back, and most dragons have large horns. A dragon's body has a vaguely feline shape, with a long neck supporting a large head, and a long, thick tail lashing behind it. Its four legs end in sharp claws that are deadly weapons, and its mouth is full of sharp teeth. Even a young dragon is larger than a powerful warhorse, and the largest are on par with some of the larger Eldrazi (though not as mighty as the towering Eldrazi titans).

The dragons of Zendikar are not particularly intelligent, especially in comparison to the genius dragon Planeswalker Nicol Bolas. They are more aware than the average beast and perhaps slightly smarter than an ogre, but dragons are still driven primarily by their instincts—to hunt for prey and to guard their territories against any intruders. They are hot-tempered and ferocious, typically rending or incinerating anything they perceive as an enemy before even thinking to ask questions.

A dragon's most fearsome aspect is its ability to exhale a blast of fire from its mouth. As it draws breath, a red glow like that of molten metal forms around its mouth, and is sometimes visible in its neck and chest as well. The fire then erupts in a long stream or a broad cone, shaped by the dragon as it chooses. A dragon might strafe the ground with fire as it flies overhead, covering as much ground—and incinerating as many foes—as possible. A grounded dragon turns its head back and forth as it breathes, blanketing its foes in flame or creating a barrier of burning earth to cover its retreat.

The young red dragon in the Monster Manual can represent the dragons of Zendikar, but its Intelligence score is only 8 (−1). This change has no effect on its other statistics.

On a failed save, a target can't use reactions, its speed is halved, and it can't make more than one attack on its turn. In addition, the target can take either an action or a bonus action on its turn, not both. These effects last for 1 minute. A target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

info.text:
With the power of magic at their disposal, mages of the ancient past and of Zendikar's present have been able to create objects bearing the semblance of life, capable of carrying out orders and even acting independently.

In a number of ancient sites associated with the Eldrazi, stone creatures have been found standing eternal guard. Created from fragments of hedrons or carved to resemble them, these constructs were intended to help the people of Zendikar eliminate the brood lineages after the titans were imprisoned, and were implanted with a fragment of the power that bound and imprisoned the Eldrazi. They have served as useful allies in battling the Eldrazi broods, and some mages have had limited success in prying the secrets of their magic from their artificial minds. Other hedron constructs are of more recent make, fashioned in imitation of the originals. These have no power over the Eldrazi beyond what their physical strength gives them, and their creators used them for menial tasks. They are most often found in the ancient ruins of the kor or in merfolk cities. The various modrons can be used to represent these dedicated constructs.

The golems of Zendikar are effectively artificial elementals, and can be represented by stone golems [MM]. Mages fashion bodies from special stone and infuse them with the power of movement and limited understanding. Golems are rare and powerful, especially when shaped from stone that already possesses magical power.

entries.name: Animated
entries.description:
If the object lacks legs or other appendages it can use for locomotion, it instead has a flying speed of 30 feet and can hover. If the object is securely attached to a surface or larger object, such as a chain bolted to a wall, its speed is 0.

When the animated object drops to 0 hit points, it reverts to its original object form, and any remaining damage carries over to its original object form.

The DM might rule that a specific objects slam attack inflicts slashing or piercing damage based on its form.

entries.name: Bloodied Fury
entries.description: While Bloodied [XPHB], Adam has Advantage [XPHB] on attack rolls.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: Adam has Advantage [XPHB] on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Adam makes two Slam attacks and uses Crush or Throw.

entries.name: Slam
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Lightning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled [XPHB] condition (escape 18) from one of two hands.

entries.name: Crush
entries.description: STR Saving Throw: 18, one creature Grappled [XPHB] by Adam. Failure: 13 (2d6 + 6) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Lightning damage, and the target has the Restrained [XPHB] condition. While Restrained [XPHB], the target is suffocating.

entries.name: Throw
entries.description: Adam throws a creature Grappled [XPHB] by him to a space he can see within 30 feet of himself that isn't in the air. DEX Saving Throw: 18, the creature thrown and each creature in the destination space. Failure: 13 (2d6 + 6) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Prone [XPHB] condition. Success: Half damage only.

entries.name: Violent Leap
entries.description: Adam spends 10 feet of movement to jump to a space within 40 feet that contains one or more Medium or smaller creatures. DEX Saving Throw: 18, each creature in Adam's destination space. Failure: 14 (4d6) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Prone [XPHB] condition. Success or Failure: The target moves to the nearest unoccupied space.

info.text:
Dr. Viktra Mordenheim's greatest invention is also her worst mistake: Adam, an automaton imprinted with the neuroprint of Viktra's dead lover. Adam's hulking figure and disheveled appearance are a result of his final struggle with Viktra, which also resulted in Adam's memories being corrupted. He now haunts the halls of Mordenheim Kinetics, searching for clues that might explain his monstrous nature and why the doctor hunts him.

Adam is described in more detail in the "Personnel Directory [PL]" section.

entries.name: Bolster Inventions
entries.description: At the end of each of Viktra's turns, each of her Construct allies in a 5-foot Emanation [XPHB] originating from Viktra gains 5 Temporary Hit Points [XPHB]. This trait doesn't function if Viktra has the Incapacitated [XPHB] condition.

entries.name: Darklord Restoration
entries.description: If Viktra dies, she revives with all her Hit Points [XPHB] in 1d10 weeks somewhere in Mordenheim Kinetics.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Domain)
entries.description: If Viktra fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Viktra makes two Lightning Rod attacks. She can replace one attack with a use of Syringe.

entries.name: Lightning Rod
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. or range 90 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Lightning damage, and the target can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Syringe
entries.description:
CON Saving Throw: 16, one creature Viktra can see within 5 feet. Failure: The target has the Poisoned [XPHB] condition for 1 minute. While Poisoned [XPHB] in this way, the target suffers one of the following effects (Viktra's choice). The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. The target succeeds automatically after 1 minute:

• Corrosive Serum.

The target takes 10 (4d4) Acid damage at the start of each of its turns, and its Speed [XPHB] decreases by 10 feet.
• Deadly Serum.

The target takes 11 (2d10) Necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns, and it can't regain Hit Points [XPHB].
• Mind-Altering Serum.

The target takes 10 (3d6) Psychic damage at the start of each of its turns, and it has Disadvantage [XPHB] on saving throws to maintain Concentration [XPHB].

entries.name: Shocking Prod
entries.description: Viktra moves up to half her Speed [XPHB] and makes one Lightning Rod attack. Viktra can't take this action again until the start of her next turn.

entries.name: Static Explosion
entries.description: DEX Saving Throw: 16, each creature in a 10-foot-radius Sphere [XPHB] centered on a point Viktra can see within 90 feet. Failure: 5 (2d4) Lightning damage. Success: Half damage.

entries.name: Activate Constructs (1/Day)
entries.description:
Viktra casts Animate Objects [XPHB], using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability.

Spellcasting ability: INT.

1/day: Animate Objects [XPHB]

info.text:
The founder and president of Mordenheim Kinetics is an eccentric visionary, unparalleled technologist, and notorious recluse.

The stat block in this section is based on the Viktra Mordenheim stat block inRavenloft: The Horrors Within. You can use the additional details and rules in that book to further describe Viktra and emphasize her ability to control her domain.

Viktra is described in more detail in the "Personnel Directory [PL]" section.

entries.name: Berserk
entries.description:
Whenever the created starts its turn Bloodied [XPHB], roll 1d6. On a 6, the created goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the created attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the created attacks an object. Once the created goes berserk, it remains so until it is destroyed or it is no longer Bloodied [XPHB].

The created's creator, if within 60 feet of the berserk created, can try to calm it by taking an action to make a 15 Charisma (Persuasion [XPHB]) check; the created must be able to hear its creator. If this check succeeds, the created ceases being berserk until the start of its next turn, at which point it resumes rolling for the Berserk trait again if it is still Bloodied [XPHB].

entries.name: Immutable Form
entries.description: The created can't shape-shift.

entries.name: Lightning Absorption
entries.description: Whenever the created is subjected to Lightning damage, it regains a number of Hit Points [XPHB] equal to the Lightning damage dealt.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.description: The created has Advantage [XPHB] on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The created makes two Slam attacks.

entries.name: Slam
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 4 (1d8) Lightning damage.

entries.name: Malfunction Recharge 6
entries.description:
The created randomly creates one of the following effects (roll 1d4):

• 1: Insect Hive.

CON Saving Throw: 15, each creature within 10 feet. Failure: The creature takes 13 (3d8) Poison damage and has the Poisoned [XPHB] condition until the start of its next turn.
• 2: Melting Plastic.

DEX Saving Throw: 15, each creature in a 15-foot Cone [XPHB]. Failure: 13 (3d8) Fire damage. Until the end of the target's next turn, the target's Speed [XPHB] is halved; the target can't take Reactions; and the target can take either an action or Bonus Action [XPHB] on its turn, not both. Success: Half damage only
• 3: Electrical Discharge.

DEX Saving Throw: 15, each creature within 10 feet. Failure: 18 (4d8) Lightning damage. Success: Half damage
• 4: Haywire.

The created makes two Slam attacks and goes berserk. It rolls for the Berserk trait each round, whether or not it is Bloodied [XPHB], for 1 minute.

info.text:
The created are Chief Engineer Hendrik von Aubrecker's attempt to replicate and improve upon Dr. Mordenheim's incredible humanlike automaton, Adam.

At his project's outset, Hendrik crafted a custom neuroprint by combining his own neuroprint with neuroprints from each of his siblings. Hendrik injects all of his created with the same copy of this chimeric neuroprint, but no two created are the same. Each created manifests a unique combination of the three von Aubreckers' intellects, obsessions, and personality flaws. The only things the created have in common are their violent dispositions toward anyone but the von Aubreckers and their tendency to go haywire when physically damaged.

Though his ultimate goal is to perfectly replicate the human form, Hendrik is no artist, and he lacks access to realistic fabricated flesh and textiles. He clumsily enrobes his creations with what materials he has on hand—contrivances that only emphasize the created's artificial nature. Roll on or choose a result from the Created Facade table to inspire the eerie appearance of a created.

1d6 | The Created Wears...
1 | Clothes patched together from discarded lab coats, protective goggles, and disposable gloves.
2 | Hair made from tangles of copper wiring and plastic tubing.
3 | Nonfunctional extra limbs stolen from other created.
4 | Digits and extremities cobbled together from ordinary office stationery.
5 | A mirror for a face.
6 | Jewelry made from microscope lenses, circuit wires, and electrical diodes.

info.text:
Once an empty echo is injected with a neuroprint, it becomes a fully functional echo. Beneath its sturdy mechanical frame, an echo has all the same memories and personality traits as its neuroprint donor, also called the echo's agent.

As an echo, an agent retains all of its learned skills and talents but none of its muscle memory. It can take months or even years before an agent is able to perform once-routine activities in its new echo body. Most echoes succumb to Spontaneous Echo Malfunction before regaining their full motoric functions.

entries.description: The echo can't shape-shift.

info.text:
An echo is "empty" until imprinted with its agent's neuroprint. While empty, an echo possesses just enough computing power to move around and perform basic tasks on its own, though it lacks the ability to reason, feel emotions, or form memories.

Unsupervised, empty echoes have the unsettling tendency to self-activate, leave their storage units, and wander the halls of Mordenheim Kinetics. Even more unsettlingly, an empty echo's only means of verbal communication is to emit an ear-piercing screech. Technicians are advised to wear hearing protection at all times when working on empty echoes.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Gerta makes three Cryogun attacks.

entries.name: Cryogun
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. Hit: 16 (3d8 + 3) Cold damage.

entries.name: Cryocannon Recharge 5–6
entries.description: CON Saving Throw: 14, each creature in a 60-foot Cone [XPHB]. Failure: 36 (8d8) Cold damage. Success: Half damage.

entries.name: Camouflage Generator
entries.description: While in Dim Light [XPHB] or Darkness [XPHB], Gerta takes the Hide action.

info.text: Towering, fierce Gerta may be the youngest von Aubrecker, but she looms over her brothers in both stature and force of personality. Gerta's custom plasteel skeleton and weatherproofed chassis protect her from the dangers of her work with dormant empty echoes in the Cryogenics department.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Hendrik makes two Slam attacks and uses Numbing Needle.

entries.name: Slam
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Numbing Needle
entries.description: CON Saving Throw: 14, one creature within 5 feet. Failure: 7 (2d6) Poison damage. Until the end of the target's next turn, the target's Speed [XPHB] is halved; the target can't take Reactions; and it can take either an action or a Bonus Action [XPHB] on its turn, not both. Success: Half damage only.

entries.name: Parry
entries.description: Trigger: Hendrik is hit by a melee attack roll. Response: Hendrik adds 2 to his AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

info.text: Hendrik has modified his body to truly monstrous effect. In place of bones and organs, Hendrik has a carbon fiber exoskeleton and a self-recharging engine in his rib cage. Hydraulic pistons give Hendrik incredible speed and enable him to deliver devastating blows. For particularly elusive enemies, Hendrik employs syringes full of potent sedatives from his third arm.

entries.name: Immutable Form
entries.description: The K-Nine can't shape-shift.

entries.name: Pack Tactics
entries.description: The K-Nine has Advantage [XPHB] on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the K-Nine's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated [XPHB] condition.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the Prone [XPHB] condition.

entries.name: X-Ray Scanning
entries.description: The K-Nine gains Blindsight to a range of 60 feet. This Blindsight ignores Total Cover [XPHB] created by up to 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, or 3 feet of wood or dirt. Thicker substances or thin sheets of lead block the Blindsight as usual. This benefit lasts for 1 minute or until the K-Nine has the Blinded [XPHB] condition.

info.text:
Shaped like a hunting dog and programmed to be five times as vicious, the Mordenheim Kinetics K-Nine unit is a combat machine designed for tactical warfare and conflict suppression.

When funding for Mordenheim Kinetics' primary ventures started to dwindle, Dr. Mordenheim turned to less scrupulous clients for capital. The K-Nine is one of the company's most successful creations developed for military defense contractors and private mercenary groups.

Before Mordenheim Kinetics' fall into ruin, K-Nine prototypes and deactivated units decorated the facility's lobbies. Now, packs of the mechanical hounds stalk the campus like feral wolves, hunting down and forcibly disabling escaped experiments and wayward visitors alike.

entries.name: Quarterstaff
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) Bludgeoning damage, or 5 (1d8 + 1) Bludgeoning damage if used with both hands.

entries.name: Feedback Loop
entries.description: CON Saving Throw: 11, one creature within 60 feet. Failure: 4 (1d8) Thunder damage, and the target has the Deafened [XPHB] condition until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The evangelist casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability:

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

At will: Guidance [XPHB]

2/day: Cure Wounds [XPHB]

entries.name: Dagger
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Disengage
entries.description: The infiltrator takes the Disengage [XPHB] action.

entries.name: Greatclub
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Pistol
entries.description: Ranged Attack Roll: +2, range 30/90 ft. Hit: 5 (1d10) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Static Arc
entries.description: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit: 5 (1d10) Lightning damage.

entries.description:
The technician casts one of the following spells, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 11):

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: Minor Illusion [XPHB]

2/day each: Burning Hands [XPHB], Grease [XPHB]

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: Rudolph makes one Taser attack and uses Spellcasting to cast Command [XPHB] or Mind Spike [XPHB].

entries.name: Taser
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (4d6) Lightning damage, and the target has the Paralyzed [XPHB] condition until the start of Rudolph's next turn.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Rudolph casts one of the following spells, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save 15):

At will: Detect Thoughts [XPHB], Mind Spike [XPHB]

1/day: Command [XPHB]

entries.description: Rudolph gains Blindsight to a range of 60 feet. This Blindsight ignores Total Cover [XPHB] created by up to 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, or 3 feet of wood or dirt. Thicker substances or thin sheets of lead block the Blindsight as usual. This benefit lasts for 1 minute or until Rudolph has the Blinded [XPHB] condition.

entries.name: Forcefield Generator
entries.description:
Rudolph casts Shield [XPHB] in response to the spell's trigger, requiring no spell components and using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

Spellcasting ability: INT.

At will: Shield [XPHB]

info.text: Despite his near-total transformation into a technological monster, Rudolph remains the most charming of the von Aubrecker siblings. All that remain of the elder brother's original form are his handsome face and formidable brain; the latter is augmented by cybernetic enhancements that amplify his mental powers to supernatural levels.

entries.name: Immutable Form
entries.description: The echo can't shape-shift.

entries.name: Mimicry
entries.description: The echo can mimic voices. A creature that hears the sound can tell it is an imitation only with a successful 10 Wisdom (Insight [XPHB]) check.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The echo makes two Slam attacks.

entries.name: Slam
entries.description: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Unearthly Scream Recharge 6
entries.description: CON Saving Throw: 13, each creature of the echo's choice within 30 feet. Failure: 9 (2d8) Thunder damage, and the creature has the Deafened [XPHB] condition until the start of the echo's next turn. While Deafened [XPHB], the creature also has the Frightened [XPHB] condition.

entries.name: Automated Self-Preservation
entries.description: The echo takes the Dash or Disengage action.

info.text:
A shattered echo is an echo that has undergone Spontaneous Echo Malfunction (SEM). Both empty echoes and neuroprint-injected echoes are susceptible to the phenomenon, which has no known cause. Signs of a shattered echo include unpredictable movements, murderous outbursts, and violent hallucinations. Once an echo has shattered, it's impossible to repair the echo's neuroprint or return the echo to working condition.

If a shattered echo had an agent before undergoing SEM, it often retains corrupted fragments of its agent's memories and personality. Such shattered echoes might attempt to reenact disjointed memories or chirp half-remembered bits of overheard dialogue. Though such behaviors may give the impression of a latent intellect, they're in fact nothing more than misfiring bits of computer code.

entries.name: Fey Ancestry
entries.description: Aerisi has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put her to sleep.

entries.name: Howling Defeat
entries.description: When Aerisi drops to 0 hit points, her body disappears in a howling whirlwind that disperses quickly and harmlessly. Anything she is wearing or carrying is left behind.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (2/Day)
entries.description: If Aerisi fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Aerisi is a 12th-level spellcaster. Her spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). Aerisi has the following wizard spells prepared:

Spellcasting ability: INT.

Cantrips (at will): gust [xge], mage hand, message, prestidigitation, ray of frost, shocking grasp

Level 1 (4 slots): charm person, feather fall, mage armor, thunderwave

Level 2 (3 slots): dust devil [xge], gust of wind, invisibility

Level 3 (3 slots): fly, gaseous form, lightning bolt

Level 4 (3 slots): ice storm, storm sphere [xge]

Level 5 (2 slots): cloudkill, seeming (cast each day)

Level 6 (1 slots): chain lightning

entries.name: Windvane
entries.description: Melee Weapon or Ranged Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d6 + 6) piercing damage, or 10 (1d8 + 6) piercing damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack, plus 3 (1d6) lightning damage.

sections.title: Lair Actions
sections.description:
If Aerisi is in the air node while Yan-C-Bin [PotA] isn't, Aerisi can take lair actions. On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), Aerisi uses a lair action to cast one of her spells, up to 3rd level, without using components or a spell slot. She can't cast the same spell two rounds in a row, although she can continue to concentrate on a spell she previously cast using a lair action. Aerisi can take no other lair actions while concentrating on a spell cast as a lair action.

If Aerisi casts invisibility using this lair action, she also draws the power of the air node into herself. By doing so, she regains 15 (3d8 + 2) hit points.

info.text:
Aerisi Kalinoth is the air prophet of the Elder Elemental Eye and leader of the Cult of the Howling Hatred. Tall and slender, with dark hair and (illusory) feathered wings that gently fan the air, Aerisi Kalinoth speaks to her people in a whisper that belies her violent temper, which reveals itself whenever she is denied.

Aerisi was a sheltered moon elf princess named Dara Algwynenn Kalinoth who grew up in a remote Faerie realm. Her parents had wished to protect her from the harsh realities of the world, but they only succeeded in spoiling her. When they tried to discipline their wilful daughter, she used the power of elemental air against them. Soon after, her dreams led her to the ancient dwarven ruins where the spear Windvane awaited her.

Dara changed her name to Aerisi and pretended to be an avariel (winged elf) princess like the ones from her storybooks. Then Aerisi used her talents for enchantment magic to sway mortals into joining her cult. She has convinced all her followers that she is in fact an avariel, and believes it herself even though she must cast seeming each day to "reveal" her wings.

Aerisi is prone to deluded flights of fancy and impulsive decadence. She sees herself as a beautiful, fierce, and just ruler who wields elemental power because she deserves it.

In the Air Node.

When danger threatens the Temple of Howling Hatred, Aerisi retreats to the Howling Caves, the air node. Within this node, Aerisi gains one additional use of her Legendary Resistance trait.

If Aerisi is in the air node while Yan-C-Bin [PotA] isn't, Aerisi can take lair actions. On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), Aerisi uses a lair action to cast one of her spells, up to 3rd level, without using components or a spell slot. She can't cast the same spell two rounds in a row, although she can continue to concentrate on a spell she previously cast using a lair action. Aerisi can take no other lair actions while concentrating on a spell cast as a lair action.

If Aerisi casts invisibility using this lair action, she also draws the power of the air node into herself. By doing so, she regains 15 (3d8 + 2) hit points.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) piercing damage.

entries.name: Claws
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) slashing damage. If the target is a creature other than an elf or undead, it must succeed on a 10 Constitution saving throw or be paralyzed for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Dagger
entries.description: Melee Weapon or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.

entries.name: Innate Spellcasting
entries.description:
Bastian's innate spellcasting ability is Constitution (spell save 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). He can innately cast the following spells:

Spellcasting ability: CON.

At will: produce flame

1/day: burning hands

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Bastian is a 9th-level spellcaster. His spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save 15, +7 to hit with spell attacks). Bastian knows the following sorcerer spells:

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

Cantrips (at will): fire bolt, mage hand, message, prestidigitation, shocking grasp

Level 1 (4 slots): mage armor, magic missile, shield

Level 2 (3 slots): misty step, scorching ray

Level 3 (3 slots): counterspell, fireball

Level 4 (3 slots): dimension door, wall of fire

Level 5 (1 slots): hold monster

info.text:
Like many in the fire cult, Bastian burns with an inner fire, but his fire is ambition, rather than a wish to see the world burn. Bastian is scheming to supplant Vanifer and claim Tinderstrike for himself.

As a practitioner of the arcane arts who learned much of his fire magic from Vanifer herself, Bastian relies on his spells in a fight, and he is a "quick-burning" sort who tries to deliver maximum impact early in the fight. If he knows a fight is coming but can't preemptively strike, Bastian becomes more cautious, casting wall of fire to protect himself before he hurls magic into the fray.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The guard makes two melee attacks.

entries.name: Morningstar
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage.

entries.name: Unyielding
entries.description: When the guard is subjected to an effect that would move it, knock it prone, or both, it can use its reaction to be neither moved nor knocked prone.

info.text:
Black Earth guards are the warriors of the earth cult. They are brutal, heavily armored thugs devoted to Ogrémoch. That devotion has granted them an uncanny ability to hold their ground against the buffeting assaults. It has also earned them the right to wear special plate armor of elemental stone, which breaks down when the guard is slain.

These guards are fanatically loyal to the Black Earth priests and the leaders of the cult. They fight to the death if commanded to do so by their superiors. Those with more potential become burrowsharks.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The priest makes two melee attacks.

entries.name: Glaive
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) slashing damage.

entries.name: Unyielding
entries.description: When the priest is subjected to an effect that would move it, knock it prone, or both, it can use its reaction to be neither moved nor knocked prone.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
The priest is a 5th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). It knows the following sorcerer spells:

Spellcasting ability: CHA.

Cantrips (at will): acid splash, blade ward, light, mending, mold earth [xge]

Level 1 (4 slots): earth tremor [xge], expeditious retreat, shield

Level 2 (3 slots): shatter, spider climb

Level 3 (2 slots): slow

info.text: The priests of the Black Earth are the drivers and organizers of Ogrémoch's cult. They are the true believers, seeing Ogrémoch as a divine force, and they have developed a twisted dogma to explain how the evil of elemental earth is destined to remake the world and rule over all. The Black Earth priests form a cabal of leaders whose fanaticism and magical power serve as the backbone of the cult. Individuals of unusual power hold higher rank in the cult, but the priests provide the cult leader with his or her authority over the rest of Ogrémoch's followers.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.description: The dragon turtle can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The dragon turtle makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws. It can make one tail attack in place of its two claw attacks.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 26 (3d12 + 7) piercing damage.

entries.name: Claw
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (2d8 + 7) slashing damage.

entries.name: Tail
entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 26 (3d12 + 7) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a 20 Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 10 feet away from the dragon turtle and knocked prone.

entries.name: Steam Breath Recharge 5–6
entries.description: The dragon turtle exhales scalding steam in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a 18 Constitution saving throw, taking 52 (15d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Being underwater doesn't grant resistance against this damage.

entries.name: Bond of the Black Earth
entries.description: The burrowshark is magically bound to a bulette trained to serve as its mount. While mounted on its bulette, the burrowshark shares the bulette's senses and can ride the bulette while it burrows. The bonded bulette obeys the burrowshark's commands. If its mount dies, the burrowshark can train a new bulette to serve as its bonded mount, a process requiring a month.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.description: The burrowshark makes three melee attacks.

entries.name: Spear
entries.description: Melee Weapon or Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack.

entries.name: Unyielding
entries.description: When the burrowshark is subjected to an effect that would move it, knock it prone, or both, it can use its reaction to be neither moved nor knocked prone.

info.text:
Elite warriors of the earth cult, burrowsharks are fierce champions who ride trained bulettes into battle. While their powerful mounts rend and tear foes to pieces, burrowsharks leap to the ground and cut down their foes without mercy.

Burrowsharks are much like Black Earth guards, since both have uncanny footing and special armor. For burrowsharks, an additional gift of Ogrémoch's might establishes a magical bond between the burrowshark and a bulette, allowing the rider to burrow with its mount and sense what its mount senses.

entries.name: Dagger
entries.description: Melee Weapon or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.description:
Cavil is a 9th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). Cavil has the following wizard spells prepared:

Spellcasting ability: INT.

Cantrips (at will): fire bolt, light, mage hand, prestidigitation

Level 1 (4 slots): detect magic, mage armor, magic missile, shield

Level 2 (3 slots): misty step, suggestion

Level 3 (3 slots): counterspell, fireball, fly

Level 4 (3 slots): greater invisibility, ice storm

Level 5 (1 slots): cone of cold

entries.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
